about: Odd days, dated for any year by odd_days.py. Names from NateDimick/funholidaysapi (MIT), dated as of 2021; each day's rule labelled by a model, checked against 2021, and the unsure ones settled by a web search (source, or sources by year for a day its organiser announces each year). Each day's about written by a model on 2026-11-25; the ones it wasn't sure of looked up on the web (about_source), none where nothing was found.

days.name: 45 Day
days.about: A day for the 7-inch, 45 RPM vinyl single. Record fans spend it pulling out their 45s to listen to them, collect them or share them.

days.name: 55 mph Speed Limit Day
days.about: Marks the 1974 law that set a national 55 mph speed limit in the US to save fuel during the oil crisis. People use it to talk about speed limits, fuel economy and road safety.

days.name: A Blue Christmas
days.about: A quieter church service or gathering around the longest night of the year, for people who are grieving or struggling during the holidays. It gives them space to acknowledge loss instead of putting on holiday cheer.

days.name: A Room Of One’s Own Day
days.about: Named after Virginia Woolf's book, it's a day to appreciate having a private space of your own. People spend time in their own room, reading, decorating, resting or just keeping to themselves without being disturbed.

days.name: Absinthe Day
days.about: A day for trying absinthe, the strong anise-flavored spirit tied to 19th-century Paris. People often serve it the traditional way, with water dripped over a sugar cube.

days.name: Absurdity Day
days.about: A day for embracing the ridiculous and doing something silly or nonsensical just for the fun of it.

days.name: Acadian Day
days.about: The national day of the Acadians, descendants of French settlers in Atlantic Canada. People fly the Acadian flag and hold a noisy street parade called the tintamarre.

days.name: Accounting Day
days.about: A day for recognizing accountants and bookkeepers. It's tied to the publication of Luca Pacioli's 1494 book describing double-entry bookkeeping.

days.name: Acorn Squash Day
days.about: A day for cooking and eating acorn squash, the small ribbed winter squash, usually roasted or stuffed.

days.name: Actors’ Day
days.about: A day to recognise acting and the people who do it. People go to a play or a film, read up on acting, or try some acting themselves.

days.name: Ada Lovelace Day
days.about: Named for the 19th-century mathematician often called the first computer programmer. It highlights women in science, technology, engineering and math through talks, events and online posts about their work.

days.name: Administrative Professionals Day
days.about: A workplace day for thanking secretaries, receptionists and office administrators. People usually do it with cards, flowers or a lunch out.

days.name: Adoption Day
days.about: Courts across the US open, often on a Saturday, to finalize adoptions of children from foster care. It's also meant to raise awareness of kids still waiting for families.

days.name: African Industrialization Day
days.about: A UN-recognized day for drawing attention to the need to build up manufacturing and industry across Africa. It's marked with conferences and policy discussions.

days.name: Aged Care Employee Day
days.about: An Australian day for thanking the people who work in nursing homes and aged care services. Facilities often hold small events or give gifts to staff.

days.name: Air Conditioning Appreciation Day
days.about: A summer day for being grateful for air conditioning and Willis Carrier, who invented the modern version. Mostly people just enjoy staying cool indoors.

days.name: Airborne Day
days.about: Honors US paratroopers and airborne forces, marking the Army's first official parachute test jump in 1940. Veterans and units hold ceremonies and remember those who served.

days.name: Alien Day
days.about: A fan day for the Alien film series, named after the planet LV-426 from the movies. Fans rewatch the films, and the studio often releases merchandise or screenings.

days.name: All or Nothing Day
days.about: A day for committing fully to something, taking the risk or chance you've been putting off instead of doing it halfway.

days.name: Almond Buttercrunch Day
days.about: A day for eating almond buttercrunch, a toffee candy coated in chocolate and chopped almonds.

days.name: Almond Day
days.about: A day for eating almonds and learning a bit about them as a healthy snack.

days.name: Alpaca Day
days.about: A day for learning about alpacas, the fluffy South American animals raised for their fiber. Farms sometimes open to visitors, and people shop for alpaca wool goods.

days.name: Amagwinya Day
days.about: A South African day for amagwinya, also called vetkoek, the fried dough 'fat cakes' eaten in communities all over the country. People make, buy and share them.

days.name: Amaretto Day
days.about: A day for drinking amaretto, the sweet almond-flavored Italian liqueur, on its own or in cocktails and desserts.

days.name: Amateur Radio Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the International Amateur Radio Union in 1925. Ham radio operators get on the air, make contacts and show the public what the hobby is about.

days.name: America Recycles Day
days.about: A US day, run by Keep America Beautiful, for encouraging people to recycle more. Communities hold collection drives and people take recycling pledges.

days.name: American Eagle Day
days.about: Marks the bald eagle being chosen as the US national emblem in 1782. People use it to learn about the eagle's recovery from near extinction and to support conservation.

days.name: American Red Cross Giving Day
days.about: A one-day fundraising push where people are asked to donate to the American Red Cross to support its disaster relief and other services.

days.name: American Touch Tag Day
days.about: A day for the classic playground game of tag, meant to get kids and adults outside running around. People play tag and its variations, like freeze tag, at parks, backyards and schools.

days.name: Amnesty International Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the human rights group Amnesty International in 1961. People write letters or sign petitions on behalf of prisoners of conscience.

days.name: Ancestor Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for researching your family tree and remembering the people you came from. People look through old records and photos or share family stories.

days.name: Animal Crackers Day
days.about: A day for eating animal crackers, the animal-shaped cookies that famously come in a circus-box package.

days.name: Animation Day
days.about: International Animation Day, started by the animation association ASIFA, marks Émile Reynaud's first public screening of animated pictures in 1892. Festivals and studios hold screenings and events.

days.name: Anime Day
days.about: A day for fans of Japanese animation to watch favorite shows and films and share their love of anime with others.

days.name: Anisette Day
days.about: A day for having anisette, a sweet licorice-flavored liqueur made from anise, often sipped after dinner or added to coffee.

days.name: Annoy Squidward Day
days.about: A fan holiday that comes from a joke in the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Employee of the Month." Fans mark it online by sharing Squidward memes and jokingly 'annoying' him the way SpongeBob does.

days.name: Another Look Unlimited Day
days.about: A day for taking another look around your home and finding things you don't need. Instead of throwing them out, people give them to charity or to friends, and it works as a fall clean-out.

days.name: Answer Your Cat’s Questions Day
days.about: A whimsical day from pet-holiday creators Thomas and Ruth Roy. You watch your cat, imagine what it's asking you, and try to answer.

days.name: Anzac Day
days.about: A national day of remembrance in Australia and New Zealand for those who served and died in war, starting with the Gallipoli landing in 1915. People attend dawn services, marches and memorials.

days.name: Apple Cider Day
days.about: A day for drinking apple cider, hot or cold, often spiced, in the autumn.

days.name: Apple Day
days.about: Started in the UK by the charity Common Ground to celebrate apples and local orchards. People hold fairs with apple tastings, juice pressing and displays of old varieties.

days.name: Apple Dumpling Day
days.about: A day for making and eating apple dumplings, whole apples wrapped in pastry and baked.

days.name: Apple Pie Day
days.about: A day for baking and eating apple pie, the classic American dessert.

days.name: Apple Strudel Day
days.about: A day for eating apple strudel, the Austrian pastry of thin layered dough rolled around spiced apples.

days.name: Apple Tree Day
days.about: It reportedly began as a tribute to an apple tree that was about two centuries old and grew into a day about apples and why they're good for you. People eat apples or plant an apple tree when the season allows.

days.name: Apple Turnover Day
days.about: A day for eating apple turnovers, the folded pastries filled with apple.

days.name: Applesauce Cake Day
days.about: A day for baking applesauce cake, a moist spiced cake made with applesauce.

days.name: Appreciate A Dragon Day
days.about: Started by fantasy author Donita K. Paul to encourage reading and literacy. People read or share dragon stories, draw dragons and talk about dragon lore.

days.name: Apricot Day
days.about: A day for eating apricots, fresh or dried, or in jams and baked goods.

days.name: Arabic Language Day
days.about: A UN day marking Arabic's adoption as an official UN language in 1973. Events highlight the language's history, poetry and calligraphy.

days.name: Arborist Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for recognizing arborists, the specialists who plant, care for and manage individual trees and woody plants. People thank them and learn more about the work they do.

days.name: Architecture Day
days.about: World Architecture Day, set up by the International Union of Architects, for thinking about how buildings and cities shape people's lives. Architects hold talks, tours and events.

days.name: Area Code Day
days.about: Marks the introduction of US telephone area codes in 1947. People share facts about their area code or show some pride in it.

days.name: Argyle Day
days.about: A day for wearing the diamond-patterned argyle print, usually socks or sweaters.

days.name: Armed Forces Day
days.about: A US day honoring everyone currently serving in the military branches, with parades, open bases and thank-yous to service members.

days.name: Army Day
days.about: A day honoring a country's army and its soldiers. In the US it is tied to the Army's history and is marked with ceremonies and recognition of soldiers.

days.name: As Young As You Feel Day
days.about: A reminder that age is partly a state of mind. People do something playful or active that makes them feel young.

days.name: Ask A Stupid Question Day
days.about: Started by teachers to get students to ask the questions they're afraid will sound dumb. The idea is that no question is too silly to ask.

days.name: ASL Day
days.about: Recognizes American Sign Language and Deaf culture, tied to the founding of the American School for the Deaf in 1817. People learn some signs or support Deaf communities.

days.name: ASMR Day
days.about: About the tingly, relaxing feeling some people get from soft sounds like whispering or tapping. Fans watch or share ASMR videos.

days.name: Asparagus Day
days.about: A food day for eating asparagus, whether grilled, roasted or in a favorite recipe.

days.name: Assistance Dog Day
days.about: Recognizes guide, hearing and service dogs and the people who train them. People learn how these dogs help and support organizations that provide them.

days.name: Asthma Day
days.about: World Asthma Day, organized by the Global Initiative for Asthma, to raise awareness of asthma and better care for it, with health campaigns and education events.

days.name: Atheist Day
days.about: Started by atheist groups as an atheist 'coming out' day, when atheists are encouraged to openly share their story. It's also meant to draw attention to the problems atheists face in different countries and to support freedom of belief.

days.name: Auctioneers Day
days.about: Promoted by the National Auctioneers Association to recognize auctioneers and their work. Auction houses sometimes hold special events.

days.name: Aunt and Uncle Day
days.about: A day for appreciating aunts and uncles by calling them, spending time together or sending a note.

days.name: Aura Awareness Day
days.about: A day for teaching people about the aura, the energy field some believe surrounds every person, and what it might mean for their physical and mental health. People go to talks on auras or get aura readings.

days.name: Australia Day
days.about: Australia's national day, marking the First Fleet's arrival in 1788, with citizenship ceremonies, barbecues and fireworks. Many Indigenous Australians mark it as Invasion Day, and it is increasingly a day of protest and debate.

days.name: Authors’ Day
days.about: Started in 1928 by Nellie McPherson to honor American authors. People read a book, thank a writer or support local authors.

days.name: Aviation Day
days.about: National Aviation Day, set on Orville Wright's birthday by Franklin Roosevelt, to mark the history of flight. People visit air museums or air shows.

days.name: Aviation Maintenance Technician Day
days.about: Honors the mechanics who keep aircraft safe. It falls on the birthday of Charles Taylor, the Wright brothers' mechanic.

days.name: Awkward Moments Day
days.about: A day for laughing off embarrassing moments and being kinder to yourself about them.

days.name: B Kinder Day
days.about: An Australian kindness day started in memory of 12-year-old Billie Kinder, who died in an accident. Schools, businesses and individuals write kind messages and share them with people who need them.

days.name: Baby Day
days.about: A day about babies and the care and attention they need, and a chance to support new parents. Families get together, take baby photos, give gifts to babies and their parents, and share stories about their kids.

days.name: Backward Day
days.about: A silly day for doing things in reverse: wearing clothes backwards, eating dessert first, walking backwards.

days.name: Bacon Day
days.about: A food day for eating bacon, on its own or worked into all kinds of dishes.

days.name: Bad Poetry Day
days.about: A day for writing deliberately terrible poems and sharing them for laughs.

days.name: Badger Day
days.about: A day that started in the UK to raise awareness of badgers, their role in the ecosystem and the dangers they face. People learn about badgers and support efforts to protect them.

days.name: Bagel Day
days.about: A food day for eating bagels with your favorite toppings.

days.name: Bake Cookies Day
days.about: A day for baking a batch of cookies, often to share during the holiday season.

days.name: Baked Alaska Day
days.about: A food day for the dessert of ice cream and cake covered in browned meringue. Its name is linked to the US purchase of Alaska.

days.name: Baked Scallops Day
days.about: A food day for cooking or ordering baked scallops.

days.name: Baklava Day
days.about: A food day for eating baklava, the layered pastry with nuts and honey syrup.

days.name: Ball Point Pen Day
days.about: Marks László Bíró's patent of the ballpoint pen. It's a nod to an everyday invention.

days.name: Ballet Day
days.about: World Ballet Day, when major ballet companies stream their classes and rehearsals online so people can see behind the scenes.

days.name: Balloon Ascension Day
days.about: Marks the Montgolfier brothers' first manned hot-air balloon flight in 1783. People learn about early flight or take balloon rides.

days.name: Balloons Around the World Day
days.about: Started by balloon artists and decorators to share the fun of balloons. People make balloon art or surprise someone with balloons.

days.name: Balloons to Heaven Day
days.about: A day for remembering loved ones who have died. Traditionally, people send up a balloon with a message to the person they lost.

days.name: Banana Bread Day
days.about: A food day for baking or eating banana bread.

days.name: Banana Cream Pie Day
days.about: A food day for making or eating banana cream pie.

days.name: Banana Day
days.about: A food day for eating bananas and appreciating the fruit.

days.name: Banana Lovers Day
days.about: Another day for banana fans to eat bananas in all their forms.

days.name: Banana Split Day
days.about: A food day for eating banana splits. The dessert is usually credited to a pharmacist in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, in 1904.

days.name: Bandana Day
days.about: An Australian fundraiser run by the charity Canteen to support young people aged 12 to 25 affected by cancer. People buy and wear Canteen bandannas, and some donate or cut or dye their hair to raise money.

days.name: Barbecue Day
days.about: A food day for firing up the grill or eating barbecue.

days.name: Barbershop Quartet Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the Barbershop Harmony Society in 1938. Fans sing or listen to four-part a cappella harmony.

days.name: Barbie Day
days.about: Marks the Barbie doll's debut in 1959. Collectors and fans share their dolls and memories.

days.name: Barista Day
days.about: A day for thanking the people who make your coffee, often with a kind word or a bigger tip.

days.name: Bartender Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for thanking bartenders with a good tip and some appreciation for their work.

days.name: Bat Appreciation Day
days.about: Raises awareness of bats and the good they do, like eating insects and pollinating plants. People learn about bats or support bat conservation.

days.name: Bathtub Day
days.about: A day about the bathtub. People take a long, relaxing soak and learn a bit about the history of the tub and indoor plumbing.

days.name: Bathtub Party Day
days.about: A made-up holiday encouraging people to skip the quick shower and enjoy a proper bath instead, maybe with bubbles, music or snacks, or even a fun bath 'party.'

days.name: Batman Day
days.about: A day DC Comics promotes for the Batman character. Comic shops and stores run events, giveaways and special editions, and fans dress up or rewatch the films.

days.name: Battery Day
days.about: A day linked to the birthday of Alessandro Volta, inventor of the battery. People learn about batteries, check and replace old ones in smoke alarms and devices, and recycle dead ones properly.

days.name: Bavarian Cream Pie Day
days.about: A food day for eating or baking Bavarian cream pie, a pie filled with a rich custard-and-whipped-cream filling.

days.name: Be a Millionaire Day
days.about: A day for thinking about your finances and setting goals for building wealth, like saving, investing or planning toward that first million.

days.name: Be An Angel Day
days.about: A day started by a minister to encourage small acts of kindness. The idea is to do something helpful for someone else, often quietly.

days.name: Be Bald And Free Day
days.about: A day for bald people to embrace their baldness, going without hats or hairpieces and being comfortable with how they look.

days.name: Be Heard Day
days.about: A day for small businesses to get noticed. Owners promote what they do, and customers shop at small businesses or share them on social media.

days.name: Be Humble Day
days.about: A day to practice humility: listen more, give others credit and keep your ego in check.

days.name: Be Kind To Lawyers Day
days.about: A day started to counter lawyer bashing. It asks people to drop the lawyer jokes and thank the attorneys who've helped them, and it nudges lawyers to act in ways that earn respect.

days.name: Be Late For Something Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day from the Procrastinators' Club of America. People take it easy, stop rushing and let themselves show up late on purpose.

days.name: Beagle day
days.about: A day for beagles, when owners share photos and spoil their dogs, and some people consider adopting one from a rescue.

days.name: Bean Day
days.about: A day for cooking and eating beans of all kinds. It's sometimes tied to the memory of Gregor Mendel, who did his famous genetics work with peas.

days.name: Beard Day
days.about: A day for growing, grooming and showing off beards, with some beard contests and gatherings held around it.

days.name: Beaujolais Nouveau Day
days.about: The day that year's Beaujolais Nouveau, a young French red wine, is released, and people open the first bottles at parties, bars and wine shops.

days.name: Beautician’s Day
days.about: A day to thank hairdressers, stylists and other beauty professionals, often with a tip, card or small gift.

days.name: Beaver Day
days.about: A day for learning about beavers and how their dams create wetlands that help water, wildlife and fire resistance. It honors conservationist Dorothy Richards, who lived alongside beavers.

days.name: Beef Tallow Day
days.about: Started by the Healthy Fats Coalition to bring attention to beef tallow and other traditional animal fats used in cooking. People learn about tallow and try cooking or frying with it.

days.name: Beer and Pizza Day
days.about: A day for having pizza with a beer, whether at home or at a pizzeria or brewpub.

days.name: Beer Can Appreciation Day
days.about: It marks the anniversary of the first canned beer going on sale in 1935. Collectors show off their cans and people crack open a canned beer.

days.name: Beer Day
days.about: It marks the day in 1933 when beer became legal to sell again as Prohibition was loosened. People go out for a beer at a bar or brewery.

days.name: Beer Day Britain
days.about: Britain's beer day, held on the anniversary of Magna Carta, which mentions ale. Pubs promote British beer and people raise a glass together in a nationwide 'Cheers to Beer' toast.

days.name: Beer Lover’s Day
days.about: A day for people who enjoy beer and the grains, hops and brewing methods behind it. People have a beer with friends, try local brews and give a shout-out to their favorite brewers.

days.name: Belly Laugh Day
days.about: A day to have a good, hearty laugh. Participants are encouraged to throw their arms up and laugh out loud at an agreed time.

days.name: Bellydance Day
days.about: A day for belly dancing, when dancers hold performances, workshops and classes to share the art form.

days.name: Best Friends Day
days.about: A day to spend time with your best friend or reach out and let them know you appreciate them.

days.name: Better Breakfast Day
days.about: A day to encourage eating a healthy breakfast instead of skipping it or grabbing junk food.

days.name: Beverage Day
days.about: A day for slowing down and enjoying your favorite drink, whether it's hot or cold, alcoholic or not.

days.name: Bicarbonate of Soda Day
days.about: A day for baking soda and its many uses in baking, cleaning, deodorizing and home remedies.

days.name: Bicycle Day
days.about: It marks Albert Hofmann's 1943 bike ride home while experiencing the first deliberate LSD trip. Psychedelic enthusiasts recognize it with gatherings and talks.

days.name: Bike To Work Day
days.about: A day promoted by cycling groups to get people to commute by bike, often with organized group rides and free snacks along the routes.

days.name: Bikini Day
days.about: It marks the anniversary of the bikini's debut in Paris in 1946. People mention it as a nod to the swimsuit and to beach season.

days.name: Binge Day
days.about: A day for guilt-free bingeing, mostly binge-watching a favorite TV series or set of films in one sitting.

days.name: Biodiesel Day
days.about: It marks Rudolf Diesel running an engine on peanut oil in 1893. The day promotes biodiesel and other renewable fuels made from plant oils and fats.

days.name: Biographers Day
days.about: It marks the day James Boswell met Samuel Johnson, whose famous biography he later wrote. People read a biography or think about whose life story they'd like to know.

days.name: Biological Clock Day
days.about: A day to learn about the body's internal clock, which controls when you sleep, wake, and feel alert, and to work on getting your own sleep schedule back on track.

days.name: Bird Day
days.about: A day started by bird welfare groups to raise awareness about birds in captivity and in the wild. People go birdwatching, put out feeders or learn about protecting birds.

days.name: Biscotti Day
days.about: A day for eating or baking biscotti, the crunchy twice-baked Italian cookies often dipped in coffee.

days.name: Biscuit Day
days.about: A day for baking and eating biscuits, often with butter, jam or gravy.

days.name: Bittersweet Chocolate Day
days.about: A day for eating bittersweet chocolate, the dark, less sugary kind, on its own or in baking.

days.name: Bittersweet Chocolate With Almonds Day
days.about: A day for eating dark bittersweet chocolate paired with almonds.

days.name: Black Cat Appreciation Day
days.about: A day to counter superstitions about black cats and encourage people to adopt them, since they're often passed over in shelters. Its founder started it in memory of his sister's black cat.

days.name: Black Cat Day
days.about: A day started by the UK charity Cats Protection to push back against bad-luck myths and encourage people to adopt black cats, which tend to wait longest for homes.

days.name: Black Forest Cake Day
days.about: A day for eating or baking Black Forest cake, the German chocolate cake layered with cherries and whipped cream.

days.name: Black Friday
days.about: The day after Thanksgiving in the US, when stores run big sales to kick off holiday shopping and people line up early for deals.

days.name: Blah Blah Blah Day
days.about: A day to stop talking about the things you keep meaning to do and actually get them done.

days.name: Blame Someone Else Day
days.about: A joke day started by a woman in New York after a rough morning, giving people permission to pin their mishaps on someone else for the day.

days.name: Blase’ Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day that gives you permission to feel bored and unimpressed by just about everything. It's meant for world-weary people who want to enjoy their indifference.

days.name: Blogger Day
days.about: A day for recognizing bloggers and blogging. It's tied to Blogger, one of the earliest blog-publishing platforms.

days.name: Blonde Brownie Day
days.about: A food day for blondies, the brown-sugar-and-butter cousin of the chocolate brownie. People bake a batch or pick some up.

days.name: Bloody Mary Day
days.about: A day for the tomato-juice-and-vodka cocktail, often as a brunch or hangover drink. People mix one up, often with elaborate garnishes.

days.name: Blue Monday
days.about: A Monday in January billed as the most depressing day of the year, an idea that began as a 2005 travel-company PR stunt. People use it as a reason to check in on each other or do something cheering.

days.name: Blueberry Cheesecake Day
days.about: A food day for cheesecake topped or swirled with blueberries. People make or order a slice.

days.name: Blueberry Muffin Day
days.about: A food day for blueberry muffins. People bake some or grab one with their coffee.

days.name: Blueberry Pancake Day
days.about: A food day for pancakes made with blueberries. People have them for breakfast.

days.name: Blueberry Pie Day
days.about: A food day for blueberry pie. People bake one or have a slice.

days.name: Blueberry Popover Day
days.about: A food day for popovers, the light hollow eggy rolls, made with blueberries. People try baking them.

days.name: Blueberry Popsicle Day
days.about: A food day for blueberry ice pops. People buy or freeze their own.

days.name: Bobblehead Day
days.about: A day started by the National Bobblehead Hall of Fame and Museum for the nodding-head figurines. Collectors show off their bobbleheads and people buy new ones.

days.name: Bologna Day
days.about: A food day for bologna, the lunch meat. People have a bologna sandwich, sometimes fried.

days.name: Bomb Pop Day
days.about: A day for the red, white and blue rocket-shaped popsicle, promoted by the company that makes it. People eat one, usually outdoors in summer.

days.name: Book Lovers Day
days.about: A day for reading. People set aside time with a book, swap recommendations or visit a library or bookstore.

days.name: Boss/Employee Exchange Day
days.about: A day for bosses and employees to swap roles so each side sees what the other's job is really like.

days.name: Boss’ Day
days.about: A day for employees to thank their managers, started in 1958 by a secretary who picked her boss and father's birthday. People give a card, lunch or small gift.

days.name: Boston Cream Pie Day
days.about: A food day for Boston cream pie, actually a sponge cake filled with custard and topped with chocolate. People bake or order one.

days.name: Bouillabaisse Day
days.about: A food day for bouillabaisse, the Provençal fish stew from Marseille. People cook it or order it at a seafood restaurant.

days.name: Bourbon Day
days.about: A day for bourbon, the American corn-based whiskey. People have a glass or a bourbon cocktail, or visit a distillery.

days.name: Bow Tie Day
days.about: A day for wearing a bow tie. People put one on, sometimes learning to tie a real one.

days.name: Bowling Day
days.about: A day for ten-pin bowling. People go to the lanes with friends or family.

days.name: BoxKart Bash Day
days.about: Named after the Burghfield BoxKart Bash, a charity race where teams build homemade soapbox karts and race them downhill. People build or race karts, or go and watch.

days.name: Boyfriend’s Day
days.about: A day for appreciating your boyfriend. People do something nice for him or spend time together.

days.name: Brandied Fruit Day
days.about: A food day for fruit preserved or soaked in brandy. People make a jar or use some over desserts.

days.name: Break The Monotony Day
days.about: A day for breaking out of your usual routine. People try something new, like going somewhere they haven't been or learning a new skill.

days.name: Bridge Day
days.about: A yearly festival at West Virginia's New River Gorge Bridge, the one day the bridge is closed to traffic. BASE jumpers leap off it and crowds walk across and watch.

days.name: Bring Flowers To Someone Day
days.about: A day for giving flowers to someone for no particular reason, whether that's a friend, family member, coworker or stranger. People pick or buy a bouquet and drop it off, or have one delivered.

days.name: Bring Your Bible to School Day
days.about: A day promoted by Focus on the Family for students to bring a Bible to school. Kids carry one and talk about their faith with classmates.

days.name: Bring Your Manners To Work Day
days.about: Started by The Protocol School of Washington as a reminder about good manners and etiquette at work. People make a point of being polite and considerate to coworkers and clients.

days.name: Bring Your Teddy Bear To Work & School Day
days.about: A light-hearted day for taking your teddy bear (or a favourite stuffed toy) along to work or school. Kids and adults bring them in for a bit of comfort and fun.

days.name: Brisket Day
days.about: A food day for brisket, the slow-cooked beef cut. People smoke or braise one or go out for barbecue.

days.name: Broadcast Traffic Professionals Day
days.about: A day for the TV and radio staff who schedule commercials and programs, the 'traffic' department, not road reporters. Stations thank the people who do this behind-the-scenes work.

days.name: Brother’s Day
days.about: A day for appreciating brothers. People call, message or spend time with theirs.

days.name: Brownie Day
days.about: A food day for chocolate brownies. People bake a pan or share some.

days.name: Brutus Day
days.about: Named after Brutus, who betrayed Julius Caesar, it's a reminder that backstabbing still goes on. People use it to think about who in their lives they can really trust and to drop the ones who don't have their back.

days.name: Bubble Bath Day
days.about: A day for taking a bubble bath and relaxing. People run a bath and take some time for themselves.

days.name: Bubble Wrap Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for bubble wrap, started in 2001 by a radio station in Indiana. People pop it for fun and do bubble-wrap games and crafts.

days.name: Bubblegum Day
days.about: A day started by children's author Ruth Spiro, when schools let kids chew gum in exchange for a small donation to charity. People blow bubbles and raise money.

days.name: Buckfast Day
days.about: A day for fans of Buckfast, the strong tonic wine made by monks at Buckfast Abbey in Devon. It was started in 2015 by Wreck The Hoose Juice Ltd, and people mark it by getting together to drink it.

days.name: Buffet Day
days.about: A day for all-you-can-eat buffets. People go out to one or lay out a spread at home.

days.name: Build A Scarecrow Day
days.about: A day for making your own scarecrow. People build them from old clothes and stuffing to put in gardens or fields to keep birds and pests away.

days.name: Building and Code Staff Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for thanking the people who manage and enforce building codes, the inspectors and code officials whose work keeps buildings safe.

days.name: Bulldogs Are Beautiful Day
days.about: A day for showing appreciation for bulldogs, set up by children's book author Jackie Valent in 2007. Owners spend it pampering their bulldogs and showing them off.

days.name: Bundt Cake Day
days.about: A food day for Bundt cake, baked in the ring-shaped fluted pan. People bake one.

days.name: Bunsen Burner Day
days.about: A day on chemist Robert Bunsen's birthday, recognizing the lab gas burner named after him. Science teachers and students mark it with experiments.

days.name: Burger Day
days.about: A food day for hamburgers. People grill some or go out for one, often with restaurant deals.

days.name: Burlesque Day
days.about: A day for the art and history of burlesque, the comic, cabaret-style stage performance. People go to burlesque shows, watch burlesque films or read up on how the form developed.

days.name: Business Women’s Day
days.about: A day marking the founding of the American Business Women's Association in 1949, recognizing women in business. Groups hold events and networking meetups.

days.name: Buttercrunch Day
days.about: A food day for buttercrunch, a toffee often coated in chocolate and nuts. People make or buy some.

days.name: Butterscotch Cinnamon Pie Day
days.about: A day for pie that combines butterscotch and cinnamon, which became popular through the video game Undertale. People bake the pie, share it and eat it.

days.name: Butterscotch Pudding Day
days.about: A food day for butterscotch pudding. People make a batch or have a cup.

days.name: Button Day
days.about: A day for appreciating buttons, from collecting antique and decorative ones to sorting through the button jar. It traces back to the founding of the National Button Society.

days.name: Buy a Book Day
days.about: A nudge to buy a book, ideally from a local bookstore or an author you want to support.

days.name: Buy Nothing Day
days.about: A protest against consumerism on the day after US Thanksgiving, when people skip shopping entirely. Adbusters popularized it.

days.name: Buzzards Day
days.about: Hinckley, Ohio marks the yearly return of its turkey vultures, and people gather to watch for the birds and join in local festivities.

days.name: Cab Franc Day
days.about: A day for drinking and learning about Cabernet Franc, the red grape behind many Loire Valley and Bordeaux wines.

days.name: Cable Car Day
days.about: Marks Andrew Hallidie's patent for the cable car system that became San Francisco's famous cable cars. People ride them or learn their history.

days.name: Caesar Salad Day
days.about: A day for eating Caesar salad, credited to restaurateur Caesar Cardini in Tijuana in the 1920s.

days.name: Cake Day
days.about: An excuse to bake or eat cake of any kind.

days.name: Cake Decorating Day
days.about: A day for trying your hand at frosting, piping and decorating cakes, or admiring other people's work.

days.name: Calendar Adjustment Day
days.about: Recalls Britain and its colonies switching to the Gregorian calendar in 1752, when eleven days were skipped. It's mostly a chance to learn about calendar history.

days.name: Call Your Doctor Day
days.about: A reminder to book the checkups and screenings you've been putting off, especially aimed at women's health.

days.name: Camcorder Day
days.about: A day honoring the portable camcorder and video recording devices in general. People take out a video camera and shoot some footage, or watch old home videos.

days.name: Camera Day
days.about: A day for appreciating cameras and photography, usually by going out and taking some pictures.

days.name: Canada Day
days.about: Canada's national holiday, marking confederation in 1867. People take the day off for fireworks, parades and barbecues.

days.name: Canadian Bacon Day
days.about: A day for eating Canadian or back bacon, the lean cured pork loin, or Canada's peameal bacon.

days.name: Canadian Beer Day
days.about: The Wednesday before Canadian Thanksgiving, set aside to honour Canadian beer and the people who brew, sell, serve and drink it. People have a Canadian beer, often from a local brewery or pub.

days.name: Canadian Thanksgiving
days.about: Canada's harvest thanksgiving holiday, held in October. Families get together for a big meal, often turkey.

days.name: Cancer Survivors Day
days.about: A day honoring people who have survived cancer, with community events, walks and gatherings for survivors and their families.

days.name: Candied Orange Peel Day
days.about: A day for making or eating candied orange peel, the sugar-preserved peel used in baking and as candy.

days.name: Candlemas day
days.about: A Christian feast of the Presentation of Jesus at the Temple, when churches bless candles. Old folk lore uses the day's weather to predict how long winter will last.

days.name: Candy Cane Day
days.about: A day for eating or decorating with candy canes, the striped peppermint Christmas candy.

days.name: Candy Corn Day
days.about: A day for eating candy corn, the tri-colored Halloween candy people either love or hate.

days.name: Candy Day
days.about: An excuse to eat or share your favorite candy.

days.name: Canoe Day
days.about: A day for paddling a canoe and appreciating its history, started by the Canadian Canoe Museum.

days.name: Cappuccino Day
days.about: A day for drinking cappuccino, espresso topped with steamed and foamed milk.

days.name: Caps Lock Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day poking fun at people who type in all caps. Some people type everything in capitals for the day as a joke.

days.name: Car Insurance Day
days.about: A reminder to look over your car insurance policy and make sure your coverage still fits your needs at a fair price. People use it to review their policy, compare quotes or check their liability limits.

days.name: Caramel Apple Day
days.about: A day for making or eating apples dipped in caramel, a fall fair favorite.

days.name: Caramel Day
days.about: A day for eating caramel in any form, from candies to sauces.

days.name: Caramel Popcorn Day
days.about: A day for making or snacking on caramel-coated popcorn.

days.name: Carbonated Beverage with Caffeine Day
days.about: A day for drinking caffeinated sodas like cola.

days.name: Card Making Day
days.about: A day for making handmade greeting cards, promoted by paper-crafting and stamping companies.

days.name: Card Playing Day
days.about: A day for getting together to play card games, from poker to solitaire.

days.name: Carousel Day
days.about: Marks an early US patent for a carousel design. People ride merry-go-rounds or learn about carousel history and carving.

days.name: Carpe Diem Day
days.about: A nudge to seize the day by doing something you've been putting off or making the most of the day.

days.name: Carrot Cake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating carrot cake, usually with cream cheese frosting.

days.name: Carrot Day
days.about: A day for eating carrots and learning about the vegetable.

days.name: Cartoonists’ Day
days.about: Honors cartoonists on the anniversary of the Yellow Kid, an early newspaper comic character. People read comics or appreciate their favorite artists.

days.name: Cashew Day
days.about: A day for eating cashews, on their own or in cooking.

days.name: Cat Day
days.about: A day for appreciating cats and encouraging people to adopt from shelters.

days.name: Cat Herders Day
days.about: A humorous day for anyone whose job means managing chaotic people or projects, as in 'like herding cats.'

days.name: Catfish Day
days.about: Proclaimed by President Reagan to promote farm-raised catfish. People eat catfish dishes.

days.name: Caves and Karst Day
days.about: A day for learning about caves and karst landscapes and why they matter for groundwater. Some people visit show caves.

days.name: Caviar Day
days.about: A day for eating caviar, the salted fish roe treated as a luxury.

days.name: CD Player Day
days.about: Marks the release of the first commercial CD players in the early 1980s. People dig out their old CDs.

days.name: Celebrate Bisexuality Day
days.about: A day for recognizing bisexual people and their history and community. It was started in 1999 by bisexual activists Wendy Curry, Michael Page and Gigi Raven Wilbur.

days.name: Celebrate Your Unique Talent Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the skills and odd abilities that make each person different. People show off a party trick or hobby, teach someone what they're good at or try to find a new talent.

days.name: Celebration Of Life Day
days.about: Originally a day for honoring the children and grandchildren in your life, it has grown into a day for being grateful to be alive. People give kids extra attention, do fun things together with family, or just stop to appreciate their own lives.

days.name: Celiac Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness of celiac disease, the autoimmune reaction to gluten. It falls on the birthday of Samuel Gee, who described the condition.

days.name: Cellophane Tape Day
days.about: Marks Richard Drew's patent for clear Scotch tape, the everyday office and gift-wrapping staple.

days.name: Cereal Day
days.about: A day for enjoying a bowl of breakfast cereal, whether an old favorite or something new.

days.name: Ceviche Day
days.about: A day for eating ceviche, raw fish or seafood cured in citrus juice. It is especially popular in Peru, where the dish is a national point of pride.

days.name: Chainmail Day
days.about: A day about chainmail, the medieval armor made of linked metal rings, and the craft of making it. People visit museums or medieval fairs, watch videos on how it's made, or try weaving something small like a chainmail bracelet.

days.name: Champagne Day
days.about: A day for opening a bottle of Champagne and learning a bit about the French region and wines behind the name.

days.name: Change A Light Day
days.about: An energy-saving campaign that asks people to swap at least one bulb at home for an energy-efficient one.

days.name: Chaos Never Dies Day
days.about: A day for admitting that everyday life at home, school or work is often hectic and messy. People accept the chaos, take a deep breath and try to bring a little order back into their lives.

days.name: Check The Chip Day
days.about: A reminder from vets to make sure your pet's microchip is registered and your contact details are up to date, so a lost pet can be returned.

days.name: Check Your Batteries Day
days.about: A reminder to test and replace the batteries in smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. It's usually tied to the clock changes for daylight saving time.

days.name: Checkers Day
days.about: A day for playing a game of checkers (draughts) with someone.

days.name: Checklist Day
days.about: Marks the 1935 crash of a Boeing test plane that led to pilots using preflight checklists. It's a nudge to appreciate checklists and use them in your own work and life.

days.name: Cheese Day
days.about: A day for eating and sampling all kinds of cheese.

days.name: Cheese Doodle Day
days.about: A day for snacking on cheese doodles, the puffy orange cheese-flavored corn snacks.

days.name: Cheese Fondue Day
days.about: A day for making cheese fondue and dipping bread and other bites into a pot of melted cheese.

days.name: Cheese Lovers Day
days.about: A day for cheese fans to enjoy their favorite cheeses or try some new ones.

days.name: Cheese Pizza Day
days.about: A day for eating a plain cheese pizza.

days.name: Cheese Toast Day
days.about: A day for making cheese toast, bread topped with melted cheese.

days.name: Cheeseball Day
days.about: A day for making or serving a cheese ball, the round party spread usually rolled in nuts and eaten with crackers.

days.name: Cheeseburger Day
days.about: A day for eating a cheeseburger, often with restaurants offering deals.

days.name: Cheesecake Day
days.about: A day for eating cheesecake, in any style or flavor.

days.name: Cherish An Antique Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the old things you own, like heirloom furniture, coins or a grandparent's keepsakes. People dust them off and put them on display, or visit antique shops and exhibitions to learn more.

days.name: Cherries Jubilee Day
days.about: A day for making cherries jubilee, a dessert of cherries flambéed in liqueur and usually spooned over vanilla ice cream.

days.name: Cherry Pie Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating cherry pie.

days.name: Cherry Popover Day
days.about: A day for making cherry popovers, light, puffy baked rolls filled with or served with cherries.

days.name: Cherry Popsicle Day
days.about: A day for cooling off with a cherry popsicle.

days.name: Cherry Tart Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating a cherry tart.

days.name: Cherry Turnover Day
days.about: A day for eating cherry turnovers, pastries folded over a cherry filling.

days.name: Chic Spy™ Day
days.about: A fashion website started this day to honor the style of fictional spies in films and on TV, and it falls on the anniversary of James Bond's screen debut. Fans dress up in their best spy-inspired outfits.

days.name: Chicken Cacciatore Day
days.about: A day for cooking chicken cacciatore, the Italian 'hunter-style' chicken braised with tomatoes, peppers, onions and herbs.

days.name: Chicken Dance Day
days.about: A day for doing the Chicken Dance, the silly flapping dance familiar from weddings and polka parties.

days.name: Chicken Finger Day
days.about: A day for eating chicken fingers, the breaded strips of chicken usually served with dipping sauce.

days.name: Chicken Soup for the Soul Day
days.about: Tied to the 'Chicken Soup for the Soul' book series. It encourages people to do something kind and share uplifting stories.

days.name: Children’s Book Day
days.about: International Children's Book Day falls on Hans Christian Andersen's birthday. It promotes reading and children's books, so people read with kids and give them books.

days.name: Chili Dog Day
days.about: A day for eating chili dogs, hot dogs topped with chili and often cheese and onions.

days.name: Chilli Day
days.about: A day for making and eating a pot of chili. Some people hold cook-offs to compare recipes.

days.name: Chimborazo Day
days.about: About Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador, whose summit is the point on Earth farthest from the planet's center because of the bulge at the equator. People learn about the mountain and that bit of geography.

days.name: Chinese Language Day
days.about: One of the UN's language days, honoring Chinese and Cangjie, the legendary inventor of Chinese characters. People learn about the language and its writing.

days.name: Chip and Dip Day
days.about: A day for snacking on chips with a dip, such as salsa, guacamole or French onion.

days.name: Chocolate Cake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating chocolate cake.

days.name: Chocolate Caramel Day
days.about: A day for treats that pair chocolate with caramel.

days.name: Chocolate Chip Day
days.about: A day for chocolate chips, most often baked into a batch of chocolate chip cookies.

days.name: Chocolate Covered Anything Day
days.about: A day for dipping whatever you like in chocolate, from fruit and pretzels to more unusual things.

days.name: Chocolate Covered Cashews Day
days.about: A day for snacking on cashews coated in chocolate.

days.name: Chocolate Covered Raisins Day
days.about: A day for eating chocolate-covered raisins, the movie-theater candy staple.

days.name: Chocolate Cupcake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating chocolate cupcakes.

days.name: Chocolate Day
days.about: A general day for enjoying chocolate in any form.

days.name: Chocolate Fondue Day
days.about: A day for melting a pot of chocolate and dipping fruit, marshmallows or cake into it.

days.name: Chocolate Ice Cream Day
days.about: A day for eating a scoop or bowl of chocolate ice cream.

days.name: Chocolate Macaroon Day
days.about: A day for eating chocolate macaroons, the chewy coconut cookies made with or dipped in chocolate.

days.name: Chocolate Milkshake Day
days.about: A day for having a chocolate milkshake.

days.name: Chocolate Mint Day
days.about: A day for treats that combine chocolate and mint, such as mint chocolate candies or mint chocolate chip ice cream.

days.name: Chocolate Mousse Day
days.about: A food day for making or eating chocolate mousse, the light, airy whipped chocolate dessert.

days.name: Chocolate Pecan Pie Day
days.about: A food day for baking or eating pecan pie with chocolate added to the filling.

days.name: Chocolate Pudding Day
days.about: A food day for making or eating chocolate pudding.

days.name: Chocolate Soufflé Day
days.about: A food day for trying to bake, or ordering, a puffed-up chocolate soufflé.

days.name: Chocolate Wafer Day
days.about: A food day for eating thin chocolate wafer cookies, on their own or in desserts like icebox cake.

days.name: Chocolate with Almonds Day
days.about: A food day for eating chocolate with almonds, such as an almond chocolate bar.

days.name: Chocolate Éclair Day
days.about: A food day for eating chocolate éclairs, the cream-filled pastries with chocolate icing on top.

days.name: Chocolate-Covered Cherry Day
days.about: A food day for eating chocolate-covered cherries, the boxed candies with a cherry and syrupy filling inside.

days.name: Chocolate-Covered Peanuts Day
days.about: A food day for snacking on chocolate-covered peanuts.

days.name: Chocolates Day
days.about: A food day for eating or giving boxed chocolates and other chocolate candies.

days.name: Chop Suey Day
days.about: A food day for eating chop suey, the Chinese-American stir-fry of meat and vegetables in sauce.

days.name: Choral Day
days.about: Also called World Choral Day, it was started by the International Federation for Choral Music as a day for choral singing. Choirs around the world hold concerts and sing together, often around a shared theme like peace.

days.name: Christmas Card Day
days.about: Marks the first commercial Christmas card, made in England in 1843 for Henry Cole. People use it as a nudge to write and send their holiday cards.

days.name: Cinnamon-Raisin Bread Day
days.about: A food day for eating cinnamon-raisin bread, often toasted with butter.

days.name: Clam Chowder Day
days.about: A food day for eating clam chowder, whether creamy New England style or tomato-based Manhattan style.

days.name: Clarinet Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the clarinet, when people listen to clarinet music or play their own.

days.name: Clean Comedy Day
days.about: A day for comedy without profanity or crude material. People watch or share family-friendly comedy that everyone can laugh at.

days.name: Clean Off Your Desk Day
days.about: A January day for clearing the clutter and old paperwork off your desk to start the year organized.

days.name: Clean Out Your Computer Day
days.about: A day for tidying up your computer: deleting old files, organizing folders, backing things up, and physically dusting it off.

days.name: Clean Out Your Refrigerator Day
days.about: Falls shortly before Thanksgiving, for throwing out old leftovers and expired food to make room for holiday cooking.

days.name: Clean Your Aquarium Day
days.about: A reminder for people with fish tanks to give their aquarium a good, thorough cleaning at least once a year. People scrub the glass, change some of the water and tidy the tank so their fish and plants stay healthy.

days.name: Clean Your Floors Day
days.about: A day for cleaning the floors in your home, whether they're hardwood, tile, vinyl or carpet. You can do it by yourself or with family or friends.

days.name: Clean Your Virtual Desktop Day
days.about: A day for clearing the clutter of icons and files off your computer desktop and organizing them into folders.

days.name: Cliché Day
days.about: A lighthearted day about clichés, for noticing overused phrases or playing with them on purpose.

days.name: Client’s Day
days.about: A day for business owners and managers to thank their clients. Customers often get discounts, special offers and small gifts.

days.name: Clinical Trials Day
days.about: Marks James Lind's 1747 scurvy experiment, often called the first clinical trial. It honors the researchers and volunteers who make medical studies possible.

days.name: Cloves Syndrome Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness of CLOVES syndrome, a rare congenital disorder involving tissue overgrowth and vascular malformations, and supports affected families.

days.name: Coast Guard Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the US Coast Guard's predecessor in 1790 and honors Coast Guard members, with events in Coast Guard towns.

days.name: Coastal Cleanup Day
days.about: Tied to the Ocean Conservancy's International Coastal Cleanup, when volunteers pick up trash from beaches and waterways and record what they find.

days.name: Coconut Torte Day
days.about: A food day for baking or eating a coconut torte, a layered cake made with coconut.

days.name: Coffee Ice Cream Day
days.about: A food day for eating coffee-flavored ice cream.

days.name: Coffee Milk Shake Day
days.about: A food day for drinking a coffee milkshake, a favorite in New England.

days.name: Cognac Day
days.about: A day for sipping cognac, the brandy from the Cognac region of France.

days.name: Cold Cuts Day
days.about: A food day for sliced deli meats, usually eaten in sandwiches or on a platter.

days.name: Collect Rocks Day
days.about: A day for picking up interesting rocks, adding to a rock collection, or starting one.

days.name: College Colors Day
days.about: Started by the Collegiate Licensing Company, it's a day near the start of football season for wearing your college's colors or gear.

days.name: College Student Grief Awareness Day
days.about: Started by the group Actively Moving Forward to draw attention to college students grieving a loved one's death and the support they need.

days.name: Color TV Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the first commercial color TV broadcast, which CBS aired in 1951. It's a day to remember how TV went from black-and-white to color.

days.name: Coloring Book Day
days.about: A day for picking up crayons or colored pencils and filling in a coloring book, for kids and adults alike.

days.name: Columbus Day
days.about: A US federal holiday marking Christopher Columbus's 1492 arrival in the Americas, often observed with parades and Italian-American heritage events. Many places now mark it as Indigenous Peoples' Day instead.

days.name: Columnists Day
days.about: Honors newspaper columnists on the anniversary of war correspondent Ernie Pyle's death in 1945.

days.name: Comic Book Day
days.about: A day for reading comic books and appreciating the artists and writers who make them. It's separate from the industry's Free Comic Book Day.

days.name: Coming Out Day
days.about: Started in 1988 to mark the anniversary of the 1987 March on Washington for gay rights, it's a day supporting LGBTQ people who come out and raising visibility.

days.name: Commitment Day
days.about: A day for showing love and commitment to the person closest to your heart.

days.name: Common Courtesy Day
days.about: A reminder to practice basic manners, like saying please and thank you and holding doors for people.

days.name: Community Media Day
days.about: A day to recognize community radio and TV stations, and the people and groups behind them, that support free speech and make media open to everyone. The idea is that anyone should be able to share their story.

days.name: Companies That Care Day
days.about: A day for employers to think about how well they look after their staff and their local community. Companies might thank employees with lunches, massages or notes of appreciation, or ask staff how valued they feel.

days.name: Compliment Your Mirror Day
days.about: A day for looking in the mirror and saying something kind to yourself, as a small self-esteem boost.

days.name: Computer Security Day
days.about: Started in 1988 to remind people to protect their computers and data, by updating passwords, installing updates, and backing up files.

days.name: Concussion Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness about concussions, especially in sports: how to recognize the signs and why proper recovery matters.

days.name: Conflict Resolution Day
days.about: A day started by the Association for Conflict Resolution to promote mediation and other peaceful ways of settling disputes. Schools, courts and community groups hold workshops and events about it.

days.name: Constitution Day
days.about: Marks the signing of the US Constitution in 1787. Schools and federal agencies hold lessons and readings about the document.

days.name: Cook a Sweet Potato Day
days.about: A food day for cooking sweet potatoes, whether baked, mashed, fried or in a pie.

days.name: Cook Something Bold and Pungent Day
days.about: A day for cooking with strong flavors like garlic, onions, chilies, ginger or curry, and trying something more intense than usual.

days.name: Cookie Day
days.about: A day for baking, sharing and eating cookies of any kind.

days.name: Cooking Day
days.about: A day to encourage home cooking. A cookware seller started it, and people mark it by making a meal from scratch with fresh ingredients or by learning a basic kitchen skill.

days.name: Copyright Law Day
days.about: Marks the first US federal copyright law, passed in 1790. People use it to learn about copyright and creators' rights.

days.name: Coquito Day
days.about: A day for coquito, the Puerto Rican holiday drink of coconut, rum and spices. People make it and share it with friends and family.

days.name: Cordon Bleu Day
days.about: A food day for cordon bleu, chicken or veal wrapped around ham and cheese, then breaded and fried or baked.

days.name: Corgi Day
days.about: A day for corgi fans. A corgi owners' group in Omaha started it to raise money for corgi rescue, and people share corgi photos, hold corgi meet-ups and support rescue groups.

days.name: Corn Dog Day
days.about: Started by friends in Oregon and held on the first Saturday of the NCAA basketball tournament. People eat corn dogs, often with tater tots and beer, while watching the games.

days.name: Corn Fritters Day
days.about: A food day for corn fritters, fried batter cakes studded with corn kernels.

days.name: Corn On The Cob Day
days.about: A summer food day for eating fresh corn on the cob, usually boiled or grilled with butter and salt.

days.name: Cornchip Day
days.about: A snack day for corn chips, eaten plain, with dips, or in dishes like Frito pie.

days.name: Corned Beef Hash Day
days.about: A food day for corned beef hash, chopped corned beef fried with potatoes and onions, often eaten at breakfast with eggs.

days.name: Cosmopolitan Day
days.about: A day for the cosmopolitan cocktail of vodka, triple sec, cranberry juice and lime.

days.name: Cotton Candy Day
days.about: A day for eating cotton candy, the spun sugar treat familiar from fairs and carnivals.

days.name: Count Your Buttons Day
days.about: A silly day for finding out how many buttons you own by counting the ones on your clothes and around the house. Some people also wear or collect pin-back buttons.

days.name: Country Inn Bed & Breakfast Day
days.about: A day to appreciate small country inns and B&Bs. People mark it by booking a stay or a weekend away at one, often a local, family-run place.

days.name: Cousins Day
days.about: A day for getting in touch with your cousins, whether by calling, visiting or spending time together.

days.name: Cow Appreciation Day
days.about: Chick-fil-A's promotion, tied to its cows urging people to 'eat mor chikin'. Customers who come in dressed as a cow get free food.

days.name: Coworking Day
days.about: Marks the opening of the first coworking space in San Francisco in 2005. Shared workspaces hold open houses and events.

days.name: Crabmeat Day
days.about: A food day for crabmeat, eaten in crab cakes, salads, dips or straight from the shell.

days.name: Crackers Over The Keyboard Day
days.about: Thomas and Ruth Roy of Wellcat Holidays came up with this joke day. You bring crackers or cookies to work and eat them right over your keyboard, crumbs and all, to show you're still a free thinker.

days.name: Craft Jerky Day
days.about: A day for small, artisanal jerky makers and the skill that goes into making jerky. People buy or try craft jerky, or make their own with whatever meat and seasonings they like.

days.name: Cranberry Relish Day
days.about: A food day for cranberry relish, the tart side dish of chopped cranberries and sugar that's common at Thanksgiving.

days.name: Cranky Co-Workers Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day for co-workers who grumble and complain all year. Everyone lets them stay cranky instead of trying to cheer them up.

days.name: Crayola Crayon Day
days.about: Crayola's day for crayons, honoring the company's history and encouraging kids and adults to color and draw.

days.name: Cream Cheese Brownie Day
days.about: A food day for brownies swirled with a layer of sweetened cream cheese.

days.name: Cream Cheese Frosting Day
days.about: Arla Foods started this day for cream cheese frosting. People make it at home and eat cakes, cupcakes and other desserts topped with it.

days.name: Cream Filled Donut Day
days.about: A food day for donuts filled with custard or cream, like Boston cream.

days.name: Cream Tea Day
days.about: A British day for cream tea, which is scones with jam and clotted cream alongside a pot of tea. It's often used to raise money for charity.

days.name: Cream-Filled Chocolates Day
days.about: A day for chocolates with soft cream or fondant centers, the kind found in boxed assortments.

days.name: Creampuff Day
days.about: A food day for cream puffs, light choux pastry shells filled with whipped cream or custard.

days.name: Creamsicle Day
days.about: A day for creamsicles, the frozen treat of orange ice over vanilla ice cream on a stick.

days.name: Create A Great Funeral Day
days.about: A day to encourage people to plan their own funeral and talk about their wishes with family, so loved ones aren't left guessing.

days.name: Creative Ice Cream Flavor Day
days.about: A day for inventing or trying unusual ice cream flavors and mixing in unexpected ingredients.

days.name: Crepe Day
days.about: A day for making and eating crepes, the thin French pancakes served sweet or savory.

days.name: Croissant Day
days.about: A food day for croissants, the flaky, buttery crescent-shaped pastries.

days.name: Crossword Puzzle Day
days.about: Marks Arthur Wynne's first crossword, published in a New York newspaper in 1913. People do a crossword or try making one.

days.name: Crowdfunding Day
days.about: A day to spread the word about crowdfunding, where many people each chip in a small amount, usually online, to pay for projects, startups and causes. People back or start campaigns for things they care about.

days.name: Crown Roast of Pork Day
days.about: A food day for crown roast of pork, a rack of pork ribs tied into a ring and roasted, often as a holiday centerpiece.

days.name: Crush a Can Day
days.about: A day to get people recycling. You crush your aluminum cans, maybe pick up cans that have been littered too, and take them to a recycling or buy-back center.

days.name: Crème Brûlée Day
days.about: A food day for crème brûlée, baked custard topped with a layer of caramelized sugar you crack with a spoon.

days.name: Cuban Sandwich Day
days.about: A day for the Cuban sandwich of roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard pressed on Cuban bread. It's especially popular in Tampa and Miami.

days.name: Cubicle Day
days.about: A nod to the office cubicle, which grew out of Herman Miller's Action Office design. Office workers decorate or show off their cubicles.

days.name: Cuddle Up Day
days.about: A cold-weather day for cuddling up with someone you love, or with a pet or a blanket.

days.name: Cupcake Day
days.about: A day for baking and eating cupcakes. In Canada and the UK there's also a Cupcake Day where people hold bake sales to raise money for animal charities.

days.name: Curious Events Day
days.about: A day for looking into strange, odd or unexplained happenings, like the Bermuda Triangle, Stonehenge or the Loch Ness Monster. People read up on the ones that interest them and try to puzzle them out.

days.name: Curling Is Cool Day
days.about: A day to appreciate the sport of curling and get new people to try it. People go curling at a local club, or outside on ice the way the game was first played.

days.name: Curmudgeons Day
days.about: A day honoring the grumpy, cranky people in your life, linked to W.C. Fields' birthday. People tolerate a curmudgeon's grumbling, or embrace their own inner grouch.

days.name: Custodial Worker Day
days.about: A day for thanking the janitors and custodians who keep schools, offices and buildings clean. People write notes, give small gifts, or just say thanks.

days.name: Cut Your Energy Costs Day
days.about: A reminder in the middle of winter to look for ways to lower your energy bills, like sealing drafts, adjusting the thermostat or switching to efficient bulbs.

days.name: Cyber Monday
days.about: The Monday after Thanksgiving, when online retailers run big sales. It was coined by the National Retail Federation's Shop.org as the online counterpart to Black Friday.

days.name: Cycle to Work Day
days.about: A UK-born day encouraging people to ride a bike to work instead of driving, for health and the environment. Many try commuting by bike for the first time.

days.name: D.A.R.E. Day
days.about: A day recognizing the D.A.R.E. program, where police officers teach kids in school about resisting drugs and violence. Schools and police departments hold events and recognize participants.

days.name: Daffodil Day
days.about: A cancer charity fundraiser in countries like Australia, New Zealand, Ireland and Canada, where volunteers sell daffodils or daffodil pins to raise money for cancer research and support.

days.name: Daiquiri Day
days.about: A day for making or ordering a daiquiri, the rum, lime and sugar cocktail from Cuba, whether classic or frozen and fruity.

days.name: Dalek Remembrance Day
days.about: A Doctor Who fan day marking the anniversary of the Daleks' first appearance on the show in 1963. Fans rewatch Dalek episodes and share their love of the villains.

days.name: Darwin Day
days.about: Held on Charles Darwin's birthday to promote science and evolution. Schools, museums and science groups hold talks, lectures and events.

days.name: Data Privacy Day
days.about: An awareness day about protecting personal information online, marking the anniversary of a European data protection treaty. Organizations share tips on passwords, privacy settings and how data is collected.

days.name: Date Nut Bread Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating date nut bread, the moist quick bread made with dates and walnuts.

days.name: Day of Acceptance
days.about: A day started by the 3E Love organization to promote acceptance of people with disabilities, using a wheelchair-heart symbol. People share messages about inclusion and treating everyone with respect.

days.name: Day Of Awesomeness
days.about: Also called the International Day of Awesomeness, it's a fun, unofficial day for honoring awesomeness of every kind. People try a 'feat of awesomeness,' like setting a new personal best or helping someone in an unexpected way.

days.name: Day of Bullying Prevention
days.about: An anti-bullying day, promoted by STOMP Out Bullying, where people wear blue to show they stand against bullying. Schools hold talks and activities on kindness and standing up for others.

days.name: Day Of Hope
days.about: Also called the National Day of Hope, it was started by the nonprofit Childhelp to raise awareness of child abuse and neglect. People say a prayer, keep a moment of silence or light a candle, or do something directly to help protect children.

days.name: Day of Listening
days.about: Started by StoryCorps for the day after Thanksgiving, it encourages people to record a conversation with a family member or friend about their life and memories.

days.name: Day of Mourning
days.about: Another name for Workers' Memorial Day. It's for remembering people who were killed, injured or made ill by their work, and for pushing for safer workplaces, often with memorial events and moments of silence.

days.name: Day of Pink
days.about: An anti-bullying day that began after two Nova Scotia students handed out pink shirts to support a classmate bullied for wearing pink. People wear pink to stand against bullying, homophobia and transphobia.

days.name: Day Of Reconciliation
days.about: A South African public holiday meant to foster national unity and reconciliation after apartheid. People attend commemorations and community events.

days.name: Day Of Silence
days.about: A student-led protest organized by GLSEN, where students stay silent for the day to draw attention to the silencing of LGBTQ people through bullying and harassment.

days.name: Day of the Horse
days.about: Recognized by the US Congress to honor the role horses have played in American history, economy and culture. People visit stables, ride, or support horse rescues.

days.name: Day of Unplugging
days.about: A sundown-to-sundown break from phones and screens, started by the group Reboot. People put away their devices and spend time offline with family, friends and hobbies.

days.name: Day Without Art Day
days.about: Started by the arts group Visual AIDS on World AIDS Day to mourn artists lost to AIDS. Museums and galleries cover or remove artworks, or hold programs about the epidemic.

days.name: Daylight Appreciation Day
days.about: It falls on the summer solstice, the longest day of the year, and is about appreciating sunlight and what it does for us. People spend time outdoors or let more natural light into their homes.

days.name: Dear Diary Day
days.about: A day for writing in a diary or journal, or starting one, to record your thoughts and experiences.

days.name: Decorating With Candy Day
days.about: A day for using candy, often Halloween leftovers, to decorate things like gingerbread houses, cakes and crafts.

days.name: Deep Dish Pizza Day
days.about: A day for eating Chicago-style deep dish pizza, the thick pie with a tall crust, cheese and chunky tomato sauce on top.

days.name: Defy Superstition Day
days.about: A day for ignoring superstitions, like walking under a ladder, opening an umbrella indoors or not worrying about black cats.

days.name: Dentist’s Day
days.about: A day for thanking your dentist and the work they do keeping teeth healthy, and a reminder to book a checkup.

days.name: Department Store Day
days.about: A day about the history of department stores and the part they play in shopping and the economy. These are the big shops that sell many kinds of goods in separate departments under one roof. People mark it by visiting or shopping at one.

days.name: Deskfast Day
days.about: A day for eating breakfast at your desk, often while you start on work or study. Offices sometimes treat staff to a desk breakfast.

days.name: Dessert Day
days.about: A day for eating your favorite dessert, whether cake, pie, ice cream or anything sweet.

days.name: Developmental Language Disorder Awareness Day
days.about: An awareness day about DLD, a common but little-known condition where kids have lasting trouble learning and using language. Speech therapists, schools and families share information to help it get recognized.

days.name: Deviled Egg Day
days.about: A day for making and eating deviled eggs, hard-boiled eggs with the yolks mashed with mayonnaise and mustard and piped back in.

days.name: Dice Day
days.about: A day about dice, an ancient gaming tool. People mark it by playing board games or role-playing games that use dice.

days.name: Dictionary Day
days.about: Held on Noah Webster's birthday, it's about the value of dictionaries and building vocabulary. Teachers often have students look up and learn new words.

days.name: Different Colored Eyes Day
days.about: A day about heterochromia, the condition where a person's eyes are two different colors. People learn about it, notice it in other people and in pets like cats and dogs, and point out well-known people who have it.

days.name: Digital Learning Day
days.about: Started by the Alliance for Excellent Education to highlight good uses of technology in classrooms. Teachers and schools share digital lessons and tools.

days.name: Disability Day
days.about: A UN-backed day for promoting the rights and well-being of people with disabilities and raising awareness of the barriers they face. Groups hold talks, panel discussions and cultural events.

days.name: Disc Golf Day
days.about: A day for playing disc golf, honoring Ed Headrick, who invented the sport and the disc golf basket. Courses host events and tournaments.

days.name: Disc Jockey Day
days.about: A day honoring radio and club DJs who play and introduce music. People listen to their favorite DJs or radio shows.

days.name: Disobedience Day
days.about: A day about civil disobedience and harmless rule-breaking. People think about why it matters to stand up to unjust laws or authority through peaceful protest, or they just break out of their usual routine.

days.name: Dissociative Identity Disorder Awareness Day
days.about: An awareness day about DID, a condition involving multiple distinct identity states, usually linked to childhood trauma. People share accurate information to counter stigma and myths.

days.name: Ditch New Year’s Resolutions Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day for giving up the New Year's resolutions you've already struggled to keep, or rethinking them into something more realistic.

days.name: DIY Day
days.about: A day for doing things yourself. People make, build, craft or fix something with their own hands and pick up new practical skills.

days.name: DNA Day
days.about: Marks the publication of Watson and Crick's DNA double helix paper and the completion of the Human Genome Project. Schools and scientists hold genetics lessons and outreach events.

days.name: Do a Grouch a Favor Day
days.about: A day for doing something nice for a grumpy person in your life, in hopes of cheering them up.

days.name: Doctors’ Day
days.about: A day for thanking physicians, tied to the first use of ether anesthesia in surgery by Dr. Crawford Long. Hospitals and patients often give cards, gifts or red carnations.

days.name: Dog Day
days.about: Started by pet lifestyle expert Colleen Paige to honor dogs and encourage adopting from shelters. People spoil their dogs, post photos and donate to rescues.

days.name: Doll Day
days.about: A day for dolls and the people who collect them, whether that means getting out an old favorite, visiting a doll museum, or adding to a collection.

days.name: Dolphin Day
days.about: A day for teaching people about dolphins and the threats they face, started by the environmental group Earth Island Institute. People learn about dolphins and help protect them, for example by joining beach cleanups.

days.name: Donald Duck Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Donald Duck's first cartoon appearance, in The Wise Little Hen. Fans watch his old shorts and share his famously garbled quacking.

days.name: Donate A Day’s Wages To Charity Day
days.about: Encourages people to give one day's pay to a charity or cause they care about.

days.name: Donor Day
days.about: Raises awareness of organ, tissue, marrow, and blood donation. People sign up as donors or give blood.

days.name: Don’t Cry Over Spilled Milk Day
days.about: A reminder to let go of small mistakes and things you can't change, and to move on instead of dwelling on them.

days.name: Don’t Fry Day
days.about: Started by the National Council on Skin Cancer Prevention, at the start of summer, to remind people to protect themselves from the sun with sunscreen, shade, and covering up.

days.name: Don’t Make Your Bed Day
days.about: Gives you permission to leave your bed unmade for a day and enjoy a small break from routine.

days.name: Don’t Step On A Bee Day
days.about: A reminder to watch where you walk barefoot in summer, both to avoid getting stung and to spare the bees, which matter for pollination.

days.name: Double Cheeseburger Day
days.about: A food day for the double cheeseburger. People order or grill one with two patties and two slices of cheese.

days.name: Doughnut Day
days.about: Started by the Salvation Army to honor the women who served doughnuts to soldiers in World War I. Today shops often give out free doughnuts, and some of the proceeds go to charity.

days.name: Dr. Seuss Day
days.about: Falls on Dr. Seuss's birthday and is tied to Read Across America. Kids and schools read his books and promote reading.

days.name: Dracula Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the publication of Bram Stoker's novel Dracula. Fans read the book or watch vampire films.

days.name: Draw a Picture of a Bird Day
days.about: A day for drawing a bird. Grab paper and crayons, or sidewalk chalk, and sketch one, which is popular with kids and young bird lovers.

days.name: Drawing Day
days.about: A day for remembering how much you like making and looking at drawings. People pick up a pencil, crayon, charcoal or a tablet and draw something.

days.name: Dress in Blue Day
days.about: A colorectal cancer awareness day, promoted by the Colorectal Cancer Alliance. People wear blue to encourage screening and to support patients.

days.name: Dress Up Your Pet Day
days.about: Created by pet lifestyle expert Colleen Paige. People put costumes or outfits on their pets and share photos.

days.name: Dribble to Work Day
days.about: A basketball day tied to Selection Monday for the NCAA tournaments. People dribble a basketball on their way to work and post videos of it with #DribbleToWork.

days.name: Drink Beer Day
days.about: A day for having a beer, maybe trying a new brew or visiting a local brewery with friends.

days.name: Drink Wine Day
days.about: A day for enjoying a glass of wine, maybe opening a new bottle or sharing one with friends.

days.name: Drinking Straw Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Marvin Stone's patent for the paper drinking straw, and looks at how straws came about.
