days.name: Drive Your Studebaker Day
days.about: Owners of Studebaker cars take their vintage vehicles out for a drive to honor the defunct American automaker.

days.name: Drive-In Movie Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the first drive-in theater, which opened in Camden, New Jersey. People go see a movie at a drive-in.

days.name: Drive-Thru Day
days.about: A day about the convenience of drive-thru windows, and an excuse to grab food or coffee without leaving your car.

days.name: Dry Shampoo Day
days.about: A day started by the haircare brand Klorane to highlight dry shampoo as a quick way to freshen hair without washing it. People use it, talk about it and swap tips.

days.name: Dump The Pump Day
days.about: Promoted by the American Public Transportation Association to get people to ride public transit instead of driving and to show the savings.

days.name: Dump Your Significant Jerk Day
days.about: Encourages people in bad or disrespectful relationships to end them and move on.

days.name: Duran Duran Appreciation Day
days.about: A fan day for the British band Duran Duran. People listen to their songs and share memories of the band.

days.name: Dynamic Harmlessness Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of H. Jay Dinshah, who founded the American Vegan Society. It promotes his idea of doing the least harm and the most good to other beings, through both what you do and what you don't do.

days.name: Earmuffs Day
days.about: Honors Chester Greenwood of Maine, who patented an improved earmuff as a teenager. People wear earmuffs to mark it.

days.name: Earth Day
days.about: Started in 1970 by Senator Gaylord Nelson as a day for environmental protection. People plant trees, clean up litter, and take part in environmental events.

days.name: Earth Hour
days.about: Organized by WWF. People and landmarks around the world switch off their lights for one hour to show support for action on climate and nature.

days.name: Earth Overshoot Day
days.about: Calculated by the Global Footprint Network, it marks the point in the year when humanity has used up the natural resources the planet can renew that year. It draws attention to overconsumption.

days.name: Earth’s Rotation Day
days.about: Marks Léon Foucault's pendulum demonstration that proved the Earth rotates on its axis. It's a day to learn about that experiment and the planet's spin.

days.name: Eat A Cranberry Day
days.about: A day for eating cranberries, fresh, dried, or as sauce, around the time they're a holiday staple.

days.name: Eat a Hoagie Day
days.about: A day for eating a hoagie, the long Philadelphia-style sandwich stuffed with meats, cheese, and toppings.

days.name: Eat A Peach Day
days.about: A day for eating a fresh peach while they're in season.

days.name: Eat A Red Apple Day
days.about: A day for eating a red apple as a healthy snack.

days.name: Eat An Apple Day
days.about: Encourages people to eat an apple, a simple healthy snack.

days.name: Eat Beans Day
days.about: A day for eating beans of any kind and noticing how cheap, filling, and nutritious they are.

days.name: Eat Ice Cream For Breakfast Day
days.about: Started in the 1960s by Florence Rappaport of Rochester, New York, to cheer up her kids on a cold winter morning. People have ice cream for breakfast.

days.name: Eat What You Want Day
days.about: Created by Thomas and Ruth Roy as a day off from dieting, when you eat whatever you like without guilt.

days.name: Eat Your Vegetables Day
days.about: A reminder to get your vegetables in, maybe by trying a new one or adding more to your meals.

days.name: Education Support Professionals Day
days.about: Part of the NEA's American Education Week. It honors school staff like bus drivers, cafeteria workers, paraeducators, and custodians.

days.name: Education Technology Day
days.about: A day for recognising the digital tools used in teaching and learning, and the teachers and staff who build, support and use them in class.

days.name: Egg Day
days.about: A day for eggs. People cook them in their favorite ways and appreciate how versatile they are.

days.name: Eggnog Day
days.about: A day for drinking eggnog, the creamy holiday drink, with or without alcohol.

days.name: Eggs Benedict Day
days.about: A day for eating eggs Benedict, poached eggs and ham or bacon on an English muffin with hollandaise, usually at brunch.

days.name: Eiffel Tower Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the Eiffel Tower's completion and opening for the 1889 Paris World's Fair. A day to learn about its history.

days.name: Electronic Greetings Day
days.about: A day for sending e-cards or other electronic greetings to friends and family.

days.name: Elephant Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for learning about elephants and appreciating them, started in the 1990s by a small publishing company after the founder's daughter gave him a book of elephant pictures. People read up on elephants, visit them at zoos or sanctuaries, or support conservation groups.

days.name: Embrace Your Geekness Day
days.about: A day for owning your nerdy interests, whether that's comics, sci-fi, gaming, or obscure hobbies. People wear fandom shirts and spend time on whatever they geek out about.

days.name: Emergency Nurses Day
days.about: A day during Emergency Nurses Week, promoted by the Emergency Nurses Association, to recognize ER nurses. Hospitals and patients thank them, often with treats or notes.

days.name: Emma M Nutt Day
days.about: Honors Emma Nutt, who became the first female telephone operator in Boston in 1878. People remember her and other telephone operators and the early days of the phone.

days.name: Employee Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for employers to thank their staff, popularized by workplace-recognition author Bob Nelson. Companies often put on lunches, give small gifts, or write thank-you notes.

days.name: Employee Legal Awareness Day
days.about: A day meant to encourage workers to learn their legal rights on the job, such as wage, discrimination and safety protections. People read up on employment law or check their company policies.

days.name: Endangered Species Day
days.about: Started by a US Senate resolution and backed by conservation groups, it raises awareness of threatened plants and animals. Zoos, parks and schools run events and people support habitat protection efforts.

days.name: English Language Day
days.about: A UN language day for English, held on the traditional date of Shakespeare's birth and death. People share facts about the language, its history and its odd words.

days.name: Entrepreneurs’ Day
days.about: A day recognizing people who start businesses. In the US it was proclaimed under President Obama. People support small and local businesses and share founders' stories.

days.name: Equal Pay Day
days.about: It marks roughly how far into the year a typical woman has to work to earn what a typical man earned the previous year, to highlight the gender pay gap. Groups hold rallies and share pay-gap data.

days.name: Escapology Day
days.about: A day about escape artists like Harry Houdini, who get out of handcuffs, straitjackets, cages and other traps. People mark it by learning about famous escapes or trying escape-style puzzles.

days.name: Escargot Day
days.about: A food day for eating escargot, the cooked snails usually served in garlic butter in French cuisine. People order or try making them.

days.name: Espresso Day
days.about: A coffee day for the concentrated Italian coffee shot. People order espressos, and coffee shops often run deals.

days.name: Etch A Sketch Day
days.about: Marks the toy drawing screen with two knobs, introduced by the Ohio Art Company in 1960. People dig one out and try to draw something with it.

days.name: Euro Day
days.about: A day marking the introduction of the euro, the shared currency of the European Union, and a chance to learn about the euro's history.

days.name: Evaluate Your Life Day
days.about: A day for stepping back to look at where your life is going, what's working, and what you'd like to change. People reflect, journal or set new goals.

days.name: Event Organizers Day
days.about: A day for thanking the people and companies who plan and run events. Some people also plan a small event for someone they care about.

days.name: Executive Coaching Day
days.about: A day for recognising executive coaches, who help business leaders get better at leading and doing their jobs. People who have worked with a coach use it to thank them.

days.name: Extra Mile Day
days.about: Started by author Shawn Anderson and proclaimed by many US cities, it's about going above and beyond for others. People do something extra for someone at work or in their community.

days.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil Day
days.about: A food day for extra virgin olive oil and its health benefits. People cook with it, use it in more of their meals, and try out different oils.

days.name: Extraterrestrial Culture Day
days.about: Established by the New Mexico legislature, home of Roswell, to honor possible visitors from other worlds and the state's UFO lore. People watch alien movies, visit UFO sites or talk about life beyond Earth.

days.name: Face Your Fears Day
days.about: A day for taking on something that scares you, big or small. People try a thing they've been avoiding, like public speaking or heights.

days.name: Fair Trade Day
days.about: World Fair Trade Day, promoted by the World Fair Trade Organization, encourages buying goods from producers paid fairly and treated well. People buy fair-trade coffee, chocolate or crafts.

days.name: Fairy Day
days.about: A whimsical day for fairy folklore and make-believe, tied to midsummer traditions. Kids dress up as fairies, build fairy houses or read fairy stories.

days.name: False Confession Day
days.about: A day for harmless jokes where you tell friends, family or coworkers silly made-up 'confessions' that are obviously untrue, just to get a laugh.

days.name: False Teeth Day
days.about: A day about dentures and how much they help people who have lost their natural teeth. It's also used to remind people to look after their teeth and gums.

days.name: Family Day
days.about: A statutory holiday in several Canadian provinces, meant to give people a day off to spend with their families. People do outings or stay home together.

days.name: Fancy Rat & Mouse Day
days.about: A day for domesticated pet rats and mice, bred as fancy varieties, meant to improve their reputation as pets. Owners share photos and spoil their pets.

days.name: Farm Workers Day
days.about: A day to honor farm workers, who face many risks and hardships to grow the food we eat.

days.name: Farmworker Appreciation Day
days.about: A day to thank farmworkers for their hard physical work and their key part in getting food onto our plates. Farming communities often hold events, and groups use it to talk about worker safety and rights.

days.name: Fast Food Day
days.about: A food day for burgers, fries and other quick-service meals. People grab fast food and chains run promotions.

days.name: Fat Thursday
days.about: The last Thursday before Lent, mainly a Polish tradition, for eating rich sweets before the fasting season. People line up at bakeries for pączki and other doughnuts.

days.name: Father-in-Law Day
days.about: A day for showing your spouse's father some appreciation, often by spending time with him or taking him out.

days.name: Faux Fur Friday
days.about: Held on the day after Thanksgiving by animal-welfare advocates, it encourages wearing and buying fake fur instead of real fur. People show off faux-fur outfits.

days.name: Felt Hat Day
days.about: Marks the old fashion custom of men switching from summer straw hats to felt hats in autumn. People wear a fedora or other felt hat.

days.name: Feral Cat Day
days.about: Started by Alley Cat Allies to promote humane care of community cats, especially trap-neuter-return programs. People volunteer, donate, or help neuter local strays.

days.name: Ferret Day
days.about: A day for ferrets and their owners. People share ferret photos, learn about ferret care and pamper their pets.

days.name: Ferris Wheel Day
days.about: Held on George Ferris's birthday, it honors the wheel he built for the 1893 Chicago World's Fair. People go for a ride on one.

days.name: Festival Of Sleep Day
days.about: An early-January day for catching up on sleep after the holidays. People nap or sleep in.

days.name: Festivus
days.about: The made-up holiday from Seinfeld, the 'festival for the rest of us.' Fans put up a bare aluminum pole, air their grievances and hold 'feats of strength.'

days.name: Fibonacci Day
days.about: Picked because the date written as 11/23 echoes the start of the Fibonacci sequence (1, 1, 2, 3). Math fans talk about the sequence and where it shows up in nature.

days.name: Fibromyalgia Awareness Day
days.about: An awareness day for fibromyalgia, a chronic pain and fatigue condition. Patients and advocates share information, wear purple and raise research funds.

days.name: Fight Procrastination Day
days.about: A day for finally tackling the tasks you keep putting off. People work through their to-do list.

days.name: Filet Mignon Day
days.about: A food day for the tender beef tenderloin steak. People cook one at home or order it out.

days.name: Fill Our Staplers Day
days.about: Held right after the daylight saving time changes, as a reminder to refill staplers and restock office supplies. People top up their staplers at work.

days.name: Financial Independence Awareness Day
days.about: A day to think about how you could get to the point where your savings and investments cover your living costs, set some goals, and plan the steps to get there.

days.name: Find A Rainbow Day
days.about: A day for looking out for rainbows and enjoying them. People hunt for one after rain or make their own with a hose or prism.

days.name: Fire Prevention Day
days.about: Tied to Fire Prevention Week and the anniversary of the Great Chicago Fire, it promotes fire safety. Fire departments visit schools and people check smoke alarms and practice escape plans.

days.name: Firefighters’ Day
days.about: International Firefighters' Day, on St. Florian's feast day, honors firefighters and remembers those who died on duty. Started after Australian firefighters died in a bushfire, people wear red and blue ribbons and thank local crews.

days.name: Firefly Day
days.about: A day for fireflies, promoted by firefly conservation groups to raise awareness of their decline from habitat loss and light pollution. People watch for them at dusk and turn off outdoor lights.

days.name: Firewalk Day
days.about: A day when groups around the world hold firewalks on the same day, so people can host or join one and walk barefoot across hot coals.

days.name: First Love Day
days.about: A day for remembering your first romantic feelings, maybe by swapping first-love stories with friends or spending time with the person you love now.

days.name: Fish and Chip Day
days.about: A UK day promoted by the fish-frying trade to honour the classic takeaway. People head to their local chippy for fish and chips.

days.name: Fish Fingers and Custard Day
days.about: A Doctor Who fan day based on the Eleventh Doctor's odd favourite snack. Fans eat fish fingers dipped in custard and rewatch the show.

days.name: Flag Day
days.about: Marks the day the Continental Congress adopted the Stars and Stripes as the US flag. People fly the flag, and some towns hold parades.

days.name: Flashlight Day
days.about: Falls on about the longest night of the year, so it's a nod to the humble flashlight. People check their batteries and keep one handy for emergencies.

days.name: Flatmate’s Day
days.about: A day for thanking the people you share your home with, usually through small gestures or doing something fun together.

days.name: Flip-Flop Day
days.about: Started by Tropical Smoothie Cafe, which gives a free smoothie to people who show up in flip-flops and raises money for Camp Sunshine, a retreat for kids with serious illnesses.

days.name: Floral Design Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the art of arranging flowers. It honors Carl Rittner, who founded a floral design school in Boston. People make or buy flower arrangements, or take a floral design class.

days.name: Flossing Day
days.about: Set the day after Thanksgiving to remind people to floss after the big meal and keep up good dental habits.

days.name: For Pete’s Sake Day
days.about: A playful day about the old phrase "for Pete's sake," a polite stand-in for stronger oaths. People use the phrase all day, look up other old idioms like it, or do something nice for someone named Pete.

days.name: Ford Mustang Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the Ford Mustang's 1964 debut at the New York World's Fair. Owners and fans show off and drive their Mustangs.

days.name: Forefathers’ Day
days.about: Marks the Pilgrims' landing at Plymouth in 1620. It's observed mainly in Plymouth, Massachusetts, where the Old Colony Club holds a traditional dinner and ceremony.

days.name: Forget-me-not Day
days.about: The day before Veterans Day, for remembering soldiers who came home wounded or disabled. It started in the 1920s as a fundraiser where people sold forget-me-not flowers to help these veterans.

days.name: Forgive an Ex Day
days.about: A day for letting go of anger and resentment toward a former partner. People think back on the breakup and what they learned from it so they can move on.

days.name: Forgive Mom & Dad Day
days.about: A day for letting go of old grudges against your parents, since holding on to anger can hurt you. People think over past hurts and try to forgive their parents or make up with them.

days.name: Fortune Cookie Day
days.about: A day for the crisp folded cookie with a little paper fortune inside; people eat them, read the fortunes, or make their own at home.

days.name: Fountain Pen Day
days.about: Started by pen enthusiasts to keep fountain pens in use. People write with one, and pen shops often run deals.

days.name: Franchise Appreciation Day
days.about: Promoted by the franchise industry to recognise franchise businesses and the people who run and work at them.

days.name: Frankenstein Day
days.about: Falls on Mary Shelley's birthday and honours her novel Frankenstein. People read the book or watch the classic films.

days.name: Frappe Day
days.about: A day for the frappe, a cold, frothy blended drink usually made with coffee, milk, ice and sometimes ice cream. People make or buy one, sometimes in a new flavor.

days.name: Free Comic Book Day
days.about: An annual comics-industry event when participating comic shops hand out specially printed free comics to bring in new readers.

days.name: Free Slurpee Day
days.about: 7-Eleven's day, tied to its 7/11 name, when stores give out free small Slurpees.

days.name: Free Trade Day
days.about: Created by Dr. Tom Stevens, founder of the Objectivist Party, to get people thinking about how free trade creates wealth and raises living standards. It falls on economist Friedrich Hayek's birthday, since he argued for free trade.

days.name: Freedom Of Information Day
days.about: Held on James Madison's birthday to promote open government and the public's right to know what officials are doing.

days.name: Freethinkers Day
days.about: Tied to Thomas Paine's birthday, it honours freethought: forming beliefs through reason rather than religious authority or tradition.

days.name: French Bread Day
days.about: A day for French bread, especially the long, crusty baguette. People eat it, often dipped in soup or olive oil.

days.name: French Fried Clam Day
days.about: Another name for National Deep Fried Clams Day, which honors the deep-fried clam. That dish is credited to a man who fried clams from Massachusetts' Essex River in the same equipment he used for potato chips. People eat fried clams on the day.

days.name: French Fries Day
days.about: A day for eating French fries. Many fast-food chains give away free or discounted fries to mark it.

days.name: French Toast Day
days.about: A day for French toast, the breakfast dish made by dipping bread in egg and frying it. People make it at home or go out for it.

days.name: Fresh Breath Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of oral hygiene and what causes and prevents bad breath. Dentists use it to remind people to brush, floss and look after their mouths.

days.name: Fresh Spinach Day
days.about: A day for eating spinach fresh rather than canned or frozen, like in a salad or a smoothie.

days.name: Fresh Veggies Day
days.about: A day to get people to eat more fresh vegetables and to notice how many kinds are on offer and how nutritious they are. People try new veggies and share the day online with #FreshVeggiesDay.

days.name: Fried Chicken Day
days.about: A food day for fried chicken. People eat it at home or go to chicken chains like KFC and Church's, which often run deals on the day.

days.name: Friendship Day
days.about: A day for appreciating your friends. People call, meet up with, or send cards to the people close to them.

days.name: Fritters Day
days.about: A food day for fritters, which are fried bits of batter or dough often filled with fruit, vegetables or meat. People make their own fritters or try sweet and savory ones from different places.

days.name: Frog Jumping Day
days.about: Inspired by Mark Twain's story 'The Celebrated Jumping Frog of Calaveras County', which led to real frog-jumping contests, most famously in Calaveras County, California.

days.name: Frozen Food Day
days.about: Dates back to a 1984 proclamation by President Reagan recognising the frozen food industry. People appreciate frozen foods and the convenience they bring.

days.name: Frozen Yogurt Day
days.about: A food day for frozen yogurt. People get a cup of froyo, often from chains like Menchie's or Yogurtland, which run buy-one-get-one-free deals on the day.

days.name: Fruit Compote Day
days.about: A food day for fruit compote, which is sweetened fruit cooked on the stovetop. People make a batch to eat with biscuits, oatmeal or yogurt.

days.name: Fruitcake Day
days.about: A day after Christmas for the classic fruit-filled holiday cake, which has a lot of fans and a lot of critics. People eat leftover fruitcake or bake their own.

days.name: Fruitcake Toss Day
days.about: Comes just after the holidays as a joke about getting rid of unwanted fruitcake. Some places, like Manitou Springs, Colorado, have held contests to see who can throw one farthest.

days.name: Fudge Day
days.about: A food day for fudge, the rich, creamy sweet. People make a batch at home, or buy some from a candy shop and share it.

days.name: Fun At Work Day
days.about: A day for loosening up at the office. Coworkers take a break from routine to play games, do team activities or bring in treats, so the workplace feels friendlier.

days.name: Fun Day
days.about: A day for setting aside stress and routine work so you can relax and do something you enjoy just for the fun of it.

days.name: Fun Facts About Names Day
days.about: Part of Celebrate Your Name Week. People dig into the history, meaning and trivia behind names, including their own, and pass along the interesting facts they find.

days.name: Games Day
days.about: A day for playing games. People get out their favorite board games, card games and so on and play with friends or family.

days.name: Garage Sale Day
days.about: It's for the old tradition of the garage sale. People clear out good used stuff they don't need anymore and sell it from their garage or yard, and other people go around looking for bargains.

days.name: Garbage Man Day
days.about: Promoted by the waste industry to thank sanitation workers. People leave notes, snacks, or drinks out for their collectors.

days.name: Garden Meditation Day
days.about: It's a nudge to take some time for yourself and relax in a garden. People sit quietly or meditate outside among plants to slow down and ease stress.

days.name: Gardening Exercise Day
days.about: It's about getting the most health benefit out of gardening. People treat digging, weeding and planting as a workout and add exercise to their garden routine.

days.name: Garfield The Cat Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the first Garfield comic strip in 1978. Fans read the comics, watch the cartoons, or eat lasagna in his honor.

days.name: Garlic Day
days.about: A day for garlic lovers. People cook garlic-heavy dishes or try roasted garlic, garlic bread and the like.

days.name: Gary Gygax Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of Gary Gygax, co-creator of Dungeons & Dragons. Fans get together to play D&D and other tabletop role-playing games in his memory.

days.name: Geek Pride Day
days.about: Started in Spain in 2006 and set on the anniversary of the first Star Wars film's release. People openly enjoy their geeky interests, wear fan gear and meet up with other fans.

days.name: Genealogy Day
days.about: A day for tracing your family history. People dig into old records, ask relatives about the past, or start a family tree.

days.name: Geocaching Day
days.about: International Geocaching Day is for the GPS treasure-hunting hobby. Geocachers head out to find hidden containers and log their finds, often at organized events.

days.name: Geologists’ Day
days.about: A professional holiday from the Soviet era, still kept in Russia and other former Soviet countries, honoring geologists and people in mining and exploration. Colleagues hold gatherings and awards.

days.name: German Beer Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the 1516 Bavarian beer purity law, the Reinheitsgebot. People drink German beer and learn about German brewing.

days.name: German Butterbrot Day
days.about: Started in Germany to promote the traditional buttered bread slice, the Butterbrot. People make and share simple open sandwiches of bread and butter with toppings.

days.name: German Chocolate Cake Day
days.about: For the layered chocolate cake with coconut-pecan frosting. It's named after Sam German, who developed a baking chocolate, not after Germany. People bake or eat a slice.

days.name: Get A Different Name Day
days.about: For people who don't like their name. They try going by a different name or nickname for the day.

days.name: Get Organized Day
days.about: It's a day to take stock of your stuff. People declutter and reorganize their home or workspace, and some donate the things they don't need.

days.name: Get Out of the Doghouse Day
days.about: For making amends with someone you've upset, like a partner, friend or coworker. People apologize and do something nice to fix things.

days.name: Get Out Your Guitar Day
days.about: It's a reminder to take your guitar out of its case and play it. People dust off guitars they haven't touched in a while or start learning to play.

days.name: Get Over It Day
days.about: For letting go of grudges, breakups, mistakes or anything else you've been dwelling on. People make a point of moving on.

days.name: Get Ready Day
days.about: Run by the American Public Health Association to encourage emergency preparedness. People put together emergency kits, make family plans and stock up on supplies.

days.name: Get Smart About Credit Day
days.about: An American Bankers Association effort where bankers visit schools and community groups to teach young people about credit and managing money.

days.name: Ginger Cat Appreciation Day
days.about: For orange tabby cats. Owners give their ginger cats extra attention and share photos of them.

days.name: Gingerbread Decorating Day
days.about: A day for decorating gingerbread, mostly gingerbread cookies and houses. People ice them and add candy and other toppings, often as a family holiday activity.

days.name: Gingerbread House Day
days.about: For building and decorating gingerbread houses with icing and candy, a holiday tradition for families and in competitions.

days.name: Gingersnap Day
days.about: For the crisp, spiced ginger cookie. People bake or eat gingersnaps.

days.name: Girl Friends Day
days.about: For appreciating your female friends. Women get together, call old friends, or do something fun with their close girlfriends.

days.name: Girl Scout Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the Girl Scouts by Juliette Gordon Low in 1912. Scouts wear their uniforms, do service projects and hold events.

days.name: GIS Day
days.about: Started by the mapping software company Esri to show what geographic information systems can do. Schools, agencies and universities hold mapping demos and open houses.

days.name: Giving Tuesday
days.about: The Tuesday after Thanksgiving, started in 2012 as a giving-focused answer to Black Friday and Cyber Monday. People donate to charities and volunteer.

days.name: Global Accessibility Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness of digital access for people with disabilities. Developers and designers test sites and apps with screen readers and keyboard-only navigation, and organizations hold talks.

days.name: Global Beatles Day
days.about: Held on the anniversary of the 1967 'Our World' broadcast where the Beatles premiered 'All You Need Is Love.' Fans listen to Beatles music and remember the band's message of peace.

days.name: Global Community Engagement Day
days.about: A day to encourage people, groups and businesses to get more involved in their local communities. People volunteer, join local efforts and look for ways to work with their neighbors. It was started by the organization Engage 2 Act.

days.name: Global Dignity Day
days.about: Co-founded by Crown Prince Haakon of Norway. Volunteers run workshops in schools around the world where students talk about dignity and respect for every person.

days.name: Global Forgiveness Day
days.about: A day for practicing forgiveness. People make peace with someone, accept an apology or let go of anger they've been holding onto.

days.name: Global Handwashing Day
days.about: Promotes washing hands with soap to prevent disease, especially in places where infections spread easily. Schools and health groups run demonstrations and campaigns.

days.name: Global Love Day
days.about: Promoted by The Love Foundation as a day of unconditional love toward everyone. People do kind acts and try to treat others with compassion.

days.name: Global Talent Acquisition Day
days.about: A day that recognizes recruiters, sourcers and other talent acquisition professionals who find and hire the people organizations depend on. Companies use it to thank their recruiting teams.

days.name: Go Barefoot Day
days.about: Started by the nonprofit Soles4Souls, this day is for going without shoes for a while to think about people who don't have any. It encourages people to donate new and used shoes to people in need, such as victims of natural disasters.

days.name: Go Birding Day
days.about: A day to get outside and watch birds, whether you head to a park or nature spot or just look around your own backyard.

days.name: Go Caroling Day
days.about: For singing Christmas carols, often by going door to door or to nursing homes in groups.

days.name: Go Cook For Your Pets Day
days.about: Started by a pet nutrition author to encourage making homemade, healthy food or treats for your dog or cat.

days.name: Go Fishing Day
days.about: A push to get outdoors and go fishing, alone or with family and friends.

days.name: Go For A Ride Day
days.about: A day for going on a ride just for the fun of it, by car, bike, train or anything else. The idea is to slow down and enjoy the trip without needing a destination.

days.name: Go For Broke Day
days.about: Honors the Japanese American soldiers of the 442nd Regimental Combat Team in World War II, whose motto was 'Go for Broke.' People remember their service and the discrimination they faced at home.

days.name: Go Skateboarding Day
days.about: Started in 2004 by the International Association of Skateboard Companies. Skaters go out and ride, and skate shops hold group sessions and events.

days.name: Goats Cheese Day
days.about: A food day for goat cheese, also called chèvre. People eat it or cook with it, and some use the day to appreciate the farmers who produce the goat milk it's made from.

days.name: Gobstopper Day
days.about: A day for gobstoppers, the hard, layered jawbreaker candy made famous by Roald Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. People spend it eating them.

days.name: Golden Retriever Day
days.about: For the golden retriever breed. Owners spoil their dogs and share photos of them.

days.name: Golf Day
days.about: A day for golf lovers to go out and play a round. It grew out of a charity golf event the PGA has held every year since 1952.

days.name: Golfer’s Day
days.about: A day for golf fans of every level, from beginners to pros, to enjoy the game. People head out for a casual round, play in tournaments or watch golf on TV.

days.name: Good Hair Day
days.about: A day about hair care and how healthy, well-kept hair can boost your confidence. People treat themselves to a nice hairstyle, and some salons run hair-care and styling workshops.

days.name: Good Neighbor Day
days.about: Started by Becky Mattson of Montana and proclaimed nationally by President Carter in 1978. People get to know their neighbors and do something kind for them.

days.name: Goof Off Day
days.about: A day for slacking off and doing something silly or unproductive instead of working.

days.name: Gorgeous Grandma Day
days.about: A day for recognizing grandmothers as vibrant, active, and attractive people. People compliment, visit, or spoil the grandmothers in their lives.

days.name: Gorilla Suit Day
days.about: A goofy day started by Mad magazine cartoonist Don Martin, for putting on a gorilla suit and going about your day in it.

days.name: Goth Day
days.about: A day started by UK radio DJs to celebrate goth music and subculture. Goths and fans dress up, play goth music, and go to events.

days.name: Grammar Day
days.about: A day for promoting good grammar and correct language use. People share grammar tips, puzzles, and gentle corrections.

days.name: Grand Marnier Day
days.about: A day for enjoying Grand Marnier, the French orange-and-cognac liqueur. People sip it straight or use it in cocktails, crêpes Suzette, and desserts.

days.name: Grandparent’s Day
days.about: A day for honoring grandparents and their place in the family. People visit or call them, send cards, and spend time together.

days.name: Granola Bar Day
days.about: A food day for eating granola bars, whether store-bought or homemade.

days.name: Greasy Food Day
days.about: A day for giving yourself permission to eat fried, greasy comfort food like fries, burgers, and onion rings.

days.name: Great American Pizza Bake
days.about: A week for making pizza at home instead of ordering it. People bake their own and choose their own toppings, such as vegetables, lean meat and whole-grain crust.

days.name: Greenpeace Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the environmental group Greenpeace, which began with a 1971 protest voyage against nuclear testing. People learn about environmental causes and support conservation.

days.name: Grenache Day
days.about: A wine day for drinking and learning about Grenache, one of the most widely planted red grapes. Wineries and wine lovers hold tastings.

days.name: Grief Awareness Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of grief and the different ways people go through loss. It encourages people to talk about it openly and support those who are grieving.

days.name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich Day
days.about: A food day for making and eating grilled cheese sandwiches, from the classic version to fancier ones.

days.name: Groundhog day
days.about: The traditional day when a groundhog, most famously Punxsutawney Phil in Pennsylvania, supposedly predicts whether winter will last six more weeks by whether it sees its shadow. Crowds gather to watch.

days.name: Gryffindor Pride Day
days.about: A day for Harry Potter fans in Gryffindor house to show house pride. They wear red and gold and celebrate the house's bravery.

days.name: Guacamole Day
days.about: A food day for making and eating guacamole, the mashed avocado dip.

days.name: Guide Dogs Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the work of guide dogs that help blind and visually impaired people. It also honors the organizations and trainers who raise them.

days.name: Guinea Pig Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for appreciating guinea pigs as pets. Owners give them treats and attention, and people learn about caring for them or adopting one.

days.name: Gumdrop Day
days.about: A candy day for eating gumdrops, the small sugar-coated gummy candies, or using them to decorate treats.

days.name: Gummi Worm Day
days.about: A candy day for eating gummy worms.

days.name: Gunpowder Day
days.about: Another name for Guy Fawkes Night. It marks the failure of the 1605 Gunpowder Plot to blow up the English Parliament and kill King James I. People light bonfires, watch fireworks and read up on the history.

days.name: Gymnastics Day
days.about: A day for promoting gymnastics and fitness, backed by USA Gymnastics. Gyms hold open houses, demonstrations, and fundraisers.

days.name: Hagfish Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the slimy, odd-looking hagfish. It uses an 'ugly' animal to get people interested in ocean conservation.

days.name: Haiku Poetry Day
days.about: A day for reading and writing haiku, the short three-line poetic form from Japan.

days.name: Hairball Awareness Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of hairballs in cats. Owners learn how brushing, diet, and vet care can prevent them.

days.name: Hamburger Day
days.about: A food day for grilling and eating hamburgers.

days.name: Hammock Day
days.about: A day for relaxing in a hammock and taking it easy.

days.name: Hamster Day
days.about: A day for appreciating hamsters as pets. Owners give them extra attention, and people learn about caring for them.

days.name: Handbag Day
days.about: A day for appreciating handbags, whether that's using a favorite purse, buying a new one, or cleaning out the one you carry.

days.name: Handcuff Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of George A. Carney's patent for modern swing-through handcuffs, a design that helped standardize the handcuffs police use today. People learn about the history of handcuffs, and collectors show off antique pairs.

days.name: Handwriting Day
days.about: Held on John Hancock's birthday, a day for writing by hand: letters, journals, and notes instead of typing.

days.name: Hanging Out Day
days.about: Not about socializing: it's a day for hanging laundry outside on a clothesline to dry. The point is to save energy.

days.name: Happiness Happens Day
days.about: A day from the Secret Society of Happy People for noticing and sharing the things that make you happy.

days.name: Happy Heart Hugs Day
days.about: A day for hugging and cuddling the people you love, including your pets, and telling them how much you care about them.

days.name: Happy Hour Day
days.about: A day for going out to happy hour, the after-work stretch when bars offer cheap drinks and snacks. The term is said to have started with sailors in the US Navy.

days.name: Happy Mew Year Day For Cats
days.about: A day created by Thomas and Ruth Roy for making New Year's resolutions on behalf of your cat. That can mean better care, a healthier diet, or more playtime.

days.name: Harlem Globetrotter’s Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the Harlem Globetrotters' first game in 1927. It honors the exhibition basketball team known for trick shots and comedy.

days.name: Harvey Milk Day
days.about: A day honoring Harvey Milk, one of the first openly gay elected officials in the US, held on his birthday. Schools and communities, especially in California, remember his work for gay rights.

days.name: Harvey Wallbanger Day
days.about: A day for mixing and drinking a Harvey Wallbanger, the vodka, orange juice, and Galliano cocktail popular in the 1970s.

days.name: Hat Day
days.about: A day for wearing your favorite hat, or a silly one.

days.name: Haunted Refrigerator Night
days.about: A joke observance the night before Halloween about the forgotten leftovers going bad at the back of the fridge. People dig out the old containers and clean out the fridge.

days.name: Have A Bad Day Day
days.about: A joke day from Thomas and Ruth Roy for people tired of hearing 'have a nice day.' You tell everyone to have a bad day instead.

days.name: Have a Bagel Day
days.about: A food day for eating bagels with your favorite toppings.

days.name: Have a Party with Your Bear Day
days.about: A day for throwing a party or picnic with your teddy bear. It's mostly for kids, though adults who still have a bear join in too.

days.name: Healthy Fats Day
days.about: The Healthy Fats Coalition started this day to get people talking about cooking with traditional animal fats like beef tallow, lard, duck fat and goose fat. Others also use it to point out that fats like those in olive oil, nuts and avocados are good for you.

days.name: Hedgehog Day
days.about: A day for appreciating hedgehogs. It's held on the same day as Groundhog Day, a nod to European weather lore that used hedgehogs before groundhogs.

days.name: Help A Horse Day
days.about: A day started by the ASPCA to support horse rescues and shelters. People donate, volunteer, or learn about horse welfare.

days.name: Heritage Treasures Day
days.about: A day for sharing your heritage and helping to protect famous landmarks, monuments and wildlife. People look through old photos and family history, visit historic sites or give money to groups that look after monuments.

days.name: High Five Day
days.about: A day started by University of Virginia students in 2002 for giving high-fives to friends and strangers. It's sometimes tied to fundraising.

days.name: Hippo Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness about hippos and the threats they face, like habitat loss and poaching. People share hippo facts and support conservation groups.

days.name: HIV Long-Term Survivors Day
days.about: A day honoring people who have lived with HIV for many years, especially those diagnosed before effective treatment existed. It was started by survivor activists and is marked with gatherings, stories and attention to survivors' ongoing needs.

days.name: Hoagie Day
days.about: A day for eating hoagies, the long sandwiches on Italian rolls closely tied to Philadelphia.

days.name: Hobbit Day
days.about: A day for Tolkien fans, falling on the shared birthday of Bilbo and Frodo Baggins. Fans throw hobbit-style parties, go barefoot, eat a lot and reread the books.

days.name: Holistic Pet Day
days.about: A day for looking at pet health as a whole, including diet, exercise and natural or alternative care alongside regular vet visits.

days.name: Holistic Therapy Day
days.about: A day about holistic therapies, which treat mind, body and spirit together, and about looking after your physical, emotional and social wellbeing.

days.name: Homeless Animals Day
days.about: A day for drawing attention to stray and shelter animals and the need to spay, neuter and adopt. Animal groups hold candlelight vigils and adoption events.

days.name: Homemade Bread Day
days.about: A day for baking your own bread from scratch.

days.name: Homemade Soup Day
days.about: A day for making a pot of soup from scratch, often to share with family or neighbors.

days.name: Honesty Day
days.about: A day for being truthful, created as a counterpoint to April Fools' Day. People are encouraged to speak honestly and to recognize honest people.

days.name: Hop A Park Day
days.about: A nudge to get out of the house and visit your local parks, whether that means taking a walk, having a picnic or just spending time in a public green space.

days.name: Horse Protection Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of horse neglect and abuse and encouraging people to support or adopt from horse rescues.

days.name: Horse Rescue Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of horses that have been neglected or abused. People support rescue groups by visiting, volunteering at or donating to a local horse rescue.

days.name: Hospital Admitting Clerks Day
days.about: A day to thank hospital admitting and registration staff, who are often the first people patients deal with and who take down the information needed for their care.

days.name: Hospitality Workers in HealthCare Day
days.about: A day to recognize the non-clinical staff in hospitals, care homes and other medical facilities, such as kitchen teams, cleaners, porters and laundry workers. Hospitals often use it to publicly thank these teams.

days.name: Hot Air Balloon Day
days.about: A day marking the Montgolfier brothers' first public hot air balloon flight. Some people take a balloon ride or watch balloon launches.

days.name: Hot Cocoa Day
days.about: A day for drinking a mug of hot chocolate.

days.name: Hot Cross Bun Day
days.about: Good Friday, when people traditionally eat spiced, cross-topped hot cross buns.

days.name: Hot Dog Day
days.about: A summer day for eating hot dogs, promoted by the hot dog and sausage industry. Some places run hot dog deals and events.

days.name: Hot Fudge Sundae Day
days.about: A day for eating ice cream topped with hot fudge sauce.

days.name: Hot Mulled Cider Day
days.about: A day for warming apple cider with spices like cinnamon and cloves and drinking it.

days.name: Hot Pastrami Sandwich Day
days.about: A day for eating hot pastrami sandwiches, the deli classic often served on rye.

days.name: Hot Sauce Day
days.about: A day for hot sauce fans to try different sauces and add some heat to their food.

days.name: Hot Toddy Day
days.about: A day for making a hot toddy, the warm drink of whiskey, hot water, honey and lemon.

days.name: Houseplant Appreciation Day
days.about: A winter day for paying attention to your indoor plants by watering, repotting or adding a new one.

days.name: Housewife’s Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the work of homemakers who run a household.

days.name: Housing Day
days.about: A grassroots campaign where tenants, housing associations, local councils and advocates highlight the good that social housing does and make the case for secure, affordable homes for everyone.

days.name: Howl At The Moon Day
days.about: A night for wolves, coming shortly before Halloween: people go outside and howl at the moon, often with friends, and some groups use it to teach about wolves and how to protect them.

days.name: Hufflepuff Pride Day
days.about: A Harry Potter fan day for showing pride in Hufflepuff house and its values of loyalty, fairness and hard work. Fans wear yellow and black.

days.name: Hug A Bear Day
days.about: A day for hugging your teddy bear, not a wild one. People take out their own teddy bear for a squeeze, or borrow a friend's.

days.name: Hug A Drummer Day
days.about: A day to show some appreciation for drummers, who keep the beat in a band but often get overlooked. People hug a drummer they know or learn about great rock and jazz drummers.

days.name: Hug A Greeting Card Writer Day
days.about: A day to recognize the mostly anonymous people who write the verses and messages in greeting cards. Some people try writing or making their own cards.

days.name: Hug A Plumber Day
days.about: A day to thank plumbers for the hard and often unpleasant work of keeping our plumbing clean and working. People hug a plumber they know, after asking first, or thank one on social media.

days.name: Hug A Shed And Take A Selfie
days.about: A day tied to the UK shed-enthusiast community, where people hug their garden shed, photograph it and share the picture online.

days.name: Hug A Sheep Day
days.about: A day for appreciating sheep and what they give us, like wool. People go and hug a real sheep at a farm or sanctuary, or hug one in a symbolic way.

days.name: Hug a Vegetarian Day
days.about: A day promoted by PETA for showing appreciation to vegetarians. People give vegetarians a hug, join meetups and share animal pictures to spread the word about eating meat-free.

days.name: Hug an Australian Day
days.about: A light-hearted day about Australian culture and friendliness. People hug the Australians they know, or do something typically Aussie, like baking an Australian pie.

days.name: Hug Your Boss Day
days.about: A day for showing your boss you appreciate them and for building better relationships at work. It was started by the job site TipTopJob, and the hug can be real or just a gesture of thanks.

days.name: Hug Your Cat Day
days.about: A day for giving your cat extra affection, if it will tolerate a hug.

days.name: Hug Your Hound Day
days.about: A day for spending time with your dog and appreciating it, started by a dog behavior author. People take their dogs out and give them extra attention.

days.name: Hugging Day
days.about: A day for hugging family and friends, started in the 1980s by a Michigan man who thought people didn't show affection enough in public. People are encouraged to ask before hugging.

days.name: Human Resource Professional Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the work HR teams do, like hiring, onboarding, training and handling benefits. Workplaces thank their HR staff, and HR people are encouraged to spend time on their own professional development.

days.name: Human Rights Day
days.about: A UN day marking the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948. Governments, schools and activists hold events about human rights.

days.name: Humanitarian Day
days.about: A UN day honoring aid workers, especially those killed or injured while helping others. It marks the anniversary of the 2003 bombing of the UN headquarters in Baghdad.

days.name: Humbug Day
days.about: A day in the busy pre-Christmas season for letting out holiday stress and grumbling like Scrooge, so you can move on.

days.name: Humiliation Day
days.about: A day to practice humility, look inward and be grateful for what you have. People also think about the harm that humiliating others causes and make a point of treating others with respect.

days.name: Husband Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for wives and partners to show their husbands some appreciation.

days.name: Hypnotism Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of hypnosis and hypnotherapy and clearing up misconceptions about them. Hypnotists often offer demonstrations or free sessions.

days.name: I Forgot Day
days.about: A day for catching up on things you forgot, like a missed birthday, call or thank-you.

days.name: I Hate Coriander Day
days.about: A day for people who can't stand coriander, or cilantro, which tastes like soap to some people. They share their dislike online.

days.name: I Love to Write Day
days.about: A grassroots day started by writer John Riddle in 2002 to get people of all ages to spend some time writing. Schools, churches and community groups hold writing activities.

days.name: I Love Yarn Day
days.about: Promoted by the Craft Yarn Council to share yarn crafts. People knit, crochet, show off their projects or teach someone else.

days.name: I Need A Patch For That Day
days.about: A day for patches of all kinds, from fabric patches on clothes and quilts to eye patches. People fix things that need patching or share photos of their patches.

days.name: Ice Cream Cone Day
days.about: A day for eating ice cream in a cone, nodding to the cone's popularization around the early 1900s.

days.name: Ice Cream Day
days.about: National Ice Cream Day, proclaimed by Ronald Reagan in 1984. People go out for ice cream and shops often run deals.

days.name: Ice Cream For Breakfast Day
days.about: Started in the 1960s by a Rochester mom, Florence Rappaport, to cheer up her kids on a snowy winter day. People eat ice cream for breakfast, and some use it to raise money for charity.

days.name: Ice Cream Sandwich Day
days.about: A day for eating ice cream sandwiches, the ice cream pressed between two cookies or wafers.

days.name: Ice Cream Soda Day
days.about: Marks the ice cream soda, credited to Robert Green in 1874. People order or make one: ice cream dropped into soda water and syrup.

days.name: Iced Tea Day
days.about: A summer day for drinking iced tea, sweet or unsweet.

days.name: Iguana Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness of iguanas, many of them threatened in the wild, and supports conservation groups that protect them.

days.name: Improve Your Office Day
days.about: A day for making your workspace nicer to be in, whether that means clearing clutter, adding flowers or art, or upgrading your chair, keyboard or filing system.

days.name: Inane Answering Message Day
days.about: A day to listen to your voicemail greeting and replace it if it's silly or annoying.

days.name: Inconvenience Yourself Day
days.about: A day for putting yourself out a little so someone else's day goes more smoothly, like holding a door, letting someone go ahead of you, or calling a friend instead of texting.

days.name: Independence From Meat Day
days.about: It falls on the US Independence Day and is about skipping meat and getting your protein from plants instead, for example by grilling plant-based food at the barbecue.

days.name: Independent Bookstore Day
days.about: A spring Saturday when independent bookstores hold events, sell exclusive items and invite people to shop locally. It started in California in 2014.

days.name: India Pale Ale Day
days.about: Started online in 2011 as a day for drinking and talking about IPAs. Breweries and bars often feature them.

days.name: Indian Pudding Day
days.about: For the old New England dessert of cornmeal baked slowly with milk and molasses, often served warm with ice cream.

days.name: Indianapolis 500
days.about: Not an observance but the famous 500-mile car race at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, held every Memorial Day weekend. People watch it, throw parties, or go to the track.

days.name: Indigenous Peoples Day
days.about: Held in many places instead of, or alongside, Columbus Day to honor Native American history and cultures. There are events, gatherings and educational programs.

days.name: Individual Rights Day
days.about: It falls on philosopher John Locke's birthday and is a day to think about the basic rights each person has, and to stand up for them.

days.name: Industrial Workers Of The World Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the IWW labor union in Chicago in 1905. Labor activists remember its history and organizing.

days.name: Information Overload Day
days.about: Started by information-overload researchers to get people thinking about how much email and messaging overwhelms them, and about cutting back.

days.name: Ingersoll Day
days.about: Marks the birthday of Robert Ingersoll, the 19th-century orator and freethinker. Freethought groups read his speeches and discuss his ideas.

days.name: Innovation Day
days.about: Also called National Innovation Day, it's for encouraging young people to be creative and come up with new ideas and inventions, though anyone can join in.

days.name: Insect Repellent Awareness Day
days.about: A health reminder to use insect repellent, since bites can spread serious diseases. People put on repellent before going outside and take other steps to avoid bites, like getting rid of standing water.

days.name: Inspire Your Heart With Art Day
days.about: A day to look at, make or think about art and how it affects you, by visiting a museum, for example.

days.name: Insurance Awareness Day
days.about: A reminder to review your insurance policies and make sure your coverage still fits your needs.

days.name: Insurance Nerd Day
days.about: Started by Pioneer Mutual Insurance Company in 2016 to recognize people who work in insurance and show that the industry isn't boring. Insurance companies use it to thank their staff and share facts about why insurance matters.

days.name: Intern Day
days.about: National Intern Day, started by the job site WayUp, recognizes interns and what they contribute. Employers often thank their interns or host events.

days.name: International Anti-Corruption Day
days.about: A UN day to raise awareness of corruption and how to fight it.

days.name: International Artist Day
days.about: Started in 2004 by painter Chris MacClure, on Picasso's birthday, to recognize artists and their work.

days.name: International Ask a Question Day
days.about: A day for asking questions, especially ones you might be too nervous to ask, as a way to learn and stay curious. It falls on Albert Einstein's birthday, and teachers often use it to get students asking questions.

days.name: International Astronomy Day
days.about: Started in 1973 by Doug Berger, an astronomy club leader, to bring astronomy to the public. Clubs and observatories hold stargazing and telescope events.

days.name: International Axe Throwing Day
days.about: Created by the World Axe Throwing League to promote the sport of urban axe throwing. Member venues offer free axe throwing so anyone can try it.

days.name: International Bagpipe Day
days.about: Organized by bagpipe enthusiasts to showcase the many kinds of bagpipes around the world. Pipers perform and share their music.

days.name: International Bat Night
days.about: Coordinated by European bat conservation groups. People join evening bat walks and talks to learn about bats and help protect them.

days.name: International Bath Day
days.about: A day about baths as a way to relax and take care of yourself. People take a long bath, and parents may make bath time fun and educational for their kids.

days.name: International Beer Day
days.about: Started in 2007 in Santa Cruz, California. Friends get together to drink beer and thank the people who brew and serve it.

days.name: International Body Piercing Day
days.about: Started by a friend of piercing pioneer Jim Ward, who opened the first professional piercing studio, to mark his birthday. It's used to raise awareness of piercing culture and to teach people about safety standards in the piercing industry.

days.name: International Book Giving Day
days.about: Started by Amy Broadmoore to get books into children's hands. People give books to kids or donate them to libraries and charities.

days.name: International Bow Day
days.about: Started by the accessories retailer Claire's for the bow as a fashion accessory. People wear their favorite bows in their hair or on other accessories and share photos on social media.

days.name: International Cat Day
days.about: Started in 2002 by the International Fund for Animal Welfare to raise awareness of cats and their welfare. People fuss over their cats or support shelters.

days.name: International Cheetah Day
days.about: Started by Dr. Laurie Marker of the Cheetah Conservation Fund to raise awareness of the endangered cheetah and support efforts to save it.

days.name: International Chef Day
days.about: Started by chef Bill Gallagher and the World Association of Chefs' Societies. Chefs are recognized and often teach children about healthy eating.

days.name: International Chernobyl Disaster Remembrance Day
days.about: A UN-designated day to remember the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear accident and its victims, and to think about its lasting effects.

days.name: International Chess Day
days.about: Marks the founding of FIDE, the world chess federation, in 1924. People play chess and clubs hold tournaments.

days.name: International Chicken Wing Day
days.about: A day for chicken wings, the bar snack that came out of Buffalo and is now eaten all over the world. People eat wings in all kinds of sauces and dry rubs.

days.name: International Childfree Day
days.about: Recognizes people who choose not to have children. It grew out of Non-Parents' Day, started in the 1970s.

days.name: International Civil Aviation Day
days.about: A UN day backed by the International Civil Aviation Organization, recognizing the importance of air travel for connecting the world.

days.name: International Clouded Leopard Day
days.about: Raises awareness of the clouded leopard, a threatened wild cat of Southeast Asia, and supports work to protect it.

days.name: International Coffee Day
days.about: A day promoted by the International Coffee Organization to recognize coffee and the farmers who grow it, often with attention to fair trade. Many cafés offer free or discounted cups.

days.name: International Country Music Day
days.about: A day for country music, held on Hank Williams' birthday. Country music festivals, live shows and dance events take place in various places around the world.

days.name: International Dance Day
days.about: Started by UNESCO's International Theatre Institute on the birthday of ballet reformer Jean-Georges Noverre, to draw attention to dance as an art form. People put on performances, workshops and open classes.

days.name: International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the World Health Organization removing homosexuality from its list of mental disorders. People use it to raise awareness of discrimination against LGBTQ people, with events and campaigns.

days.name: International Day for Biological Diversity
days.about: A UN day for raising awareness of biodiversity and the threats to it. Schools, governments and conservation groups hold events and campaigns.

days.name: International Day for the Eradication of Poverty
days.about: A UN day for drawing attention to poverty and the people living in it. Organizations hold events and push for anti-poverty action.

days.name: International Day for Tolerance
days.about: A UNESCO-backed UN day for promoting tolerance and respect between cultures and peoples, mostly marked with educational events.

days.name: International Day of Charity
days.about: A UN day set on the anniversary of Mother Teresa's death, to encourage charitable giving and volunteering.

days.name: International Day of Forests
days.about: A UN day for raising awareness of forests and their importance. People plant trees and hold forest-related events.

days.name: International Day of Friendship
days.about: A UN day promoting friendship between people, cultures and countries as a way to build peace. Many people also use it to reach out to their own friends.

days.name: International Day of Happiness
days.about: A UN day recognizing happiness and well-being as goals worth pursuing. It is often tied to the release of the World Happiness Report and to small acts of kindness.

days.name: International Day of Medical Transporters
days.about: A day to thank ambulance drivers and other medical transporters, who make sure patients get safely to where they can receive care.

days.name: International Day of Non-Violence
days.about: A UN day held on Gandhi's birthday to promote non-violence through education and public awareness.

days.name: International Day of Peace
days.about: A UN day devoted to strengthening peace, including a call for a 24-hour global ceasefire. It is marked with a minute of silence, peace bell ceremonies and community events.

days.name: International Day of Sign Languages
days.about: A UN day, pushed for by the World Federation of the Deaf, to raise awareness of sign languages and the rights of deaf people who use them.

days.name: International Day of the Girl Child
days.about: A UN day focused on the rights of girls and the challenges they face, such as education gaps and child marriage. Groups run campaigns and events about girls' empowerment.

days.name: International Day of Veterinary Medicine
days.about: A day for recognizing and thanking veterinarians, vet teams and animal-health researchers around the world for the care they give animals. People often thank their own vet or support veterinary charities.

days.name: International Dog Biscuit Appreciation Day
days.about: A lighthearted day for giving your dog a biscuit or other treat, and sometimes for baking homemade ones.

days.name: International Dot Day
days.about: Inspired by Peter H. Reynolds' children's book 'The Dot', it encourages creativity and courage, especially among kids. Classrooms make dot-themed art and read the book.

days.name: International Falafel Day
days.about: A food day for eating falafel, the fried chickpea or fava bean balls popular across the Middle East.

days.name: International Fanny Pack Day
days.about: A lighthearted day for the fanny pack, or hip bag, the 1980s accessory that has come back into fashion. People wear one or share photos of theirs.

days.name: International FND Awareness Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of Functional Neurological Disorder, a condition affecting how the brain sends and receives signals. Patients and advocacy groups share information and light buildings in the cause's colors.

days.name: International Fragrance Day
days.about: A day about perfume and other scents, and about our sense of smell. People wear or try a favorite fragrance, or learn how perfumes are made.

days.name: International Gin and Tonic Day
days.about: A day for the classic gin and tonic, started in memory of a gin lover named Mary Edith Keyburn. People mix and drink a G&T, sometimes trying a new gin or garnish.

days.name: International Happy Gose Day
days.about: A beer day for Gose, a salty, sour German wheat beer style tied to Goslar and Leipzig. Craft breweries and beer fans drink and promote it.

days.name: International Hot and Spicy Food Day
days.about: A food day for eating hot, spicy dishes and peppers, sometimes with chili-eating challenges.

days.name: International Hummus Day
days.about: Started in 2012 by Ronen Lev as a day for eating and sharing hummus, the chickpea and tahini dip.

days.name: International Irish Whiskey Day
days.about: A day about the history and craft of Irish whiskey. Fans have a glass of it or learn more about how it's made.

days.name: International Jazz Day
days.about: Created by UNESCO, with pianist Herbie Hancock as a champion, to recognize jazz and its role in bringing people together. Concerts and educational events are held worldwide.

days.name: International Kissing Day
days.about: A day that started in the UK for kissing someone you love and appreciating the simple pleasure of a kiss.

days.name: International Kite Day
days.about: Coincides with the Makar Sankranti/Uttarayan festival in India, especially Gujarat, where people spend the day flying kites, often in friendly kite-fighting battles.

days.name: International Lefthanders Day
days.about: Started in 1976 by Dean Campbell of Lefthanders International to raise awareness of left-handed people and the inconveniences of a right-handed world.

days.name: International Lego Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the Lego brick's 1958 patent. Fans build with Lego and share their creations.

days.name: International Marconi Day
days.about: An amateur radio event honoring radio pioneer Guglielmo Marconi, held around his birthday. Ham operators try to contact special stations set up at sites linked to Marconi.

days.name: International Men’s Day
days.about: Started by Jerome Teelucksingh in Trinidad and Tobago in 1999. It focuses on men's health and wellbeing and on positive male role models.

days.name: International Midwives’ Day
days.about: Promoted by the International Confederation of Midwives to recognize midwives and their role in caring for mothers and babies.

days.name: International Migrants Day
days.about: A UN day recognizing migrants' contributions and drawing attention to their rights and the challenges they face.

days.name: International Mother Language Day
days.about: A UNESCO day promoting linguistic diversity and mother-tongue education. It grew out of Bangladesh's Language Movement, which commemorates students killed in 1952 while defending Bengali.

days.name: International Mud Day
days.about: A day for letting kids play in the mud, encouraging outdoor, messy play. It started as a link between children in Nepal and Australia.

days.name: International Ninja Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day started in 2003 by the parody site Ninja Burger, all about ninjas. People dress up as ninjas, watch ninja movies or documentaries, learn a bit of real ninja history, or try a martial arts class.

days.name: International Nurses Day
days.about: Held on Florence Nightingale's birthday and promoted by the International Council of Nurses to recognize nurses' contributions to health care.

days.name: International Orangutan Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of endangered orangutans and the destruction of their rainforest habitat, often with fundraising for conservation groups.

days.name: International Panic Day
days.about: A lighthearted day for getting your worries and panics off your chest. People say out loud or share what's stressing them out, or put it into something like art, and talk it over with friends and family.

days.name: International Picnic Day
days.about: A day for eating outdoors. People pack a basket with food and drinks, grab a blanket, and have a picnic outside, often with friends or family.

days.name: International Plastic Bag Free Day
days.about: A campaign day, started in Spain and backed by Zero Waste Europe, encouraging people to stop using single-use plastic bags and switch to reusable ones.

days.name: International Podcast Day
days.about: A day for promoting podcasts and podcasters, with live events and people sharing shows they like.

days.name: International Podiatry Day
days.about: An awareness day for foot health and the podiatrists who treat foot and ankle problems. Podiatrists and clinics use it to share foot-care advice and get people thinking about looking after their feet.

days.name: International Poke Day
days.about: A day for poke (said 'poh-kay'), the Hawaiian dish of diced raw fish such as tuna, often served over rice. People go out for a poke bowl or make one at home.

days.name: International Read To Me Day
days.about: A campaign day for kids' literacy. Children are encouraged to remind and ask the adults in their lives, like parents, grandparents and siblings, to read to them.

days.name: International Red Panda Day
days.about: Started by the Red Panda Network to raise awareness of endangered red pandas. Zoos and conservation groups hold events and raise funds.

days.name: International Reggae Day
days.about: A day for reggae music and Jamaican culture, started in Kingston in the 1990s. People hold concerts, play reggae on the radio, and talk about the music's history and influence.

days.name: International Rock Day
days.about: A day about actual rocks, minerals and geology, not rock music. People learn about different kinds of rocks, go rock collecting or hiking, and swap rock-hunting stories.

days.name: International Safety Pin Day
days.about: Marks the patenting of the safety pin by Walter Hunt in 1849. People appreciate the humble pin and sometimes use it in crafts or fashion.

days.name: International Sailor Moon Day
days.about: Fans of the anime and manga Sailor Moon mark the birthday of its heroine, Usagi Tsukino. They rewatch the show, cosplay, and share fan art.

days.name: International Scrapbooking Industry Day
days.about: A day to recognize the scrapbooking industry, which makes the supplies people use to arrange and preserve photos and family memories. People spend it working on scrapbooks.

days.name: International Sloth Day
days.about: Raises awareness of sloths and the threats to their rainforest habitat. It was started by a Colombian conservation group, and people learn about sloths or donate to sanctuaries.

days.name: International Strange Music Day
days.about: A day for listening to music that's unusual or unfamiliar to you. People seek out odd genres, instruments, or experimental sounds.

days.name: International Stuttering Awareness Day
days.about: Raises public understanding of stuttering and supports people who stutter. Groups hold talks and share personal stories to reduce stigma.

days.name: International Sushi Day
days.about: A day for eating sushi, whether at a restaurant or by trying to roll your own at home.

days.name: International Sweatpants Day
days.about: A day for wearing sweatpants and enjoying comfortable clothes, at home or out and about.

days.name: International Tea Day
days.about: Recognizes tea's cultural importance and the workers and small farmers who grow it. It's now backed by the UN, and people drink tea and learn about fair trade in the industry.

days.name: International Tiger Day
days.about: Raises awareness of wild tigers and efforts to protect them. It was set up at a 2010 tiger summit, and conservation groups run campaigns and fundraisers.

days.name: International Top Spinning Day
days.about: Started by the Spinning Top and Yo-Yo Museum in Burlington, Wisconsin, this day is a nod to the spinning top, a toy that's been around for thousands of years. People get out tops and spin them.

days.name: International Transgender Day of Visibility
days.about: A day for recognizing transgender people's lives and accomplishments, and for drawing attention to the discrimination they face. It was started in 2009 by activist Rachel Crandall, and people share stories and hold events.

days.name: International Translation Day
days.about: Honors translators and interpreters on the feast of St. Jerome, who translated the Bible. Language professionals hold events about the value of their work.

days.name: International Tug-of-War Day
days.about: A day for tug-of-war, the game where two teams pull on opposite ends of a rope and each tries to drag the other across a line. People get together and play it.

days.name: International Whale Shark Day
days.about: Raises awareness of whale sharks, the largest fish, and the need to protect them. It came out of a 2008 conservation conference, and groups share research and run awareness campaigns.

days.name: International Whisk(e)y Day
days.about: A day for whisky and whiskey drinkers, held on the birthday of the late writer Michael Jackson. It was set up to raise money for Parkinson's research, and people raise a glass and donate.

days.name: International Widows Day
days.about: A UN day drawing attention to the poverty and injustice many widows face around the world. Groups push for widows' rights and support.

days.name: International Wig Day
days.about: A lighthearted day for putting on a wig, silly or serious, to try a new look. It also raises awareness of hair loss caused by illness and chemotherapy.

days.name: International Women’s Day
days.about: A day recognizing women's achievements and pushing for gender equality. People hold marches, events, and talks, and in some countries give women flowers.

days.name: International Workers’ Day
days.about: Also called May Day, it honors workers and the labor movement. People hold rallies and marches, and in many countries it's a public holiday.

days.name: International Yada, Yada, Yada Day
days.about: A nod to the Seinfeld episode that made 'yada, yada, yada' famous as a way to skip the boring parts of a story. Fans rewatch the episode and work the phrase into conversation.

days.name: International Yoga Day
days.about: A UN-recognized day promoting yoga and its health benefits. People join group yoga sessions, often outdoors.

days.name: International Youth Day
days.about: A UN day focused on young people and the issues they face. It has a different theme each year, and groups hold events about youth involvement.

days.name: Internaut Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the World Wide Web opening to the public in 1991. People reflect on how the web changed their lives.

days.name: Internet Day
days.about: Marks the first message sent over ARPANET in 1969, the forerunner of the internet. People think about how the internet came to be.

days.name: Introduce A Girl To Engineering Day
days.about: Held during Engineers Week to get girls interested in engineering careers. Engineers and schools run hands-on activities and mentoring sessions.

days.name: iPod Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Apple's introduction of the iPod in 2001. People reminisce about the device and how it changed music listening.

days.name: Iris Day
days.about: A day for the iris flower, which has ties to Brussels, Belgium. People grow, pick or buy irises, give them to someone, paint them, or go to the Iris Festival in Brussels.

days.name: Irish Coffee Day
days.about: A day for drinking Irish coffee, the mix of hot coffee, Irish whiskey, sugar, and cream.

days.name: Isdal Woman Day
days.about: Named after an unidentified woman whose body was found in Norway in 1970 and whose death is still unsolved. It's a day to remember her and to draw attention to other unidentified people, mysterious deaths, and the victims' families.

days.name: I’m Not Going To Take It Anymore Day
days.about: A day for finally standing up to something that's been bothering you. People quit a bad habit, speak up, or make a change they've been putting off.

days.name: Jackfruit Day
days.about: A day about jackfruit, a tropical fruit, built around the idea of 'independence from meat.' People swap a meat meal for one made with jackfruit.

days.name: Jelly Bean Day
days.about: A day for eating jelly beans and trying all the flavors.

days.name: Jellyfish Day
days.about: A day for learning about jellyfish and their place in ocean ecosystems. Aquariums often hold special displays.

days.name: Jerky Day
days.about: A day for eating jerky, the dried, seasoned meat snack.

days.name: Jewel Day
days.about: A day for appreciating gems and jewelry. People wear their favorite pieces or give someone jewelry.

days.name: Job Action Day
days.about: A day for taking stock of your career and planning your next steps. It was started to help people stay employable, and people update résumés, learn skills, or network.

days.name: Johnny Appleseed Day
days.about: Remembers John Chapman, the pioneer who planted apple trees across the American frontier. People plant apple trees, eat apples, and tell his story.

days.name: Join Hands Day
days.about: Encourages young and older people to volunteer together on community projects. It was started by fraternal benefit societies, and people team up across generations for local service.

days.name: Joke Day
days.about: A day for telling jokes and making people laugh.

days.name: Joy Germ Day
days.about: A day for spreading happiness as if it were contagious. People do small things to cheer others up.

days.name: Juggling Day
days.about: Promoted by the International Jugglers' Association to share the skill of juggling. People hold juggling meetups, shows, and lessons for beginners.

days.name: Jukebox Day
days.about: Marks the debut of the first coin-operated phonograph, a jukebox forerunner, in a San Francisco saloon in 1889. People play songs on old jukeboxes or reminisce about them.

days.name: Juneteenth
days.about: Commemorates the end of slavery in the US, marking when enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, learned of their freedom in 1865. It's now a federal holiday, and people hold cookouts, parades, and community gatherings.

days.name: Junk Food Day
days.about: A day for indulging in junk food like chips, candy, and fast food.

days.name: K.I.N.D Day
days.about: Also called Kids in Need of Diapers Day, it raises awareness that many families can't afford enough diapers. People donate diapers or money to diaper banks, or volunteer with them.

days.name: Kahlua Day
days.about: A day for Kahlúa, the coffee liqueur. People mix drinks like a White Russian or use it in desserts.

days.name: Kazoo Day
days.about: A day for the kazoo, the simple instrument you hum into. People play kazoos, sometimes in group performances.

days.name: Kebab Day
