days.about: A food day for eating kebabs, skewered grilled meat or the doner style, at home or from a favorite shop.

days.name: Ken Day
days.about: A day for Barbie's boyfriend, the Ken doll, marking his debut at a 1961 toy fair. Fans and collectors get out their old Ken dolls, look at how the doll has changed over the years, or watch a Barbie movie.

days.name: Kickball Day
days.about: A day for playing kickball, the playground game that works like baseball with a big rubber ball you kick.

days.name: Kid Inventors’ Day
days.about: Held on Benjamin Franklin's birthday, since he invented swim fins as a boy. It recognizes things invented by children and encourages kids to try inventing.

days.name: Kidney Day
days.about: World Kidney Day raises awareness of kidney health and kidney disease. It encourages checkups and screening, especially for people at risk.

days.name: Kids Music Day
days.about: Promotes music education for children. Music stores and schools hold free lessons, recitals and instrument try-outs.

days.name: Kids Take Over The Kitchen Day
days.about: A day for letting kids plan and cook a meal, with parents helping, so they build cooking skills and learn about healthy food.

days.name: Kindergarten Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of Friedrich Froebel, the German educator who founded the first kindergarten. It recognizes the value of early childhood education.

days.name: Kiss A Ginger Day
days.about: Started as a friendly answer to the 'Kick a Ginger' bullying meme. It's a day for showing affection to redheads, or kissing one if they're willing.

days.name: Kiss And Make Up Day
days.about: A day for patching things up after an argument and making peace with someone you've fallen out with.

days.name: Kiss Your Fiance Day
days.about: A day for engaged couples to show each other some affection, starting with a kiss.

days.name: Kite Flying Day
days.about: A day for getting outside and flying a kite, whether store-bought or homemade.

days.name: Knife Day
days.about: Started by the knife maker Spyderco to appreciate pocketknives and other knives as everyday tools. Collectors show off their knives and stores run deals.

days.name: Kouign Amann Day
days.about: A day for the kouign amann, a buttery, caramelized layered pastry from Brittany. A San Francisco bakery started it in 2015, and people mark it by buying or baking one.

days.name: Lace Day
days.about: A day for appreciating lace and the skill it takes to make it by hand. People wear or use lace, or look into the history of lacemaking.

days.name: Lager Day
days.about: A day for drinking lager, the crisp, cold-fermented style of beer.

days.name: Lame Duck Day
days.about: Marks the ratification of the 20th Amendment, which shortened the time outgoing officials serve after losing an election. It's also a nod to anyone serving out their last days in a job.

days.name: Lamington Day
days.about: An Australian food day for eating lamingtons, squares of sponge cake dipped in chocolate and rolled in coconut.

days.name: Lard Day
days.about: Started by the Healthy Fats Coalition to promote lard as a traditional cooking fat. People cook or bake with it, for example in pie crusts or fried foods.

days.name: Lasagna Day
days.about: A food day for making or eating lasagna, the layered pasta dish.

days.name: Lash Stylists’ Day
days.about: A day started by Noble Lashes in 2017 to recognize eyelash technicians and their work. People mark it by thanking their lash stylist.

days.name: Laugh And Get Rich Day
days.about: A day for looking on the lighter side of life and getting "rich" in happiness, with the idea that laughing and enjoying yourself can go along with making money.

days.name: Law Enforcement Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for thanking police officers and other law enforcement. People wear blue, send thank-you notes or drop off food at stations.

days.name: Lazy Day
days.about: A day for taking it easy, skipping the chores and resting.

days.name: Lazy Mom’s Day
days.about: A day for moms to take a break from chores like laundry, dishes, carpools and cleaning. Others help out by cleaning up after themselves, rubbing mom's feet or walking the dog.

days.name: Learn About Butterflies Day
days.about: A day for learning about butterflies, including their life cycle, role as pollinators and conservation. Some people plant butterfly-friendly gardens.

days.name: Learn About Composting Day
days.about: A day for learning how to compost food scraps and yard waste, and maybe starting a compost bin.

days.name: Learn To Swim Day
days.about: Encourages kids and adults to learn to swim and promotes water safety to prevent drowning. Pools often offer lessons.

days.name: Learn Your Name In Morse Code Day
days.about: Held on Samuel Morse's birthday. It's a day for looking up how your name is spelled in dots and dashes.

days.name: Leave The Office Earlier Day
days.about: Started by productivity expert Laura Stack to encourage working efficiently enough to head home early and get some balance back.

days.name: Legal Assistance Day
days.about: A day to remind people that they have a right to legal help if they get into trouble.

days.name: Lei Day
days.about: A Hawaiian tradition for making, wearing and giving leis. It celebrates Hawaiian culture with music, hula and lei-making contests.

days.name: Lemon Chiffon Cake Day
days.about: A food day for baking or eating lemon chiffon cake, a light, fluffy cake made with oil and whipped egg whites.

days.name: Lemon Cream Pie Day
days.about: A food day for eating lemon cream pie, a creamy, tangy lemon filling in a crust.

days.name: Lemon Cupcake Day
days.about: A food day for baking or eating lemon cupcakes.

days.name: Lemon Juice Day
days.about: A day for appreciating lemon juice and its many uses, from cooking and drinks to cleaning.

days.name: Lemon Meringue Pie Day
days.about: A food day for eating lemon meringue pie, lemon curd topped with toasted meringue.

days.name: Lemonade Day
days.about: A program that teaches kids entrepreneurship by having them plan and run their own lemonade stands. Kids often save, spend or donate the money they earn.

days.name: Leprechaun Day
days.about: A day about the mischievous leprechauns of Irish folklore, with stories, crafts and hunts for pots of gold.

days.name: Let It Go Day
days.about: A day for letting go of grudges, regrets and things you can't change, and moving on.

days.name: Letter Writing Day
days.about: A day for sitting down and writing a real letter by hand to someone, then mailing it.

days.name: Levi Strauss Day
days.about: Held on Levi Strauss's birthday. It recognizes the businessman who, with tailor Jacob Davis, made the first riveted blue jeans, and people wear their jeans.

days.name: Library Workers Day
days.about: Run by the American Library Association during National Library Week to thank librarians and library staff.

days.name: Licorice Day
days.about: A food day for eating licorice, red or black, whichever side you're on.

days.name: Lighthouse Day
days.about: Marks the 1789 act of Congress that put lighthouses under federal care. It's a day to appreciate lighthouses and their keepers, and many lighthouses open for visits.

days.name: Limerick Day
days.about: Held on Edward Lear's birthday, since he popularized limericks. It's a day for reading or writing those funny five-line poems.

days.name: Lincolnshire Day
days.about: A day of county pride for Lincolnshire in England, marking the Lincolnshire Rising of 1536. It's observed with local food, events and flags.

days.name: Lineman Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for thanking the utility line workers who keep the power on, often working through storms and dangerous conditions.

days.name: Linguine Day
days.about: A food day for eating linguine, the flat, narrow pasta often served with clams or pesto.

days.name: Lips Appreciation Day
days.about: A day to pay attention to your lips and how to care for them, for example by keeping them moisturized and protected.

days.name: Lipstick Day
days.about: A day for wearing lipstick, often a bold shade, and many cosmetics brands run deals or giveaways around it.

days.name: Literacy Day
days.about: International Literacy Day was set up by UNESCO to draw attention to the importance of reading and writing. People promote literacy programs, donate books, or volunteer as tutors.

days.name: Lobster Day
days.about: A day for eating lobster, whether a lobster roll, a whole boiled lobster, or bisque, and for giving a nod to the lobster fishing industry.

days.name: Locate An Old Friend Day
days.about: A nudge to track down and reconnect with a friend you've lost touch with, by searching online, calling, or writing.

days.name: Log Cabin Day
days.about: Started by a Michigan log cabin society to encourage preserving old log cabins and learning their history. People visit or tour historic cabins.

days.name: Logistics Day
days.about: A day to recognize the people who move goods around, like truckers, warehouse workers, and supply chain planners, and the work that gets products where they need to go.

days.name: Lollipop Day
days.about: A day for eating lollipops or handing them out, especially to kids.

days.name: Look For An Evergreen Day
days.about: A day to notice and appreciate evergreen trees, which stay green through winter, maybe by taking a walk to find some.

days.name: Look On The Bright Side Day
days.about: Timed with the winter solstice, the darkest day of the year, it's a reminder to focus on the positive. Things get brighter from here.

days.name: Look Up at the Sky Day
days.about: A reminder to stop and actually look up, at clouds, sunsets, or stars, and take a moment to appreciate the sky.

days.name: Loomis Day
days.about: Honors Mahlon Loomis, a dentist who demonstrated a form of wireless telegraphy in the 1860s, before Marconi. People learn about him and early radio history.

days.name: Loosen Up, Lighten Up Day
days.about: A day for letting go of perfectionism and going with life's chaos instead of getting wound up. People skip the worrying, slow down, let small annoyances slide, and some invite friends over to relax with things like massages or a spa day.

days.name: Lost & Found Day
days.about: A day for getting lost things back where they belong. People return items they've found over the year to their owners, or go looking for something of their own they lost a while ago.

days.name: Lost Dog Awareness Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness about lost dogs and how to help them get home, such as microchipping, ID tags, and sharing lost-pet posts. It also encourages adopting from shelters.

days.name: Lost Penny Day
days.about: Falls on Lincoln's birthday, since he's on the penny. People gather the stray pennies lying around the house and put them to use, often by donating them to charity.

days.name: Lost Sock Memorial Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day to give up on the socks that vanished in the laundry and toss out or repurpose the lonely mismatched ones.

days.name: Love Island Day
days.about: A fan-made day for the launch of a new series of ITV's reality dating show Love Island. Fans often get friends together for a viewing party to watch the first episode.

days.name: Love Litigating Lawyers Day
days.about: A day to recognize litigators, the lawyers who take cases to court and argue for their clients. People thank the attorneys they know or learn more about what courtroom lawyers do.

days.name: Love Note Day
days.about: A day for writing a love note to a partner, or a note of appreciation to someone you care about, and leaving it for them to find.

days.name: Love Your Lawyer Day
days.about: Started by lawyer Nader Anise to counter lawyer jokes and bad press. People thank their attorneys or invite them out.

days.name: Love Your Pet Day
days.about: A day to spoil your pet with extra attention, treats, a new toy, or a long walk.

days.name: Love Your Produce Manager Day
days.about: A day started by Frieda's Specialty Produce to thank supermarket produce managers and their teams, held right after the busy Easter and Passover weekend. Shoppers and companies give thanks on social media, and Frieda's names standout produce managers.

days.name: Love Your Red Hair Day
days.about: A day for redheads to feel good about their hair, freckles and the wider redhead community, instead of hiding them. People show off their red hair and share photos.

days.name: Love Your Thighs Day
days.about: A body-positivity day that encourages women of every shape and size to accept their thighs however they look. It also kicks off the hot-weather chafing season, so women can feel confident in shorts and skirts.

days.name: Love’s Baby Soft Day
days.about: A nostalgic day for Love's Baby Soft, the powdery 1970s fragrance and beauty line. Fans wear the scent or treat themselves to a lotion, bath product or other beauty item.

days.name: Loving Day
days.about: Marks the 1967 Supreme Court ruling in Loving v. Virginia that struck down bans on interracial marriage. People hold gatherings and share stories about multiracial families.

days.name: Lucky Penny Day
days.about: A day based on the old saying about picking up a penny for good luck. People keep an eye out for pennies on the ground.

days.name: Lumberjack Day
days.about: A day honoring lumberjacks and their hard, old-school work. People often wear flannel or watch log-rolling and axe-throwing.

days.name: Lumpy Rug Day
days.about: About the problems you've swept under the rug. It's a prompt to finally deal with whatever you've been hiding or avoiding.

days.name: Lung Leavin’ Day
days.about: Started by Heather Von St. James, a mesothelioma survivor, to mark the day her lung was removed. People write their fears on plates and smash them into a fire, and it raises awareness of mesothelioma.

days.name: Mac & Cheese Day
days.about: A day for eating macaroni and cheese, from the boxed kind to baked homemade versions.

days.name: Macadamia Nut Day
days.about: A day for eating macadamia nuts, plain or in cookies and other treats.

days.name: Macaron Day
days.about: Started in New York by pastry chef François Payard, based on a Paris tradition. Bakeries give out free French macarons, often with a link to charity.

days.name: Macaroni Day
days.about: A day for eating macaroni pasta in any form, from casseroles to salads.

days.name: Macaroon Day
days.about: A day for eating macaroons, the chewy coconut cookies, as opposed to French macarons.

days.name: Mad Hatter Day
days.about: Inspired by the Mad Hatter's hat tag reading 10/6. It's a day for silliness, wearing odd hats, and Alice in Wonderland tea parties.

days.name: Madly In Love With Me Day
days.about: A self-love day timed with Valentine's Day, encouraging people to treat themselves kindly and appreciate who they are.

days.name: Magic Day
days.about: Held on the anniversary of Harry Houdini's death to honor magicians and magic as a performing art. People watch or put on magic shows.

days.name: Magna Carta Day
days.about: Marks the 1215 sealing of the Magna Carta, the English charter that limited the king's power. It's an occasion to learn about its influence on law and rights.

days.name: Mail Order Catalog Day
days.about: Marks Aaron Montgomery Ward's first mail-order catalog in 1872. People think back on catalog shopping or flip through one.

days.name: Maize Day
days.about: The day after Thanksgiving, for recognizing maize (corn), a plant grown all over the Americas. People cook a meal using ingredients that Native Americans traditionally used.

days.name: Make A Difference Day
days.about: A big national day of volunteering, originally started by USA Weekend magazine. People take on community service projects.

days.name: Make a Friend Day
days.about: A nudge to reach out and start a new friendship, like chatting with a neighbor or coworker you don't know well.

days.name: Make A Gift Day
days.about: A day for making gifts by hand for the coming holidays, which saves money and makes the gift more personal. People knit, paint, draw, make homemade jams or pickles, or give their time to someone who is lonely.

days.name: Make A Hat Day
days.about: A day for making your own hat, whether you knit or crochet one or put one together from paper or fabric. The National Needlearts Association uses it to get knitters and other yarn crafters started on a project for the colder months.

days.name: Make Cut-out Snowflakes Day
days.about: A day for folding and cutting paper into snowflakes, often to decorate windows.

days.name: Make Music Day
days.about: Based on France's Fête de la Musique, held on the summer solstice. Free public music events pop up everywhere, and anyone can play.

days.name: Make Up Your Mind Day
days.about: A day to finally make the decisions you've been putting off.

days.name: Make Up Your Own Holiday Day
days.about: A day to invent your own holiday, about whatever you like, and mark it however you want.

days.name: Make Your Bed Day
days.about: A reminder to make your bed in the morning. The idea is that finishing one small task first thing gives you a sense of order and gets you moving on the rest of the day.

days.name: Make Your Dream Come True Day
days.about: A day for taking at least one concrete step toward a personal goal or dream you've been putting off.

days.name: Making The First Move Day
days.about: An anti-bullying advocacy day started by bullying survivor Greshun De Bouse. Kids, families and others take pledges, talk openly and take a first step toward preventing bullying or recovering from it.

days.name: Malaria Day
days.about: World Malaria Day, set up by the World Health Organization to draw attention to malaria prevention and treatment. People raise awareness and donate to efforts like bed-net programs.

days.name: Manatee Appreciation Day
days.about: Promoted by the Save the Manatee Club to raise awareness of manatees and the threats they face, like boat strikes. People learn about them, visit them, or donate to conservation.

days.name: Mandela Day
days.about: Nelson Mandela International Day, held on his birthday and recognized by the UN. People are encouraged to spend 67 minutes doing community service, one for each year he spent in public service.

days.name: Mango Day
days.about: A day for eating mangoes and appreciating the fruit, which has deep cultural roots in India where the day is especially popular.

days.name: Maple Syrup Day
days.about: A day for enjoying real maple syrup on pancakes, waffles, or in recipes.

days.name: Marching Band Day
days.about: A day to recognize marching bands and the people who perform in them. Bands, schools and marching arts groups share performances and give shout-outs to their members.

days.name: Margarita Day
days.about: A day for making or ordering a margarita, the tequila-and-lime cocktail.

days.name: Marine Mammal Rescue Day
days.about: A day created by the California Senate to recognize the people who rescue and care for stranded or injured seals, sea lions, dolphins and whales. It also raises awareness of why those animals need protecting.

days.name: Mario Day
days.about: Nintendo's day for its Super Mario character, chosen because the date written short looks like 'MAR10'. Fans play Mario games and Nintendo often runs sales.

days.name: Maritime Day
days.about: National Maritime Day honors the U.S. merchant marine and marks the first steamship crossing of the Atlantic by the SS Savannah in 1819. Ceremonies remember merchant mariners, including those lost at sea.

days.name: Marmot Day
days.about: Alaska's answer to Groundhog Day, held on the same date, to recognize the marmot, which is common there.

days.name: Marriage Day
days.about: A day for weddings and for married couples to renew their vows. It began with the Chamber of Commerce in Elkton, Maryland, a town long known for quick weddings.

days.name: Martin Luther King Day
days.about: A U.S. federal holiday honoring civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. Many people spend it doing volunteer service, attending events, or reflecting on his work.

days.name: Martini Day
days.about: A day for mixing or ordering a martini, the classic gin or vodka and vermouth cocktail.

days.name: Marzipan Day
days.about: A day for eating marzipan, the sweet almond paste used in candies and for decorating cakes.

days.name: Mason Jar Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of John Landis Mason's 1858 patent for the screw-top glass jar. People use the day to can and preserve food or find other uses for mason jars.

days.name: Math 2.0 Day
days.about: A day about how math and technology work together and how digital tools are changing the way people learn, teach and use math. People try out math software, coding or math modeling.

days.name: May Ray Day
days.about: A day for getting outside to enjoy the sun and the warmer spring weather. People go for a hike or a bike ride, have a picnic, do yard work or just lie in the sun.

days.name: Mead Day
days.about: Started by the American Homebrewers Association to promote mead, the honey wine. People brew it, taste it, and share it at homebrew gatherings.

days.name: Measure Your Feet Day
days.about: A reminder to check your real shoe size, since feet change over time and badly fitting shoes can hurt. People take off their shoes and measure their feet at home with a tape measure, or have a professional do it.

days.name: Meatball Day
days.about: A day for making or eating meatballs, whether with spaghetti, in a sub, or on their own.

days.name: Mechanical Pencil Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the mechanical pencil, started in 2018 by the UK shop Cult Pens because fountain pens had a day and mechanical pencils didn't. People use a favorite mechanical pencil, write or draw with one, or learn about its history.

days.name: Melba Toast Day
days.about: A day for eating melba toast, the thin crisp toast named after opera singer Nellie Melba.

days.name: Melon Day
days.about: A holiday in Turkmenistan honoring the country's melons, especially its prized local varieties. People go to fairs and markets to show off, taste, and buy melons, and there are melon-themed events.

days.name: Memo Day
days.about: A day about the office memo. A Denver radio station started it to call attention to how many memos pile up at work. People use it to clear out the backlog and write fewer, better memos.

days.name: Memory Day
days.about: A day for appreciating human memory and raising awareness of memory loss from conditions like Alzheimer's and dementia. People reminisce, share old memories, and support or raise money for memory-care causes.

days.name: Men Make Dinner Day
days.about: A day for men who don't usually cook to make dinner for their household.

days.name: Menstrual Hygiene Day
days.about: Started by the nonprofit WASH United to break taboos around menstruation and push for access to period products and sanitation worldwide.

days.name: Men’s Grooming Day
days.about: Started by the men's grooming brand American Crew, this day nudges men to update their grooming routine and take better care of themselves. Barbershops and salons often hold grooming events on the day.

days.name: Mermaid Day
days.about: A day for fans of mermaids and the folklore, books, and films they appear in. People read or retell mermaid stories and do mermaid-themed crafts.

days.name: Meteor Watch Day
days.about: A day for going outside at night and watching the sky for shooting stars.

days.name: Mickey Mouse Day
days.about: Marks Mickey Mouse's screen debut in the 1928 cartoon 'Steamboat Willie'. Disney fans watch his cartoons and Disney parks hold events.

days.name: Microneedling Day
days.about: An awareness day started by Crown Aesthetics, the company that makes the SkinPen microneedling device. It's meant to get people to learn about microneedling, a minimally invasive skin treatment also called collagen induction therapy.

days.name: Microvolunteering Day
days.about: Promotes volunteering in small, quick chunks, often online, like signing petitions or doing short tasks for charities. It was started by the Help From Home organization.

days.name: Middle Child’s Day
days.about: A day to give some attention to middle children, who are often said to feel overlooked between their older and younger siblings.

days.name: Middle Name Pride Day
days.about: A day for sharing and owning your middle name, even the embarrassing ones.

days.name: Military Spouse Appreciation Day
days.about: Established by President Reagan to recognize the sacrifices and support of military spouses. Communities and businesses hold events or offer thanks and discounts.

days.name: Milk Chocolate Day
days.about: A day for eating milk chocolate, the creamier, sweeter kind.

days.name: Milk Day
days.about: A day recognizing milk and the dairy industry. People drink milk, and dairy groups promote its nutrition.

days.name: Mincemeat Day
days.about: A day for eating mincemeat, the spiced mixture of dried fruit, suet, and sometimes meat, usually baked into pies.

days.name: Miners’ Day
days.about: National Miners Day honors coal miners and remembers those killed on the job. It marks the anniversary of the 1907 Monongah mine disaster in West Virginia.

days.name: Miniature Golf Day
days.about: A day for playing a round of mini golf.

days.name: Mint Julep Day
days.about: A day for mixing a mint julep, the bourbon, mint, and sugar drink best known from the Kentucky Derby.

days.name: Mitten Tree Day
days.about: A day for collecting mittens and hanging them on a Christmas tree. The mittens are then handed out to people in need so they can keep their hands warm in winter.

days.name: Mojito Day
days.about: A day for making or ordering a mojito, the Cuban rum, mint, and lime cocktail.

days.name: Molasses Bar Day
days.about: A food day for molasses bars, chewy bar cookies made with molasses that came before chocolate brownies. People bake a batch and eat them.

days.name: Moldy Cheese Day
days.about: A day for eating cheeses that are supposed to have mold, like blue cheese, Roquefort, Gorgonzola, and Brie.

days.name: Mole Day
days.about: A chemistry day for the mole unit and Avogadro's number (6.02 × 10^23), observed from 6:02 a.m. to 6:02 p.m. on 10/23. Chemistry teachers and students do mole-themed activities and puns.

days.name: Monkey Day
days.about: A day for monkeys and other primates, started by two Michigan State art students. People learn about primates, support conservation, or just goof around and dress up as monkeys.

days.name: Monte Cristo Sandwich Day
days.about: A day for eating a Monte Cristo, the battered and fried ham-and-cheese sandwich often dusted with powdered sugar and served with jam.

days.name: Moon Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the Apollo 11 landing, when people first walked on the Moon. People look back at the mission and learn about lunar exploration.

days.name: Moonshine Day
days.about: About moonshine, the unaged homemade corn whiskey tied to bootlegging history. People read up on that history or try a legally made bottle.

days.name: More Herbs, Less Salt Day
days.about: Encourages cooking with herbs and spices instead of salt for better health. People try seasoning their meals with fresh or dried herbs.

days.name: Morning Show Hosts Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the hosts of morning TV shows. People watch their favorite morning show, read up on how the hosts got their jobs, and tell others which host they like best and why.

days.name: Morse Code Day
days.about: Falls on Samuel Morse's birthday and honors the dot-and-dash code he helped create. People learn a few letters or tap out messages, and ham radio operators often get on the air.

days.name: Moscato Day
days.about: A day for drinking Moscato, the sweet, lightly sparkling white wine originally from Italy.

days.name: Moth-er Day
days.about: Despite the name, it has nothing to do with mothers. It's a day about moths and the people who collect them, when people learn about moths and why they matter for pollination and the food chain, try going out to look for moths, or get in touch with other moth fans.

days.name: Mother Goose Day
days.about: Honors the Mother Goose nursery rhymes. People read the old rhymes aloud, especially with young children.

days.name: Mother Ocean Day
days.about: A day started by the South Florida Kayak Fishing Club for appreciating the ocean and raising awareness about protecting it. People join beach cleanups, share facts about ocean conservation, or try to go a day without plastic.

days.name: Mother-In-Law Day
days.about: A day to honor your mother-in-law, started by a Texas newspaper editor in the 1930s. People call her, send a card, or take her out.

days.name: Motivation and Inspiration Day
days.about: A day right after New Year's for getting your new-year goals going, started by motivational speaker Kevin McCrudden. People use it to plan their goals and look for something that inspires them to stick with them.

days.name: Mount Everest Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay first reaching the summit of Everest. People remember the climb and learn about the mountain and Sherpa culture.

days.name: Mountain Day
days.about: A tradition at some colleges, like Mount Holyoke and Smith, where the president picks a nice fall day and cancels classes as a surprise, announced by ringing the college bells. Students spend the day hiking up a nearby mountain or relaxing with friends.

days.name: Mousse Day
days.about: A day for eating mousse, the light, airy dessert, most often chocolate.

days.name: Mouthguard Day
days.about: A day for thinking about mouthguards, which protect athletes' teeth and gums from injury. Dentists use it to remind families to get their kids properly fitted ones before fall sports start.

days.name: Mud Pack Day
days.about: A day for putting on a mud mask or clay facial and pampering your skin.

days.name: Muffin Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating muffins.

days.name: Mule Day
days.about: Honors mules and marks the arrival of the Spanish donkeys the King of Spain sent George Washington, which he used to breed mules. People appreciate these hardworking animals, and some towns hold mule shows.

days.name: Mulled Wine Day
days.about: A day for making or drinking mulled wine, red wine warmed with spices and fruit.

days.name: Mulligan Day
days.about: Named after the golf do-over, it's a day for second chances. People retry something that went wrong or give someone else a fresh start.

days.name: Museum Day
days.about: Smithsonian magazine's yearly event where participating museums across the US give free admission to people who download a ticket.

days.name: Museum Selfie Day
days.about: Started to get people into museums and talking about them. Visitors take selfies with the art and exhibits and post them online.

days.name: Mustard Day
days.about: A day for mustard, tied to the National Mustard Museum in Wisconsin, which holds a festival. People try different kinds of mustard.

days.name: My Way Day
days.about: A day based on the saying 'my way or the highway,' when you do whatever you want however you want to do it. That might mean sleeping in, eating what you like, or taking a long shower.

days.name: Nachos Day
days.about: A day for making or eating nachos, tortilla chips loaded with melted cheese and toppings.

days.name: Nail Day
days.about: A day for manicures and nail care. People pay attention to keeping their nails healthy and try out new nail art or polish.

days.name: Naked Gardening Day
days.about: A day started by nudist groups for gardening in the nude, in a private yard or at clothing-optional places.

days.name: Name Tag Day
days.about: Encourages wearing a 'Hello, my name is' name tag so strangers can greet you by name and be friendlier.

days.name: Name Your Car Day
days.about: A day for giving your car a name, if it doesn't already have one.

days.name: Name Your PC Day
days.about: A day for giving your computer a personal name, from back when PCs were new to most households.

days.name: Name Yourself Day
days.about: A day to pick a new name for yourself, just for fun, if you've never liked yours.

days.name: Namesake Day
days.about: A day for looking into where your first name and surname came from, like who you were named after and what your family name means. It starts off Celebrate Your Name Week.

days.name: Napping Day
days.about: Set just after the clocks spring forward, it's for taking a nap to make up for the lost hour of sleep.

days.name: National Anthem Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Francis Scott Key writing 'The Star-Spangled Banner' after the bombardment of Fort McHenry. People learn its history or sing it.

days.name: National Geographic Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the National Geographic Society. People read the magazine, look at its photography, or learn about the world.

days.name: Native American Day
days.about: A day recognized in states like California and South Dakota to honor Native American history and cultures, often with events, powwows, and school lessons.

days.name: Nature Photography Day
days.about: Promoted by the North American Nature Photography Association to get people outdoors photographing plants, animals, and landscapes and sharing the pictures.

days.name: Navy Day
days.about: Honors the US Navy and was set on Theodore Roosevelt's birthday because he championed it. People thank sailors and veterans.

days.name: Near Miss Day
days.about: Marks the time an asteroid passed unusually close to Earth in 1989. It's a reminder of near-Earth objects and how lucky we sometimes are.

days.name: Neighbor Day
days.about: A day for getting to know your neighbors, whether by saying hello, bringing over food, or helping out.

days.name: Neurofibromatosis Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness of neurofibromatosis, a genetic condition that causes tumors to grow on nerves. People share information and support research and affected families.

days.name: Never Give Up Day
days.about: A day about perseverance and sticking with your goals when things get hard. It's also a time to thank the people who helped you keep going.

days.name: New Beer’s Eve
days.about: The night before the anniversary of beer becoming legal again near the end of Prohibition. People raise a beer to mark it.

days.name: New Conversations Day
days.about: A day for talking with people about things you normally wouldn't, or striking up a conversation with someone new, so you get to know them better.

days.name: New Home Owners Day
days.about: A day to mark the milestone of buying your own home and the security it gives you and your family.

days.name: Newspaper Carrier Day
days.about: Marks the hiring of the first newsboy in the US, a 10-year-old who sold the New York Sun. People thank their newspaper delivery person.

days.name: Niagara Falls Runs Dry Day
days.about: Marks the time an ice jam on the Niagara River nearly stopped Niagara Falls in 1848. People read up on the odd event and the falls.

days.name: Night Out
days.about: National Night Out, a community event where neighbors hold block parties and cookouts with local police to build relationships and promote safer neighborhoods.

days.name: No Beard Day
days.about: A day that challenges people with beards to shave them off and go clean-shaven, to see what their face looks like underneath.

days.name: No Bra Day
days.about: A breast cancer awareness day where women go braless and are reminded to do self-checks and get screened.

days.name: No Diet Day
days.about: Started in the UK by Mary Evans Young to push back on diet culture. People skip dieting and focus on body acceptance and healthy attitudes toward weight.

days.name: No Dirty Dishes Day
days.about: A day for skipping the dishwashing, either by eating out or using paper plates, or for clearing the sink completely.

days.name: No Homework Day
days.about: A day that gives students a break from homework assignments so they can rest and spend the time on other things.

days.name: No Housework Day
days.about: A day for taking a break from cleaning and chores and leaving the housework for another time.

days.name: No Interruptions Day
days.about: Created by consultant Dan Markovitz, it falls on the last business day of the year. People shut off distractions and work without being interrupted.

days.name: No News is Good News Day
days.about: A day built around the saying 'no news is good news', meaning that if you haven't heard otherwise, things are probably fine. The idea is to set aside bills and worries for the day and just relax.

days.name: No One Eats Alone Day
days.about: Run by the nonprofit Beyond Differences, it has students make sure nobody sits alone at lunch, to fight social isolation in schools.

days.name: No Pants Day
days.about: Started as a prank at the University of Texas. People go about their day in boxers or shorts instead of pants.

days.name: No Selfies Day
days.about: A day for not taking any selfies for 24 hours, putting your phone down and enjoying what's happening around you.

days.name: No Smoking Day
days.about: A UK health campaign day that encourages smokers to quit, or at least go a day without smoking.

days.name: No Socks Day
days.about: A day for going sockless, giving your feet some air and skipping the extra laundry.

days.name: No Tobacco Day
days.about: The World Health Organization's World No Tobacco Day, which raises awareness of tobacco's health harms and encourages people to quit.

days.name: Noodle Day
days.about: A day for eating noodles of any kind, from ramen to spaghetti.

days.name: Noodle Ring Day
days.about: A day for making or eating a noodle ring, a baked ring of egg noodles often filled with creamed meat or vegetables.

days.name: Norfolk Day
days.about: Launched by the Eastern Daily Press newspaper, it's for people to show pride in the English county of Norfolk and enjoy what it offers.

days.name: Notebook Day
days.about: Started in 2016 by the notebook company May Designs, it's a day about paper notebooks. People use it to start a journal, write by hand, or swap notebooks with friends.

days.name: Nothing Day
days.about: Created by columnist Harold Pullman Coffin as a day with nothing to observe. The idea is to sit back and do nothing at all.

days.name: Nougat Day
days.about: A day for eating nougat, the chewy candy made from sugar or honey, egg whites, and nuts.

days.name: Numbat Day
days.about: A Western Australian awareness day for the numbat, an endangered striped marsupial that eats termites, with events to raise conservation funds.

days.name: Numeracy Day
days.about: Run by the UK charity National Numeracy, it encourages people to build confidence with everyday maths.

days.name: Nut Day
days.about: A day for eating nuts, whether as a snack or in recipes.

days.name: Nutty Fudge Day
days.about: A day for making or eating fudge with nuts in it.

days.name: Nylon Stockings Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of nylon stockings first going on sale nationwide in the US in 1940, a big moment in fashion.

days.name: Oatmeal Cookie Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating oatmeal cookies.

days.name: Oatmeal Muffin Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating oatmeal muffins.

days.name: Oatmeal Nut Waffles Day
days.about: A day for making waffles with oats and nuts for breakfast.

days.name: Odie Day
days.about: Marks the first appearance of Odie, Garfield's dopey dog pal, in the comic strip in 1978.

days.name: Old Farmers Day
days.about: A day for honoring farmers and the old ways of farming that fed the country.

days.name: Old Rock Day
days.about: A day for appreciating very old rocks, fossils, and geology, maybe by visiting a museum or hunting for interesting stones.

days.name: Old Stuff Day
days.about: A day for appreciating your old belongings, or for sorting through them and getting rid of what you don't need.

days.name: Older Peoples Day
days.about: A day for recognizing older people's contributions and raising awareness of issues they face, tied to the UN's International Day of Older Persons.

days.name: One Cent Day
days.about: A day about the penny, the smallest U.S. coin. People look into its history and how it has changed, and some collect or count pennies or do simple coin activities.

days.name: One Day Without Shoes Day
days.about: Started by the shoe company TOMS. People go barefoot to draw attention to children around the world who have no shoes.

days.name: One Voice Day
days.about: A worldwide effort to get people in every country to read the Universal Peace Covenant aloud at the same moment, as a show of unity and peace across nations and religions.

days.name: One-Hit Wonder Day
days.about: Created by Steve Rosen as a day for listening to songs by artists who had just one big hit.

days.name: Onion Rings Day
days.about: A day for eating onion rings.

days.name: Open An Umbrella Indoors Day
days.about: A day for defying the old superstition by opening an umbrella inside.

days.name: Open That Bottle Night
days.about: Started by Wall Street Journal wine columnists Dorothy Gaiter and John Brecher. People finally open that special bottle of wine they've been saving and share it.

days.name: Opera Day
days.about: A day for learning more about opera and listening to it, whether that means going to a performance or watching one online.

days.name: Operating Room Nurse Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the nurses who work in operating rooms and care for patients before, during, and after surgery.

days.name: Opposite Day
days.about: A playful day, popular with kids, when you say and do the opposite of what you mean.

days.name: Optimism Day
days.about: A day pushed by optimist groups to get people looking on the bright side. People try to stay positive, take care of themselves and do small positive things for others.

days.name: Orange Blossom Day
days.about: A day for enjoying orange blossoms, the white flowers of orange trees, for how they look and smell. It also nods to their use in food and perfume and to their place as Florida's state flower.

days.name: Orange Chicken Day
days.about: A day for eating orange chicken, the sweet-and-tangy fried chicken dish that Panda Express made famous. Panda Express started it and often runs deals on it.

days.name: Organize Your Home Day
days.about: A day to get a head start on spring cleaning by clearing out clutter and putting your house in order early in the year.

days.name: Organize Your Home Office Day
days.about: Started by freelance writer Lisa Kanarek, it's a nudge for people who work from home to tidy and organize their home office and clear out clutter so they can get more done.

days.name: Origami Day
days.about: A Japanese day for the art of paper folding, started by the Japan Origami Association. People fold cranes and other figures, and the date's repeated 1s are meant to look like the sides of a square sheet.

days.name: Orphan Sunday
days.about: A Sunday when churches focus on orphans and children in foster care, encouraging adoption, fostering, and support for those families. It's promoted by the Christian Alliance for Orphans.

days.name: Ovarian Cancer Day
days.about: World Ovarian Cancer Day spreads awareness of ovarian cancer's subtle symptoms. People share information and raise money for research and support.

days.name: Overdose Awareness Day
days.about: International Overdose Awareness Day remembers people who have died from drug overdoses and works to reduce the stigma around drug-related deaths. It started in Australia, and people often wear purple or silver and hold vigils.

days.name: Overseas NHS Workers Day
days.about: A UK day for thanking the doctors, nurses, and other staff from abroad who work in the National Health Service, and for recognizing their contribution.

days.name: Own Business Day
days.about: Also called I Own My Own Business Day, it recognizes people who run their own independent businesses, and people mark it by giving those owners and their businesses some extra attention and support.

days.name: Oyster Day
days.about: A day for eating oysters, whether raw on the half shell, grilled, or fried.

days.name: Pack Rat Day
days.about: A day for people who tend to save and pile up stuff to take an honest look at their habits and decide what's worth keeping and what to let go.

days.name: Pack Your Lunch Day
days.about: A reminder to bring lunch from home instead of buying it, which tends to be cheaper and healthier.

days.name: Panda Day
days.about: A day for learning about giant pandas and supporting conservation efforts to protect them and their bamboo forest habitat.

days.name: Pandemonium Day
days.about: A day to accept the chaos in everyday life: you drop your usual routines, leave things undone or disorganized, and go with whatever happens.

days.name: Pangolin Day
days.about: World Pangolin Day raises awareness of pangolins, scaly anteater-like mammals that are among the most trafficked animals in the world, and of efforts to protect them.

days.name: Panic Day
days.about: It started out as a joke holiday about how stressful life already is, and these days it's mostly a reminder to look after your mental health. People use it to notice what's stressing them, try ways to calm down, and talk more openly about anxiety and panic.

days.name: Paper Airplane Day
days.about: A day for folding paper airplanes and seeing how far or how well they fly. Kids and classrooms often hold contests.

days.name: Paper Clip Day
days.about: A day about the humble paper clip, which Norwegians wore as a quiet symbol of resistance during the Nazi occupation in World War II.

days.name: Paperback Book Day
days.about: A day for curling up with a paperback. It nods to Penguin's launch of cheap paperbacks in 1935, which made books affordable for everyone.

days.name: Paranormal Day
days.about: A day for being curious about ghosts and other things science can't explain. People watch paranormal documentaries, swap ghost stories, or read up on unexplained events.

days.name: Pardon Day
days.about: It marks Gerald Ford's pardon of Richard Nixon in 1974. It's also taken as a prompt to forgive someone.

days.name: Parents’ Day
days.about: A US day, established by Congress in 1994, for honoring parents and the role they play in raising children. People thank their moms and dads together.

days.name: Parfait Day
days.about: A day for eating parfaits, whether the layered yogurt, fruit, and granola kind or the frozen French dessert.

days.name: Particularly Preposterous Packaging Day
days.about: It pokes fun at packaging that's wasteful, oversized, or nearly impossible to open. Some people avoid extra packaging by bringing their own bags and buying unpackaged goods, while others go looking for the most ridiculous packaging they can find.

days.name: Password Day
days.about: World Password Day reminds people to update weak passwords and turn on two-factor authentication. It was promoted by Intel.

days.name: Pastry Day
days.about: A day for eating pastries, such as croissants, danishes, and turnovers.

days.name: Patriot Day
days.about: The US day of remembrance for the people killed in the September 11, 2001 attacks. Flags fly at half-staff and people observe moments of silence.

days.name: Paul Bunyan Day
days.about: A day for the giant lumberjack of American folklore and his blue ox Babe. People retell his tall tales.

days.name: Pawnbrokers Day
days.about: Recognized by the National Pawnbrokers Association, it honors pawnbrokers and the role their loans and other services play in local communities, and it pushes back on the usual stereotypes. People are encouraged to learn about the history of pawnbroking or visit a local pawn shop.

days.name: Pay it Forward Day
days.about: A day for doing a good turn for a stranger, like paying for the next person's coffee, in the hope they pass it on. It was started in Australia by Blake Beattie.

days.name: PayDay It Forward
days.about: Paula Long started it in memory of her son, Paylor "PayDay" James Daniels, who was killed at 18. It asks people to show kindness and respect to young men, especially young Black men, by checking in on them, supporting them, and looking past stereotypes.

days.name: Peach Ice Cream Day
days.about: A day for eating peach ice cream, often homemade with summer peaches.

days.name: Peach Melba Day
days.about: A day for peach melba, the dessert of peaches, raspberry sauce, and vanilla ice cream that chef Auguste Escoffier created for the opera singer Nellie Melba.

days.name: Peach Pie Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating peach pie.

days.name: Peaches ‘N’ Cream Day
days.about: A day for the simple summer dessert of sliced peaches with cream.

days.name: Peanut Brittle Day
days.about: A day for eating peanut brittle, the hard candy made of cooked sugar and peanuts.

days.name: Peanut Butter and Chocolate Day
days.about: A day for treats that combine peanut butter and chocolate, like peanut butter cups.

days.name: Peanut Butter and Jelly Day
days.about: A day for eating the classic PB&J sandwich.

days.name: Peanut Butter Cookie Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating peanut butter cookies, the kind with the criss-cross fork marks.

days.name: Peanut Butter Day
days.about: A day for eating peanut butter, straight from the spoon or in sandwiches and recipes.

days.name: Peanut Butter Fudge Day
days.about: A day for making or eating peanut butter fudge.

days.name: Peanut Cluster Day
days.about: A day for peanut clusters, the candy made of peanuts held together with chocolate.

days.name: Peanut Day
days.about: A day for eating peanuts and appreciating the crop, much of it grown in the American South.

days.name: Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day
days.about: A US day honoring the people killed in the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941, which brought the US into World War II. Flags fly at half-staff and memorial ceremonies are held.

days.name: Pecan Cookie Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating pecan cookies, such as pecan sandies.

days.name: Pecan Day
days.about: A day for eating pecans, the nut native to North America.

days.name: Pecan Pie Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating pecan pie.

days.name: Pecan Torte Day
days.about: A day for making or eating pecan torte, a rich layered cake made with ground pecans.

days.name: Peculiar People Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the quirky, offbeat people who don't follow the crowd, like that odd friend or neighbor everyone's fond of, and for being a bit different yourself.

days.name: Pencil Day
days.about: A day about the pencil. It marks Hymen Lipman's 1858 patent for a pencil with an eraser attached.

days.name: Penguin Awareness Day
days.about: A day for learning about penguins and the threats they face, such as climate change, overfishing and habitat loss. People read up on them, visit aquariums or support conservation groups.

days.name: Penuche Fudge Day
days.about: A day for penuche, a caramel-like fudge made with brown sugar, butter and milk, often with nuts. People make a batch or buy some to share.

days.name: Pepper Pot Day
days.about: A day for Philadelphia pepper pot, a thick, peppery tripe and vegetable soup that legend links to feeding George Washington's troops at Valley Forge. People cook or order a bowl.

days.name: Peppermint Patty Day
days.about: A day for the chocolate-covered peppermint candy. People eat a few or make homemade versions.

days.name: Pepperoni Pizza Day
days.about: A day for the most popular pizza topping in the US. People order or make a pepperoni pizza.

days.name: Personal Chef Day
days.about: Started by the American Personal & Private Chef Association to recognize chefs who cook in clients' homes. People thank their personal chef or look into hiring one.

days.name: Personal Trainer Awareness Day
days.about: A day to recognize fitness trainers and the work they do helping clients. People thank their trainer or book a session to get started.

days.name: Pet Day
days.about: Started by animal welfare advocate Colleen Paige to appreciate pets and encourage adopting from shelters. People spoil their animals and share photos of them.

days.name: Pet Fire Safety Day
days.about: Promoted by the American Kennel Club and ADT to prevent pets from accidentally starting house fires and to make sure they can be rescued in one. People pet-proof stoves and candles and put pet alert stickers on windows.

days.name: Pet Obesity Awareness Day
days.about: Run by the Association for Pet Obesity Prevention to draw attention to overweight pets. Owners check their pet's weight with a vet and cut back on treats.

days.name: Pet Owners Independence Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day where owners imagine staying home while their pets go to work for them. Mostly it's an excuse to spend the day relaxing with your pet.

days.name: Pet Rock Day
days.about: A nod to the 1970s Pet Rock fad started by Gary Dahl, who sold ordinary rocks in boxes with care instructions. People paint or adopt a rock for fun.

days.name: Pet Theft Awareness Day
days.about: A day to warn owners that pets get stolen and to encourage protection. People microchip their pets, update ID tags and avoid leaving animals unattended outside.

days.name: Petite And Proud Day
days.about: A day for short people, usually 5'4" or under, to feel good about their height and enjoy being small instead of wishing they were taller.

days.name: Petroleum Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Edwin Drake's 1859 oil well in Pennsylvania, which started the modern oil industry. People learn about petroleum's history and its many uses.

days.name: Pharmacist Day
days.about: A day to thank pharmacists for filling prescriptions and giving medication advice. People say thanks at their local pharmacy.

days.name: Philanthropy Day
days.about: Promoted by the Association of Fundraising Professionals to recognize charitable giving and volunteering. People donate, volunteer or honor local givers.

days.name: Photography Day
days.about: Marks the 1839 announcement of the daguerreotype process, an early form of photography. People take and share photos.

days.name: Physician Assistant Day
days.about: Recognizes physician assistants and marks the 1967 graduation of the first PA class at Duke University. People thank the PAs who care for them.

days.name: Pi Day
days.about: A day for the number pi, set on March 14 because the date matches 3.14. It was started by physicist Larry Shaw at San Francisco's Exploratorium, and people eat pie and hold digit-reciting contests.

days.name: Pick Strawberries Day
days.about: A day for heading to a farm or garden to pick your own strawberries during the season.

days.name: Pickle Day
days.about: A day for pickles of all kinds. People eat them, try new varieties or pickle their own.

days.name: Pie Day
days.about: A day for pie, promoted by the American Pie Council. People bake or eat their favorite kind.

days.name: Pierogi Day
days.about: A day for the filled Polish dumplings. People eat or make pierogi with fillings like potato, cheese or sauerkraut.

days.name: Pig Day
days.about: Started by two sisters in 1972 to recognize pigs as intelligent, useful animals. People learn about pigs, collect pig figurines or visit farms.

days.name: Pig In A Blanket Day
days.about: A day for small sausages or hot dogs wrapped in dough or pancakes. People make a batch as a snack.

days.name: Pillow Fight Day
days.about: A day when people meet up in public places in cities around the world for big flash-mob pillow fights.

days.name: Pineapple Day
days.about: A day for pineapple. People eat it fresh, grilled, in drinks or on pizza.

days.name: Pinhole Photography Day
days.about: An international day for taking photos with lensless pinhole cameras, often homemade. Participants share their pictures in an online gallery.

days.name: Pink Day
days.about: A day for the color pink. People wear pink clothes and enjoy pink things.

days.name: Pinot Grigio Day
days.about: A day for the light, crisp white wine. People open a bottle with friends.

days.name: Pinot Noir Day
days.about: A day for the red wine made from the thin-skinned Pinot Noir grape. People drink a glass or try a new bottle.

days.name: Pins And Needles Day
days.about: Marks the 1937 opening of 'Pins and Needles,' a Broadway musical revue staged by members of the garment workers' union. People learn about the show and its labor history.

days.name: Pioneer Day
days.about: A Utah holiday marking the arrival of Mormon pioneers in the Salt Lake Valley in 1847. People attend parades, rodeos and fireworks.

days.name: Pistachio Day
days.about: A day for pistachios. People snack on them or use them in baking and ice cream.

days.name: Pizza Day
days.about: A day for pizza in any style. People order or make their favorite.

days.name: Pizza Party Day
days.about: A day for getting friends, family or coworkers together over pizza.

days.name: Pizza With The Works Except Anchovies Day
days.about: A day for a fully loaded pizza with every topping except anchovies. People order one piled high.

days.name: Piña Colada Day
days.about: A day for the rum, coconut and pineapple cocktail from Puerto Rico. People mix one up, with or without alcohol.

days.name: Piñata Day
days.about: A day for enjoying piñatas, the colorful papier-mâché containers full of candy and trinkets. People make them or whack one open at a party.

days.name: Plan A Solo Vacation Day
days.about: A day to encourage people to plan a trip on their own. People research destinations and book time away by themselves.

days.name: Plan Your Epitaph Day
days.about: Started by Lance Hardie as a lighthearted way to think about mortality. People write the words they'd want on their own tombstone.

days.name: Planner Day
days.about: A day for people who love planners to talk about how planning and staying organized has helped them. Many share their planners on social media, and some people use it as the day to start using a planner.

days.name: Plant a Flower Day
days.about: A day for planting flowers as spring approaches. People put in seeds, bulbs or seedlings in gardens or pots.

days.name: Plant a Lemon Tree Day
days.about: A day for planting a lemon tree, in the ground in warm climates or in a pot indoors.

days.name: Plant Power Day
days.about: A day to promote plant-based eating and its health and environmental benefits. People try vegan or vegetarian meals.

days.name: Play Doh Day
days.about: A day for the modeling compound, which started as a wallpaper cleaner. People, especially kids, mold things out of Play-Doh.

days.name: Play God Day
days.about: Despite the name, it's a day for doing something good to make someone else's life better. That can be as small as paying for the groceries of the person behind you in line or as big as donating a car to charity.

days.name: Play In The Sand Day
days.about: A day for playing in the sand. People build sandcastles at the beach or in a sandbox.

days.name: Play Monopoly Day
days.about: A day for the classic property-trading board game. People get together for a game.

days.name: Play More Cards Day
days.about: A day for getting out a deck of cards and playing card games with family and friends, like Go Fish or Old Maid. It's meant to bring people together around a simple game.

days.name: Play Tennis Day
days.about: A day meant to get people onto a court, whether that means picking up a racket for the first time or getting back into the game.

days.name: Playdate Day
days.about: A screen-free day when kids get together with their friends to play. The idea is that they stay active, get along with each other and build life skills through play.

days.name: Playing Card Collection Day
days.about: A day for appreciating and collecting playing cards, including the history and artwork of different decks. Collectors often show off their decks or add new ones to their collection.

days.name: Please Take My Children To Work Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day for worn-out stay-at-home parents, playing on Take Your Child to Work Day. The idea is that someone else takes the kids along so the parent gets a break.

days.name: Plimsoll Day
days.about: Honors Samuel Plimsoll, the British reformer behind the load line painted on ships' hulls, which shows how heavily a ship can safely be loaded.

days.name: Plum Pudding Day
days.about: A day for eating plum pudding, the steamed British Christmas pudding, which contains no plums, only raisins and other dried fruit.

days.name: Plush Animal Lover’s Day
days.about: A day for stuffed animals and the people who love them. People spend time with their plush toys, add to their collections, or give a stuffed animal to a loved one or a child in need.

days.name: Pluto Day
days.about: Marks Clyde Tombaugh's discovery of Pluto in 1930, and is a day to learn about Pluto and the outer solar system.

days.name: Pluto Demoted Day
days.about: Marks the 2006 decision by the International Astronomical Union to reclassify Pluto as a dwarf planet. People use it to revisit the debate over what counts as a planet.

days.name: Pocky Day
days.about: A Japanese day, picked because the date written as 11/11 looks like four Pocky sticks. People buy and share the chocolate-dipped biscuit sticks, and the maker Glico runs promotions.

days.name: Poem on Your Pillow Day
days.about: A day for bringing poetry home by leaving a short poem on someone's pillow, like a partner or family member, or reading a poem with your child at bedtime. Hotels are invited to join in too.

days.name: Poet in a Cupcake Day
days.about: The last day of Take Your Poet to School Week. Students look up a few fun facts about a favorite poet and then decorate cupcakes, either real or paper cut-outs, to match that poet.

days.name: Poetry And The Creative Mind Day
days.about: A day for appreciating poetry and the people who write it, and creative minds in general. People read or re-read poems they love, or use whatever art form they like to express themselves.

days.name: Poetry At Work Day
days.about: A day for bringing poetry into the workplace, by sharing a poem with coworkers, reading one in a meeting or writing one about your job.

days.name: Poet’s Day
days.about: A day for recognizing poets from the past and those writing now. People are encouraged to try writing a poem, read poetry aloud, and get kids and students interested in poetry.

days.name: Poinsettia Day
days.about: Marks the death of Joel Roberts Poinsett, who brought the poinsettia from Mexico to the US. People give or buy the plants and learn about them.

days.name: Pokémon Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the first Pokémon games' release in Japan in 1996. Fans play and share their love of the series, and the company usually announces new games and news.

days.name: Polar Bear Day
days.about: Set up by Polar Bears International to raise awareness of polar bears and the loss of the Arctic sea ice they depend on. People are encouraged to learn about the bears and cut their own carbon emissions.

days.name: Polar Bear Swim Day
days.about: Usually New Year's Day, when people take a quick plunge into freezing water, often in groups and often to raise money for charity.

days.name: Pony Express Day
days.about: Marks the start of the Pony Express in 1860, the relay of horseback riders that carried mail across the American West. It's a day to remember that bit of history.

days.name: Pop Music Chart Day
days.about: A day for paying attention to the pop music charts, the rankings of the most popular songs. People follow the current charts or listen to a top-ten countdown, and some throw a party that plays whatever is charting.

days.name: Popcorn Day
days.about: A day for making and eating popcorn, whether plain, buttered or with fancier toppings.

days.name: Positive Media Day
days.about: A day to push back against doomscrolling and bad news by focusing on hopeful, uplifting stories. People read or watch good news and share it with friends and family online.

days.name: Positive Thinking Day
days.about: A day for focusing on an optimistic outlook and practicing more hopeful self-talk.

days.name: Postal Worker Day
days.about: A day for thanking mail carriers and other postal workers, for example with a note or small treat left for the person who delivers your mail.

days.name: Potato Chip Day
days.about: A day for eating potato chips and trying different flavors.

days.name: Potato Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the potato and cooking it in its many forms.

days.name: Pothole Day
days.about: A UK day for drawing attention to the state of the roads and encouraging people to report potholes to their local council.

days.name: Pots De Creme Day
days.about: A day for making or eating pots de crème, the rich French baked custard served in little pots.

days.name: Potteries Bottle Oven Day
days.about: A day in Stoke-on-Trent for remembering the bottle-shaped kilns that used to fill the skyline when the pottery industry was at its height. There are tours of the bottle ovens that are still standing, plus exhibitions and workshops, and former pottery workers share their memories.

days.name: Poultry Day
days.about: A day for eating dishes made with chicken, turkey, duck and other poultry.

days.name: Pound Cake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating pound cake, the dense cake originally made with a pound each of flour, butter, sugar and eggs.

days.name: Pralines Day
days.about: A day for eating pralines, the Southern candy of pecans cooked in sugar and butter that's linked to New Orleans.

days.name: Pretend To Be A Time Traveler Day
days.about: A playful day for dressing and acting as if you've arrived from the past or the future, puzzling over modern things or hinting at what's to come.

days.name: Pretzel Day
days.about: A day for eating pretzels, with a nod to Pennsylvania's long pretzel-making tradition.

days.name: Prime Rib Day
days.about: A day for cooking or ordering prime rib, the large roast cut of beef rib.

days.name: Princess Day
days.about: A lighthearted day started by the makers of the animated film The Swan Princess. It's about fairy-tale princesses and the kindness, confidence and imagination they stand for, and people dress up, watch princess movies or do princess-themed activities with kids.

days.name: Pro Sports Wives Day
days.about: A day started by the Professional Sports Wives Association to recognize the wives of current and retired pro athletes, coaches and executives. It especially highlights their public service and charity work.

days.name: Professional Speakers Day
days.about: A day for recognizing professional speakers who inform, inspire and entertain audiences. People also use it to work on their own public-speaking skills.

days.name: Programmers’ Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the people who write software. Coders often mark it with in-jokes, office treats, and thanks from colleagues, and it is officially recognized in Russia.

days.name: Project Management Day
days.about: A day for recognizing project managers and their teams, often by thanking the people who keep projects on track.

days.name: Proofreading Day
days.about: Started by Judy Beaver in honor of her mother, it encourages people to check their writing carefully for errors before sending or publishing it.

days.name: Proposal Day
days.about: Started by John Michael O'Loughlin and set on the spring equinox, it encourages people to propose marriage to their partners.

days.name: Psychic Day
days.about: A day about psychics and claimed abilities beyond the five senses. It reportedly began as a publicity stunt for a manager's celebrity psychics, and people mark it by getting tarot, astrology or aura readings or by testing their own intuition.

days.name: Psychotherapy Day
days.about: A day when therapists, clients and supporters of therapy promote talk therapy, push back against the stigma of seeing a therapist, and draw attention to community mental-health needs. People share why therapy matters and encourage others to get help.

days.name: Public Gardens Day
days.about: Promoted by the American Public Gardens Association to get people to visit botanical gardens, arboretums and other public gardens in their area.

days.name: Public Radio Broadcasting Day
days.about: It marks the first public radio broadcast, sent out in New York City in 1910, and honors the people who invented radio and public broadcasting. People tune in to the radio and think about the role it has played over the years.

days.name: Public Service Day
days.about: A United Nations day recognizing civil servants and the work of public service.

days.name: Pulled Pork Day
days.about: A day for making or eating slow-cooked pulled pork, often barbecued and piled on a sandwich.

days.name: Pumpkin Day
days.about: A day for pumpkins: carving them, baking with them, or just picking one up from a patch.

days.name: Pumpkin Pie Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating a slice of pumpkin pie.

days.name: Punch Day
days.about: A day for the mixed fruit drink, so people make a bowl of punch, with or without alcohol.

days.name: Punctuation Day
days.about: Started by writer Jeff Rubin to remind people to use commas, apostrophes and the rest correctly. People hunt for punctuation mistakes on signs or brush up on the rules.

days.name: Punk for a Day Day
days.about: Musician and artist Travis Blue started this day for punk music and culture. People try out punk for a day by listening to the music, wearing the fashion and leaning into its non-conformist attitude.

days.name: Puppy Day
days.about: Started by pet advocate Colleen Paige. It's for enjoying puppies and encouraging people to adopt them from shelters instead of buying from puppy mills.

days.name: Purebred Dog Day
days.about: A day to appreciate purebred dog breeds and the history behind them, often promoted by breed clubs and responsible breeders.

days.name: Purple Day
days.about: An epilepsy awareness day started by a Canadian girl, Cassidy Megan. People wear purple to show support and help reduce stigma.

days.name: Put A Pillow On Your Fridge Day
days.about: Based on an old custom of putting a cloth or pillow in the larder for good luck and plenty. People put a pillow on or in their fridge, hoping for a prosperous year.

days.name: Put On Your Own Shoes Day
days.about: It's about the small milestone of a child learning to put on their own shoes. Parents let their kids put on their own shoes and tie their own laces.

days.name: Puzzle Day
days.about: A day for doing puzzles of all kinds: jigsaws, crosswords, sudoku, brain teasers.

days.name: Pygmy Hippo Day
days.about: It's for raising awareness of the endangered pygmy hippo, a smaller cousin of the common hippo, and the need to protect it and where it lives. People learn about the species and support efforts to save it.

days.name: Quiche Lorraine Day
days.about: A day for making or eating quiche Lorraine, the French egg-and-bacon tart.

days.name: Quiet Day
days.about: Also called National Don't Utter a Word Day, it's a day for cutting down on noise for a calmer, healthier life. People talk less, meditate, take a quiet walk outdoors or go on a one-day quiet retreat.

days.name: Quilting Day
days.about: Promoted by the National Quilting Association for quilters to show off their work, quilt together, and teach the craft to others.

days.name: Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day
days.about: A day for enjoying country songs with odd or funny titles, so people dig them up and play them.

days.name: Rabbit Day
days.about: A day for rabbits, especially pet rabbit welfare. People learn how to care for rabbits properly and support rabbit rescues.

days.name: Race Your Mouse Around The Icons Day
days.about: A lighthearted day for having some fun with your computer mouse by racing the cursor around the icons on your desktop. Some people also use it as a nudge to clean up their desktop and remove shortcuts and programs they no longer use.

days.name: Radio Commercials Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the first radio commercial, which aired on the New York station WEAF in 1922. Radio fans use the day to think back on radio advertising and the role it has played.

days.name: Radio Day
days.about: A day to appreciate radio. People tune in to their favorite stations, and UNESCO's World Radio Day highlights radio's role in news and community.

days.name: Rain Day
days.about: Comes from Waynesburg, Pennsylvania, where it has rained on this date in most years on record. The town holds a festival and keeps track of whether it rains.

days.name: Rainbow Bridge Remembrance Day
days.about: For remembering pets that have died, named after the poem about pets waiting at the Rainbow Bridge. People share photos and memories of animals they've lost.

days.name: Random Acts Of Kindness Day
days.about: A day for doing small kind things for strangers or friends, like paying for someone's coffee or leaving a nice note.

days.name: Random Acts of Poetry Day
days.about: A Canadian literacy event where poets read poems to strangers in public places, and people are encouraged to share poetry unexpectedly.

days.name: Rapture Party Day
days.about: Started as a joke response to Harold Camping's prediction that the Rapture would come in May 2011. People threw parties on the date to poke fun at it.

days.name: Rare Disease Day
days.about: Run by the European patient group EURORDIS to raise awareness of rare diseases and the people living with them. Events push for better research and care.

days.name: Raspberry Cake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating cake made with raspberries.

days.name: Raspberry Cream Pie Day
days.about: A day for making or eating raspberry cream pie.

days.name: Ravenclaw Pride Day
days.about: A day for Harry Potter fans sorted into Ravenclaw, the house known for wit and learning. Fans wear blue and bronze and show off their house pride.

days.name: Ravioli Day
days.about: A day for eating ravioli, the stuffed Italian pasta.

days.name: Re-gifting Day
days.about: Promoted by Money Management International before Christmas to make it okay to pass on gifts you won't use to someone who will, saving money and waste.

days.name: Read a Book Day
days.about: A day to sit down and read a book, any book you like.

days.name: Read A Road Map Day
days.about: A day to pull out an old-fashioned paper map and practice finding your way without GPS.

days.name: Read Across America Day
days.about: Started by the National Education Association around Dr. Seuss's birthday to get kids reading. Schools hold reading events and guest readers visit classrooms.

days.name: Read An Ebook Day
days.about: Started by the library ebook service OverDrive to encourage people to read a book on a device, often borrowed free from the library.

days.name: Read In The Bathtub Day
days.about: A day for relaxing in a warm bath with a good book.

days.name: Reading Is Funny Day
days.about: A day for showing kids that reading can be fun, often by giving them funny books and humorous stories to enjoy.

days.name: Receptionists’ Day
days.about: A day to thank receptionists, the people who greet visitors and answer the phones, often with a card, treat or small gift.

days.name: Record Store Day
days.about: Started in 2007 to support independent record shops. Stores hold events and sell special limited vinyl releases, and fans line up early to get them.

days.name: Red Mitten Day
days.about: A Canadian day for showing pride in the country's Olympic athletes. People wear or buy the red mittens that are sold to help fund those athletes.

days.name: Red Rose Day
days.about: A US day honoring the red rose as a symbol of love and romance and as the June birth flower. People often give red roses or just take time to appreciate them.

days.name: Refired, Not Retired Day
days.about: A day for people who are retired or close to it to think about their next stage of life. They might take up new interests, goals or activities instead of slowing down.

days.name: Registered Dietitian Day
days.about: Part of National Nutrition Month, from the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. It's for recognizing registered dietitians and the advice they give on food and health.

days.name: Relaxation Day
days.about: Thought up by a boy named Sean Moeller as a day to take it easy. People skip the stress, nap, read or do whatever helps them unwind.

days.name: Religion Day
days.about: Usually refers to World Religion Day, started by the Bahá'í community to promote understanding between faiths. Communities hold interfaith talks and gatherings.

days.name: Religious Freedom Day
days.about: Marks the adoption of Thomas Jefferson's Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom. It's a reminder of the right to practice any religion or none, and schools often teach about it.

days.name: Remember Me Thursday
days.about: Started by the Helen Woodward Animal Center to remember pets that died in shelters waiting for homes. People light candles, share photos online and encourage adoption.

days.name: Renewal Day
days.about: A day for new beginnings and fresh starts. People recommit to goals or resolutions they let slide, or pick back up things and relationships they had left behind.

days.name: Repair Day
days.about: For fixing broken things instead of throwing them out, often through repair cafés where volunteers help people mend electronics, clothes and other items.

days.name: Repeal Day
days.about: Marks the repeal of Prohibition in the United States in 1933, when alcohol became legal again. People raise a glass or visit a bar to mark it.

days.name: Repeat Day
days.about: A silly day about repetition, where people do things they like a second time. Examples include having another slice of pie, watching the same movie twice in a row or repeating a favorite catchphrase.

days.name: Reptile Awareness Day
days.about: A day for learning about snakes, lizards, turtles and other reptiles, and about the threats many species face. People visit zoos and reptile exhibits or share facts to ease fears about these animals.

days.name: Respect Day
days.about: A day to think about how you treat other people and to make a point of being respectful, considerate and encouraging toward loved ones, coworkers and strangers.

days.name: Respect For Parents Day
days.about: A day for thanking your parents and showing them appreciation, whether with a call, a visit or time spent together.

days.name: Restless Legs Awareness Day
days.about: A day for spreading information about restless legs syndrome (Willis-Ekbom disease), which causes an urge to move the legs, especially at night. It falls on the birthday of Karl-Axel Ekbom, a doctor who described the condition.

days.name: Revenge of the Fifth
days.about: The day after 'May the Fourth' Star Wars day, given over to the franchise's villains. Fans watch the films and dress up as Sith and other dark-side characters.

days.name: Ribbon Candy Day
days.about: A day for ribbon candy, the old-fashioned hard candy folded into wavy ribbons and usually set out in bowls around the winter holidays.

days.name: Rice Ball Day
days.about: A food day for the Japanese rice ball. People make rice balls at home or go out to eat them.

days.name: Rice Pudding Day
days.about: A day for making or eating rice pudding, the sweet dessert of rice cooked slowly in milk with sugar and often cinnamon or raisins.

days.name: Richter Scale Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of seismologist Charles Richter, who developed the Richter scale for measuring earthquake magnitude. People use it to learn about earthquakes and how they are measured.

days.name: Ride the Wind Day
