days.about: Marks the anniversary of the Gossamer Condor's prize-winning human-powered flight in 1977, and is a day for appreciating flight. People visit air museums and airfields, build and fly kites, or find other ways to ride the wind.

days.name: Ring a Bell Day
days.about: A New Year's Day observance where people ring bells to mark the end of the old year and the start of the new one, since bells have long stood for beginnings and endings.

days.name: Rivers Day
days.about: A day for appreciating rivers and drawing attention to their protection, started by Canadian conservationist Mark Angelo as BC Rivers Day and later expanded to World Rivers Day. People hold river cleanups, paddling trips and riverside events.

days.name: Roald Dahl Day
days.about: Held on the author's birthday, for reading Roald Dahl's books, such as Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and Matilda. Schools and kids often dress up as his characters.

days.name: Roast Chestnuts Day
days.about: A winter food day for roasting chestnuts over a fire or in the oven and eating them warm.

days.name: Roast Leg of Lamb Day
days.about: A food day for cooking a roast leg of lamb, often with garlic and rosemary.

days.name: Roast Suckling Pig Day
days.about: A food day for roast suckling pig, a young pig roasted whole and served as a feast dish in many cuisines.

days.name: Rocky Road Day
days.about: A day for rocky road, the chocolate ice cream (or candy bar) mixed with marshmallows and nuts.

days.name: Rollercoaster Day
days.about: A day for riding roller coasters and learning about their history, including LaMarcus Thompson's early coaster patent. Fans head to amusement parks for a ride.

days.name: Roof Over Your Head Day
days.about: A day for being grateful for having a home, and for thinking about or helping people who don't have one.

days.name: Root Beer Float Day
days.about: A day for root beer floats, made by putting a scoop of vanilla ice cream in root beer. Some restaurants hand out free or discounted floats and donate to charity.

days.name: Root Canal Appreciation Day
days.about: Started by a dentist to change the bad reputation of root canals and show that the treatment saves teeth and relieves pain rather than causing it.

days.name: Roots Day
days.about: A day for looking into your family history. People use holiday get-togethers to ask relatives about their ancestors, share family stories and start genealogy research.

days.name: Rosé Day
days.about: A day for drinking rosé wine, started by a rosé producer. People share a glass or a bottle with friends, often outdoors.

days.name: Rotisserie Chicken Day
days.about: A food day for rotisserie chicken, the whole chicken roasted on a turning spit that many grocery stores sell ready to eat.

days.name: Rounds Resounding Day
days.about: A day for singing rounds, catches and canons, the songs where groups come in one after another, like 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat' or 'Three Blind Mice.'

days.name: Rubber Duckie Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Ernie singing 'Rubber Duckie' on Sesame Street. It's a day for enjoying the bath toy, collecting ducks or doing duck-themed fun.

days.name: Rum Day
days.about: A day for drinking rum, neat or in cocktails like mojitos and daiquiris, and learning about its Caribbean history.

days.name: Rumi Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of the 13th-century Persian poet Rumi, for reading and sharing his poems and thoughts on love and spirituality.

days.name: Running Day
days.about: Also known as Global Running Day, it encourages people of all abilities to go for a run and to commit to being active.

days.name: Russian Language Day
days.about: A UN language day held on the birthday of poet Alexander Pushkin, for recognizing the Russian language and its literature.

days.name: Sachertorte Day
days.about: A day for Sachertorte, the famous Viennese chocolate cake with a layer of apricot jam and chocolate glaze, often served with whipped cream.

days.name: Safer Internet Day
days.about: An international day, started in Europe, for promoting safe and responsible internet use, especially among children and teens. Schools and organizations run lessons on online safety, privacy and cyberbullying.

days.name: Saint Patrick’s Day
days.about: The feast day of Ireland's patron saint and a celebration of Irish culture. People wear green, go to parades and gather in pubs, often with Irish food and music.

days.name: Salami Day
days.about: A food day for salami, the cured sausage eaten sliced on sandwiches, pizza or charcuterie boards.

days.name: Salesperson Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the work of salespeople and thanking those who have helped you as a customer.

days.name: Sandcastle Day
days.about: A day for heading to the beach or a sandbox and building sandcastles and sand sculptures.

days.name: Sandwich Day
days.about: A day for making and eating sandwiches, tied to the birthday of the Earl of Sandwich, whose name the food carries. Some sandwich shops run deals.

days.name: Sangria Day
days.about: A day for sangria, the Spanish punch of wine mixed with chopped fruit and sometimes brandy or soda.

days.name: Sardines Day
days.about: A food day for sardines, the small oily fish usually eaten from a can or grilled fresh.

days.name: Satisfied Staying Single Day
days.about: A day for people who are happy being single to enjoy that status, without feeling pressure to be in a relationship.

days.name: Sauntering Day
days.about: Started by W.T. Rabe at the Grand Hotel on Mackinac Island as a reaction against jogging. It's a day for slowing down and taking an unhurried, leisurely stroll.

days.name: Sausage Pizza Day
days.about: A food day for pizza topped with sausage, one of the most popular pizza toppings in the US.

days.name: Sausage Roll Day
days.about: A British food day for sausage rolls, sausage meat wrapped in puff pastry and baked, a bakery and party staple.

days.name: Save The Elephant Day
days.about: Started in Thailand to draw attention to threats to elephants, like poaching for ivory and habitat loss. People learn about the animals and support conservation groups.

days.name: Save The Frogs Day
days.about: Organized by the group SAVE THE FROGS! to raise awareness of declining amphibian populations. People join educational events, habitat cleanups and pond restoration.

days.name: Save Your Hearing Day
days.about: A day for learning how to prevent noise-induced hearing loss, for example by using earplugs and turning down headphones, and for getting your hearing checked.

days.name: Save Your Photos Day
days.about: Promoted by professional photo organizers, this is a reminder to back up, digitize and organize family photos so they aren't lost in a disaster or computer failure.

days.name: Saxophone Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of Adolphe Sax, the Belgian inventor of the saxophone. It's a day for listening to or playing sax music, especially jazz.

days.name: Say Something Nice Day
days.about: A day for saying kind words to people around you, from family to strangers, to make civility and kindness a habit.

days.name: Scented Candle Day
days.about: A day for lighting and enjoying scented candles at home, or giving one as a small gift.

days.name: School Bus Drivers Day
days.about: A day for thanking the people who drive kids to and from school, often with cards or small gifts from students and parents.

days.name: School Nurse Day
days.about: A day, promoted by the National Association of School Nurses, for recognizing the nurses who look after students' health at school.

days.name: School Principals’ Day
days.about: A day for thanking school principals for their work, often with notes or small gestures from students, staff and parents.

days.name: Science Education Day
days.about: Held on Albert Einstein's birthday to highlight the importance of science education. Schools, students and teachers use it to show off and promote science learning.

days.name: Science Fiction Day
days.about: Held on Isaac Asimov's birthday, it's a day for reading, watching or talking about science fiction.

days.name: Scotch Whisky Day
days.about: A day for having a dram of Scotch whisky and learning a bit about how it's made and where it comes from.

days.name: Scottish Wildcat Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of the Scottish wildcat, a critically endangered native cat, and supporting efforts to save it.

days.name: Scouse Day
days.about: Global Scouse Day is for cooking and eating scouse, the meat and vegetable stew Liverpool is known for, often raising money for charity.

days.name: Scrabble Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of Scrabble's inventor Alfred Butts, it's a day for sitting down to a game of Scrabble.

days.name: Scrapple Day
days.about: A day for eating scrapple, the fried loaf of pork scraps and cornmeal from Pennsylvania Dutch cooking.

days.name: Scream Day
days.about: A day for letting off stress and pent-up emotion with a good scream, ideally somewhere it won't bother anyone, like a car, a pillow, or out in nature.

days.name: Scrubs Day
days.about: A day to thank the doctors, nurses, dentists, and other medical workers who wear scrubs, the clean uniforms used in healthcare.

days.name: Scud Day
days.about: SCUD stands for 'Savor the Comic, Unplug the Drama.' Stephanie West Allen started it in 2007 as a day to look for the humor in things and stay out of drama.

days.name: Sea Monkey Day
days.about: A day for the Sea-Monkeys novelty pets, brine shrimp sold as kits, with people reminiscing about or raising them.

days.name: Second Half of the Year Day
days.about: Marking the start of the year's second half, it's a day for checking in on your goals and resetting plans for the rest of the year.

days.name: Seed Swap Day
days.about: A winter day when gardeners get together to trade seeds, often at community seed swap events, before planting season.

days.name: Selfie Day
days.about: A day for taking selfies and sharing them online.

days.name: Send a Card to a Friend Day
days.about: A day for mailing a handwritten card to a friend just to keep in touch.

days.name: Senior Citizens Day
days.about: Proclaimed by President Reagan in 1988, it's a day for honoring older people, visiting them and appreciating what they contribute.

days.name: Senior Health & Fitness Day
days.about: A day with organized events, often at community centers and senior homes, encouraging older adults to exercise and stay healthy.

days.name: Sense Of Smell Day
days.about: Started by the Sense of Smell Institute, it's a day for appreciating and learning about how our sense of smell works.

days.name: Serendipity Day
days.about: A day about serendipity, the happy accidents and lucky chance discoveries that turn out well. People notice and appreciate the good things that happen by chance.

days.name: Serpent Day
days.about: A day for learning about snakes and appreciating their role in nature rather than fearing them.

days.name: Sesame Street Day
days.about: Marking the show's 1969 premiere, it's a day for remembering and watching Sesame Street and its characters.

days.name: Sewing Machine Day
days.about: Tied to Elias Howe's sewing machine patent, it's a day for appreciating the machine and doing some sewing.

days.name: Shades Day
days.about: A day for wearing sunglasses and reminding people to protect their eyes from UV light.

days.name: Share a Hug Day
days.about: A day for giving hugs to friends and family to show affection, comfort, and support.

days.name: Shareware Day
days.about: A day for appreciating shareware programs and paying or registering for the ones you actually use.

days.name: Shark Awareness Day
days.about: A day for learning about sharks and their importance to the ocean, and for supporting shark conservation.

days.name: Sherlock Holmes Day
days.about: A day for reading or rewatching Sherlock Holmes stories and appreciating Arthur Conan Doyle's detective.

days.name: SHIFT10 Day
days.about: A day for shopping local: people pledge to move 10% of their regular spending from chain stores to local businesses.

days.name: Ship in A Bottle Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the craft of building model ships inside bottles, or trying to make one.

days.name: Shopping Reminder Day
days.about: Falls about a month before Christmas, as a nudge to get started on holiday shopping. People make their gift lists and start buying, often to catch the Black Friday sales.

days.name: Short Girl Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for appreciating short women, usually with jokes and posts about the perks and annoyances of being short.

days.name: Short Story Day
days.about: Held on the shortest day of the year, it's for reading, writing and sharing short stories.

days.name: Shortbread Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating shortbread, the buttery Scottish biscuit.

days.name: Show & Tell At Work Day
days.about: A day for bringing something from home to work and telling coworkers about it, like a school show-and-tell.

days.name: Shrimp Scampi Day
days.about: A day for cooking or eating shrimp scampi, shrimp in garlic butter and wine.

days.name: Sibling Day
days.about: Started by Claudia Evart in memory of her late siblings, it's a day for honoring brothers and sisters and getting in touch with them.

days.name: Sight Day
days.about: Known as World Sight Day, it's for raising awareness of blindness and vision problems and encouraging eye checkups.

days.name: Simplicity Day
days.about: Held on Henry David Thoreau's birthday, it's a day for cutting back clutter and busyness and living more simply.

days.name: Single Parent’s Day
days.about: A day for recognizing single parents who raise children on their own, and offering them some help or thanks.

days.name: Single Tasking Day
days.about: A day for doing one thing at a time instead of multitasking, giving each task your full attention.

days.name: Single Working Women’s Day
days.about: A day for recognizing single women who support themselves and often others through their work.

days.name: Singles Awareness Day
days.about: The day after Valentine's Day, for single people to enjoy being single, treat themselves or get together with friends.

days.name: Singles Day
days.about: Started in China on 11/11 as a day for single people, it has become a huge online shopping event.

days.name: Sinkie Day
days.about: The day after Thanksgiving, for people who eat over the kitchen sink to save time and dishes.

days.name: Sisters Day
days.about: A day for honoring sisters, spending time with them or sending them a note.

days.name: Skeptics Day
days.about: A day for questioning claims, checking facts and not taking things at face value.

days.name: Skirt Day
days.about: A day about the skirt as a piece of clothing. People wear one, buy one for themselves or someone else, or read up on the skirt's history.

days.name: Skyscraper Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for admiring skyscrapers and the engineering and design behind them. It falls on the birthday of William Van Alen, the architect of New York's Chrysler Building.

days.name: Skyscraper Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of architect Louis Sullivan, a pioneer of the skyscraper. People look up at, read about, or visit tall buildings.

days.name: Sled Dog Day
days.about: Honors sled dogs, often recalling the 1925 serum run to Nome, Alaska, when dog teams carried diphtheria medicine. People learn about the dogs and mushing.

days.name: Slinky Day
days.about: A day for the Slinky, the coiled spring toy that walks down stairs. People play with one or learn how it was invented.

days.name: Slytherin Pride Day
days.about: A Harry Potter fan day for people who identify with Slytherin house. Fans wear green and silver and show their house spirit.

days.name: Small Business Saturday (US)
days.about: The Saturday after Thanksgiving, started by American Express in 2010, encouraging people to do holiday shopping at small, local businesses.

days.name: Smart & Sexy Day
days.about: A day about the idea that people can be both smart and attractive, with women especially in mind. It started as a promotion by the lingerie and swimwear brand Smart & Sexy.

days.name: Smart Home Day
days.about: A day run by CEDIA, the smart home industry association, to make people more aware of smart home technology and the professionals who design and install it. Integrators, designers, builders and homeowners use it to look at and talk about connected-home tech.

days.name: Smart is Cool Day
days.about: A day for pushing back on the idea that smart people aren't cool. It encourages kids and adults to be proud of their intelligence and their love of learning.

days.name: Smile Power Day
days.about: A day about how much a smile can do. You smile at people in the hope that it gets them smiling and they pass it on to someone else.

days.name: Smoke and Mirrors Day
days.about: A day named after the smoke and mirrors magicians use in stage illusions. It recognizes magicians and illusion, and it's also a nudge to watch out for deception and misdirection in everyday life.

days.name: Snow Leopard Day
days.about: International Snow Leopard Day raises awareness of the endangered big cat of Central Asia's mountains and efforts to protect it.

days.name: Snowman Burning Day
days.about: Started at Lake Superior State University, people burn a snowman effigy on the first day of spring to say goodbye to winter.

days.name: Social Enterprise Day
days.about: Part of Global Entrepreneurship Week, this day raises awareness of social enterprises, which are businesses set up to tackle social or environmental problems. People learn about them and back them, for example by buying from them.

days.name: Social Media Day
days.about: Started by Mashable in 2010 to recognize social media's role in how people communicate. People hold meetups and post about it online.

days.name: Social Security Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the 1935 Social Security Act. A day to learn about the program and its benefits.

days.name: Something On A Stick Day
days.about: A day for eating food served on a stick, like corn dogs, kebabs, popsicles, or candy apples.

days.name: Son and Daughter Day
days.about: A day for parents to spend time with their children and tell them how much they mean.

days.name: Sourdough Bread Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating sourdough bread, made with a fermented starter instead of commercial yeast.

days.name: Sourest Day
days.about: A playful follow-up to Sweetest Day. It's an excuse to eat sour foods and to try to cheer up the grumpy, sour people in your life.

days.name: Space Day
days.about: Started in 1997 by Lockheed Martin to get kids interested in space, science, and math, often through school activities.

days.name: Space Exploration Day
days.about: Marks the Apollo 11 Moon landing and recognizes space exploration. People learn about space missions and astronauts.

days.name: Spaghetti Day
days.about: A day for cooking and eating spaghetti.

days.name: Spanish Paella Day
days.about: A day for making or eating paella, the saffron rice dish from Valencia, Spain.

days.name: Spareribs Day
days.about: A day for cooking and eating spareribs, usually barbecued pork ribs.

days.name: Spicy Guacamole Day
days.about: A day for making guacamole with a kick from jalapeños or other hot peppers.

days.name: Spicy Hermit Cookie Day
days.about: A day for baking hermit cookies, old New England spiced molasses cookies with raisins or nuts.

days.name: Spinach Day
days.about: A day for eating spinach, the leafy green Popeye made famous.

days.name: Splurge Day
days.about: A day to set the budget aside for once and spend some money on yourself or someone you love, like a nice meal out or something you wouldn't usually buy.

days.name: Sponge Cake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating sponge cake, the light, airy cake made with whipped eggs.

days.name: Spouse’s Day
days.about: A day for showing appreciation to your husband or wife, often with a small gesture or time together.

days.name: Spreadsheet Day
days.about: Marks the release of VisiCalc, the first spreadsheet program, in 1979. Spreadsheet users mark their dependence on tools like Excel.

days.name: Sprinkle Day
days.about: A day for the colorful candy sprinkles put on ice cream, donuts, and cupcakes.

days.name: Spumoni Day
days.about: A day for eating spumoni, the layered Italian ice cream with fruit and nuts.

days.name: Square Dancing Day
days.about: A day for square dancing, the American folk dance where four couples follow a caller's instructions.

days.name: Squirrel Appreciation Day
days.about: Started by wildlife rehabilitator Christy Hargrove, it's a day to notice squirrels and maybe put out food for them in winter.

days.name: St. Nicholas Day
days.about: The feast of St. Nicholas, the gift-giving bishop behind Santa Claus. Children leave shoes out the night before and find treats in them.

days.name: St. Urho’s Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek Finnish-American holiday from Minnesota honoring a made-up saint said to have driven grasshoppers from Finland. People wear purple and green the day before St. Patrick's Day.

days.name: Star Trek Day
days.about: Marks the 1966 TV premiere of Star Trek. Fans watch episodes and celebrate the franchise.

days.name: Star Trek First Contact Day
days.about: Marks the fictional 2063 date when Vulcans first meet humans in the Star Trek film First Contact. Fans watch the movie and get together.

days.name: Star Wars Day
days.about: A fan day built on the pun 'May the Fourth be with you.' Fans watch the movies, dress up, and stores run Star Wars promotions.

days.name: Static Electricity Day
days.about: A day about static electricity and the science behind it, like the zap from a doorknob or hair standing on end. People use it to learn how static builds up, often by trying simple experiments.

days.name: Stay Home Because You’re Well Day
days.about: A playful day for taking a day off when you're not sick, just to rest and enjoy being healthy.

days.name: Stay Out Of The Sun Day
days.about: A reminder to take sun safety seriously and give your skin a break. People stay indoors or in the shade and think about the risk of skin cancer from too much sun.

days.name: Stay Up All Night Night
days.about: An excuse to skip sleep for one night on purpose and pull an all-nighter for fun, for example with a movie or TV marathon or other late-night outings.

days.name: Steak Au Poivre Day
days.about: A day for making steak au poivre, the French dish of steak crusted in cracked peppercorns with a pan sauce.

days.name: Step In A Puddle And Splash Your Friends Day
days.about: A playful day for jumping in puddles and splashing your friends, just for fun.

days.name: Stepfamily Day
days.about: A day for recognizing stepfamilies and blended families and the relationships between stepparents, stepchildren, and step-siblings.

days.name: Steve Jobs Day
days.about: Honors Apple co-founder Steve Jobs; California's governor declared a Steve Jobs Day shortly after he died in 2011.

days.name: Sticker Day
days.about: Honors R. Stanton Avery, who invented self-adhesive labels. People collect, trade, or hand out stickers.

days.name: Sticky Bun Day
days.about: A food day for sticky buns, the gooey caramel-and-nut-topped sweet rolls. People bake or buy some to eat.

days.name: Stop Food Waste Day
days.about: A campaign started by the food-service company Compass Group to cut down on wasted food. People plan meals, use leftovers, and learn ways to throw less food away.

days.name: Straw Hat Day
days.about: Traditionally marked the start of the season for wearing straw hats instead of felt ones. People bring out their straw hats for summer.

days.name: Strawberry Cream Pie Day
days.about: A food day for strawberry cream pie. People make or eat a slice.

days.name: Strawberry Day
days.about: A day for strawberries. People eat them fresh or in desserts.

days.name: Strawberry Ice Cream Day
days.about: A food day for strawberry ice cream. People have a scoop or two.

days.name: Strawberry Parfait Day
days.about: A food day for strawberry parfaits, layered with fruit, cream or yogurt, and sometimes granola. People make or order one.

days.name: Strawberry Sundae Day
days.about: A food day for ice cream sundaes topped with strawberries or strawberry sauce. People make or order one.

days.name: Stress Awareness Day
days.about: Started in the UK by the International Stress Management Association to draw attention to stress, especially at work. People and employers look at what causes stress and how to reduce it.

days.name: Stuffed Mushroom Day
days.about: A food day for stuffed mushrooms. People make or eat them as a snack or appetizer.

days.name: Stuffing Day
days.about: A food day for stuffing (or dressing), the bread-based side dish. People make a batch, often outside the holidays.

days.name: Submarine Day
days.about: Marks the U.S. Navy buying its first commissioned submarine, the USS Holland, in 1900. It honors submarines and the people who serve on them, not sandwiches.

days.name: SUDEP Action Day
days.about: Run by the charity SUDEP Action to raise awareness of Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy. People share information on epilepsy risks and safety and support bereaved families.

days.name: Sugar Cookie Day
days.about: A food day for sugar cookies. People bake, decorate, or share them.

days.name: Sun Screen Day
days.about: A reminder to protect your skin from the sun as summer starts. People put on sunscreen and stock up.

days.name: Sundae Day
days.about: A food day for ice cream sundaes. People build one with their favorite toppings.

days.name: Sunglasses Day
days.about: A reminder to wear sunglasses to protect your eyes from UV rays. People wear or buy a pair.

days.name: Superhero Day
days.about: Started by Marvel employees to honor superheroes, both fictional ones and real-life heroes. People dress up, read comics, or thank everyday heroes.

days.name: Superhuman Day
days.about: A day for honoring people with disabilities who have pushed past the challenges and stigma they face to go after their goals. People share their stories and recognize what they've achieved.

days.name: Superman Day
days.about: A day for fans of the comic book character Superman. People read the comics, watch the films, or wear the S logo.

days.name: Supernatural Day
days.about: A fan day for the TV series Supernatural, held on the anniversary of the show's pilot episode. Warner Bros., The CW and Hot Topic declared it in 2016, and fans mark it by rewatching episodes and sharing their love for the show.

days.name: Surf Day
days.about: Linked to International Surfing Day, started by the Surfrider Foundation and Surfing Magazine. People go surfing and do beach cleanups and ocean conservation work.

days.name: Surveillance Day
days.about: A day for thinking about and debating the use of surveillance cameras in public spaces, weighing safety against privacy. Some people mark it by waving at any surveillance camera they pass.

days.name: Suspender’s Day
days.about: A day for suspenders, the clothing accessory credited to Albert Thurston, who is said to have invented the modern version in the 1820s. People mark it by wearing a pair.

days.name: Swap Ideas Day
days.about: Encourages people to share and trade ideas. People brainstorm with others and swap suggestions.

days.name: Sweater Day
days.about: Started in Canada by WWF to save energy. People turn down the heat and wear a sweater instead.

days.name: Sweetest Day
days.about: A mostly Midwestern holiday that began in Cleveland in the 1920s. People give candy, cards, or small gifts to sweethearts and friends.

days.name: Swim a Lap Day
days.about: A day for getting in the pool and swimming a few laps as low-impact exercise. It's also a nudge to get kids into the water or signed up for swim lessons.

days.name: Sword Swallower’s Day
days.about: Organized by Sword Swallowers Association International to raise awareness of sword swallowing and its contributions to medicine. Performers put on shows and raise money for charity.

days.name: Symphonic Metal Day
days.about: A day for symphonic metal, the kind of heavy metal that brings in a full orchestra. People use it to find new bands in the genre or to go back to old favorites.

days.name: System Administrator Appreciation Day
days.about: Started by sysadmin Ted Kekatos to thank the people who keep computers and networks running. Coworkers thank their IT staff, often with cake or snacks.

days.name: Systems Engineer Day
days.about: A day to thank the systems engineers, architects and analysts who design and run complex systems. It's also a chance to learn what the job involves, and some schools hold career fairs to recruit for it.

days.name: S’mores Day
days.about: A food day for s'mores, made of toasted marshmallow and chocolate between graham crackers. People make them over a campfire or at home.

days.name: Table Shuffleboard Day
days.about: A day for table shuffleboard, the bar and game-room game where you slide weighted pucks down a long table. People play it with friends, and some bars let you play for free that day.

days.name: TableTop Day
days.about: Started by Geek & Sundry and Wil Wheaton's show TableTop to promote board games. People get together to play tabletop games, often at game stores.

days.name: Taco Day
days.about: A food day for tacos. People eat them, and restaurants often run deals.

days.name: Tailors Day
days.about: A day to thank the tailors who make and alter clothes so they fit right. People wear something tailored, or treat their tailor to lunch or a gift card.

days.name: Take A Hike Day
days.about: Encourages people to get outdoors. People go hiking on a local trail.

days.name: Take A Walk In The Park Day
days.about: Encourages people to get outside. People go for a stroll in a park.

days.name: Take A Wild Guess Day
days.about: A speaker named Jim Barber started this day after noticing that it falls on US tax day, when lots of people end up guessing on their tax forms. It's a lighthearted day for making guesses and hunches, like guessing how many jelly beans are in a jar.

days.name: Take Back the Lunch Break Day
days.about: Promoted by the paper-towel brand Tork to get workers away from their desks at midday. People take a real lunch break.

days.name: Take Your Cat to the Vet Day
days.about: A reminder that cats need regular vet checkups too. Owners book an exam for their cat.

days.name: Take Your Child To The Library Day
days.about: Started by librarians to get kids visiting libraries. Families go to the library, and libraries hold special events.

days.name: Take Your Dog To Work Day
days.about: Started by Pet Sitters International to promote pet adoption. Employers let staff bring their dogs to the office.

days.name: Take Your Houseplant For A Walk Day
days.about: A silly day for giving houseplants some fresh air and attention. People carry a potted plant around outside.

days.name: Take Your Parents To Lunch Day
days.about: A school-lunch event where parents or guardians come to their kid's school and eat lunch with them in the cafeteria. The idea is to show parents what goes into putting together a healthy school meal.

days.name: Take Your Webmaster To Lunch Day
days.about: A day for thanking the person who keeps your website running by taking them out for a meal.

days.name: Talk In An Elevator Day
days.about: A day for skipping the usual awkward silence in an elevator and starting a conversation with whoever is riding with you.

days.name: Talk Like A Grizzled Prospector Day
days.about: It marks the 1848 gold find at Sutter's Mill that started the California Gold Rush. People spend the day talking like an old-timey gold prospector.

days.name: Talk Like A Pirate Day
days.about: Started as a joke between two friends, John Baur and Mark Summers, and later spread online. People spend the day saying 'Ahoy, matey' and 'Arrr' and talking like movie pirates.

days.name: Talk Like Shakespeare Day
days.about: Held on Shakespeare's birthday as a playful nod to the Bard. People pepper their speech with 'thee,' 'thou,' and Elizabethan insults or quote his lines.

days.name: Tangible Karma Day
days.about: A day for clearing out things you don't use much and giving them to someone else so they get reused instead of thrown away. It's meant as a way to build good karma.

days.name: Tap Dance Day
days.about: Honors tap dancing as an American art form, held on the birthday of the dancer Bill 'Bojangles' Robinson. People go to tap shows, take a class, or watch old tap routines.

days.name: Tapioca Day
days.about: A food day for tapioca, the starch made from cassava root. People eat it in puddings, bubble tea pearls, or other dishes.

days.name: Tapioca Pudding Day
days.about: A food day for the creamy pudding made with tapioca pearls. People make a batch or eat a cup of it.

days.name: Tartan Day
days.about: Recognizes Scottish heritage, especially among Scottish Americans and Canadians, and is tied to the Declaration of Arbroath. People wear tartan and kilts, march in parades, and listen to bagpipes.

days.name: Tater Tot Day
days.about: A food day for the crispy little shredded potato nuggets. People eat them as a side or in tater tot casserole.

days.name: Tattoo Day
days.about: A day about tattoos and tattoo art. People show off their ink, and some get a new one.

days.name: Tattoo Removal Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of laser tattoo removal for people who regret a tattoo and to recognize the people who do the removals. Removal clinics often use it to promote treatments.

days.name: Tea Day
days.about: A day for tea. People brew a favorite cup, try a new variety, or have friends over for tea.

days.name: Teach Your Children to Save Day
days.about: Promoted by the American Bankers Association Foundation to teach kids about money. Bankers visit classrooms, and parents talk with their kids about saving.

days.name: Teacher Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for thanking teachers. Students and parents give them notes, small gifts, or treats.

days.name: Team Margot Stem Cell and Bone Marrow Awareness Day
days.about: Comes from the UK campaign started for Margot Martini, a little girl with leukemia who needed a stem cell donor. It encourages people to sign up to donor registries, which can save patients with blood cancers.

days.name: Techies Day
days.about: Recognizes the IT and technical workers who keep computers and systems running. People thank their tech support staff, and some schools use it to encourage students toward tech careers.

days.name: Techno Day
days.about: A day for techno and other electronic dance music, when people listen to it and learn more about the genre.

days.name: Teddy Bear Day
days.about: A day for the stuffed bear named after Teddy Roosevelt. People hug an old teddy or give one to a child.

days.name: Teddy Bear Picnic Day
days.about: Named after the old song 'The Teddy Bears' Picnic.' Kids, and sometimes libraries and zoos, hold picnics with their teddy bears along.

days.name: Teenager Workout Day
days.about: A day to push back against teenage obesity by getting teens to exercise and stay active, often with family or friends.

days.name: Tell A Fairy Tale Day
days.about: A day for reading or telling fairy tales. Parents and teachers share classic stories with kids, or people make up their own.

days.name: Tell A Joke Day
days.about: A day for telling jokes. People share their favorites to make others laugh.

days.name: Tell A Lie Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day for harmless fibs and tall tales. People tell playful lies that hurt no one.

days.name: Tell a Story Day
days.about: A day for storytelling. People read stories aloud, share family tales, or tell their own stories.

days.name: Tell An Old Joke Day
days.about: A day for groan-worthy classic jokes. People dust off the corny old ones everyone has heard.

days.name: Tell The Truth Day
days.about: A day for honesty. People try to be truthful in everything they say and maybe come clean about something.

days.name: Tempura Day
days.about: A food day for the Japanese dish of lightly battered, deep-fried seafood and vegetables. People eat it at a restaurant or fry some at home.

days.name: Tequila Day
days.about: A day for the Mexican agave spirit. People drink it straight or in margaritas and other cocktails.

days.name: Tessellation Day
days.about: Held on M.C. Escher's birthday to celebrate repeating shapes that tile a surface with no gaps. Students and teachers draw tessellations and look at Escher's art.

days.name: Thank A Letter Carrier Day
days.about: A day for thanking the people who deliver the mail. People leave a note, card, or small treat for their mail carrier.

days.name: Thank God It’s Monday Day
days.about: A day for starting the first work week of the new year, and Mondays in general, with energy and a positive attitude instead of dreading them.

days.name: Thank You Note Day
days.about: A day for writing handwritten thank-you notes. People send one to someone they've been meaning to thank.

days.name: Thank you Thursday
days.about: A social media habit of using Thursdays to thank someone or something publicly for their help, kindness, or contributions.

days.name: That Sucks! Day
days.about: A grumpy, tongue-in-cheek day started by Bruce Novotny of the That Sucks website. It's for owning up to the things in life that are lousy and having a good complain about them, and it falls on a date already known for bad luck, like tax deadlines and the Titanic sinking.

days.name: The Duchess Who Wasn’t Day
days.about: Held on Wallis Simpson's birthday. Edward VIII gave up the throne to marry her, but she was never granted the 'Her Royal Highness' title. People read up on the abdication story.

days.name: Therapeutic Massage Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness of massage as a health treatment for stress, pain, and recovery. People book a massage or learn about its benefits.

days.name: Thesaurus Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of Peter Mark Roget, who compiled the famous thesaurus. People look up synonyms and try out new words.

days.name: Third Shift Workers’ Day
days.about: Recognizes people who work overnight shifts, like nurses, factory workers, and security guards. People thank night workers for keeping things running while everyone else sleeps.

days.name: Thomas Jefferson Day
days.about: Held on Jefferson's birthday to remember the third US president and author of the Declaration of Independence. People read about his life and legacy.

days.name: Thread The Needle Day
days.about: A day built around the different meanings of 'thread the needle.' People thread an actual sewing needle, try a precise billiards or basketball shot, do the thread-the-needle yoga pose, or look for a middle path between two opposing views.

days.name: Three Kings Day
days.about: The Christian feast of Epiphany, marking the Magi's visit to the baby Jesus. Many Latin American and Spanish families exchange gifts and share a king cake with a hidden figurine.

days.name: Thrift Shop Day
days.about: A day for secondhand shopping. People browse thrift stores for bargains or donate things they no longer need.

days.name: Throw Out Your Leftovers Day
days.about: Falls after Thanksgiving, when the fridge is still full of holiday food. People clear out leftovers before they spoil.

days.name: Thunderbirds Day
days.about: Marks the premiere of Gerry Anderson's 1960s British puppet show 'Thunderbirds' about International Rescue. Fans rewatch episodes and share their memorabilia.

days.name: Tiara Day
days.about: Started by Barbara Bellissimo to remind women and girls that they deserve to feel like queens, inside and out. People wear tiaras, pamper themselves, or make tiaras out of craft supplies.

days.name: Tick Tock Day
days.about: Comes near the end of the year as a reminder that time is running out on that year's goals. People finish up tasks they meant to get done before the new year.

days.name: Tie One On Day
days.about: The day before Thanksgiving, for wearing an apron and giving a gift wrapped in one to someone in need.

days.name: Tim Tam Day
days.about: A day for Australia's chocolate-coated biscuit. People eat them or do the 'Tim Tam Slam,' sipping a hot drink through a biscuit like a straw.

days.name: Tin Can Day
days.about: Marks the US patent for the tin can, which changed how food is preserved. People think about canned food's history, and some donate canned goods.

days.name: Title Track Day
days.about: A day for title tracks, the songs that share their name with the album they're on. People spend the day listening only to title tracks.

days.name: Toast Day
days.about: A day for toasted bread. People make toast with their favorite toppings.

days.name: Toasted Marshmallow Day
days.about: A day for toasting marshmallows over a fire or flame, often to make s'mores.

days.name: Tofu Day
days.about: A day for tofu, the soybean curd. Fans and skeptics alike try new ways to cook and eat it, from crispy stir-fries to desserts.

days.name: Tolkien Reading Day
days.about: Started by the Tolkien Society, it encourages people to read and share favorite passages from J.R.R. Tolkien's books, often at schools, libraries and fan gatherings.

days.name: Tongue Twister Day
days.about: A day for practicing tongue twisters like "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers" and learning new ones, often with friends and family.

days.name: Tooth Fairy Day
days.about: A day about the tooth fairy tradition of leaving a lost baby tooth under the pillow, often used to get kids interested in looking after their teeth.

days.name: Toothache Day
days.about: A reminder to look after your teeth, with brushing, flossing and dental checkups, so you avoid toothaches.

days.name: Top 8 Challenge Day
days.about: A day to raise money and awareness for eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders (EGIDs). It was started by the Australian group ausEE, and people who sign up avoid the top 8 allergen foods for 24 hours.

days.name: Top Gun Day
days.about: A day for fans of the 1986 film Top Gun, marking its release, usually by rewatching it and quoting the lines.

days.name: Top Up Day
days.about: A day started by MobileRecharge to recognize people living abroad who send support back home. People top up the prepaid phones of friends and family in other countries, and MobileRecharge drops its fees for the day.

days.name: Tortellini Day
days.about: A day for eating tortellini, the small ring-shaped stuffed pasta from northern Italy.

days.name: Tortilla Chip Day
days.about: A day for eating tortilla chips, typically with salsa, guacamole or queso.

days.name: Tourism Day
days.about: A day, such as the UN's World Tourism Day, for recognizing the role of tourism in economies and cultures and for promoting travel.

days.name: Towel Day
days.about: A tribute to Douglas Adams, author of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Fans carry a towel around all day, following the book's advice.

days.name: Town Criers Day
days.about: A day to recognize town criers, the bell-ringing announcers who read news aloud in public, and their place in history.

days.name: Toy Camera Day
days.about: A day for getting out cheap, simple film cameras, like the ones in the Lomo trend, and taking pictures with them for fun, happy accidents included.

days.name: Toy Soldier Day
days.about: A day for classic toy soldiers, especially the little plastic ones that many kids grew up with. People get out old collections, play with them or set them up for display, and remember playing with them as kids.

days.name: Tradesmen Day
days.about: Created by IRWIN Tools to recognize skilled tradespeople like electricians, plumbers, carpenters and welders for the work they do.

days.name: Trail Mix Day
days.about: A day for making or snacking on trail mix, the mix of nuts, dried fruit and chocolate bits.

days.name: Trails Day
days.about: Organized by the American Hiking Society, it gets people out hiking, biking or riding on trails, and volunteering to maintain them.

days.name: Train Day
days.about: Promoted by Amtrak and tied to the anniversary of the transcontinental railroad's completion, it draws attention to rail travel with station events and train exhibits.

days.name: Train Your Brain Day
days.about: A reminder to give your mind a workout. People do puzzles and brain teasers, learn something new, or pick up habits that help keep them mentally sharp.

days.name: Tripe Day
days.about: Promoted somewhat tongue-in-cheek by a British tripe appreciation group, it encourages people to try eating tripe, the stomach lining of cattle.

days.name: Trivia Day
days.about: A day for trivia quizzes, sharing obscure facts and testing friends on random knowledge.

days.name: True Confessions Day
days.about: A day for owning up to secrets you've been keeping. People confess something to get rid of the guilt, ease their stress and be more honest with the people around them.

days.name: Tuba Day
days.about: Started in 1979 to recognize tuba players, who often get overlooked in bands and orchestras, with concerts and tuba events.

days.name: Tuberculosis Day
days.about: World TB Day marks the anniversary of Robert Koch's 1882 discovery of the TB bacterium and raises awareness of the disease and efforts to end it.

days.name: Tug-of-War Day
days.about: A day for the old team game where two sides pull on opposite ends of a rope. People get a group together and have a tug-of-war match.

days.name: Turkey Free Thanksgiving
days.about: Falls on Thanksgiving itself and asks people to leave turkey off the table. People serve a different main dish or a vegetarian meal instead.

days.name: Turkey Lovers’ Day
days.about: A day started by the National Turkey Federation to remind people that turkey isn't just for Thanksgiving. People put it on the summer menu, often grilling turkey burgers or turkey dogs with friends.

days.name: Turkey Vulture Day
days.about: Also called Buzzards Day, it's for appreciating turkey vultures, scavengers that get little credit but do an important job by cleaning up dead animals. People learn about the birds, and some go to see them come back to roost, as people do in Hinckley, Ohio.

days.name: Turtle Day
days.about: World Turtle Day was started by American Tortoise Rescue to raise awareness of turtles and tortoises and help protect them and their habitats.

days.name: TV Dinner Day
days.about: A nod to the frozen TV dinner popularized by Swanson in the 1950s, usually marked by eating one in front of the television.

days.name: TV Talk Show Host Day
days.about: A day for recognizing TV talk show hosts, often linked to Johnny Carson, and what they've added to television. People watch their favorite talk shows or old clips of famous hosts.

days.name: Tweed Day
days.about: A day about tweed. It's either the wool fabric or William "Boss" Tweed, the corrupt New York politician born on this day. People wear tweed clothes or read up on Boss Tweed's history.

days.name: Twilight Zone Day
days.about: A day for fans of Rod Serling's The Twilight Zone, often marked by watching episodes or a marathon.

days.name: Two Different Colored Shoes Day
days.about: Speaker Arlene Kaiser started this day to honor what makes each person unique and different from others. People wear two shoes that don't match in color.

days.name: Typewriter Day
days.about: World Typewriter Day marks the patent of an early typewriter by Christopher Latham Sholes and appreciates the machine and its history.

days.name: Ugly Christmas Sweater Day
days.about: A day for wearing a gaudy holiday sweater to work or school. It's often tied to fundraising, notably for Save the Children.

days.name: Umbrella Cover Day
days.about: A day for noticing the little sleeves that umbrellas come in, started by the founder of the Umbrella Cover Museum in Maine. People visit the museum or look at its exhibits online, dig up old umbrella covers at home, or donate one to the museum.

days.name: Umbrella Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the umbrella, a simple and useful invention for rain and sun.

days.name: Uncommon Instrument Awareness Day
days.about: A day for paying attention to unusual musical instruments. People play or listen to instruments they don't usually come across, and some make their own.

days.name: Underdog Day
days.about: Started by Peter Moeller to honor the sidekicks, second fiddles and unsung people who do the work while others get the credit.

days.name: Underwear Day
days.about: Started by the retailer Freshpair, it's a light-hearted day about underwear, often used to promote buying new pairs.

days.name: Unfriend Day
days.about: Proposed by Jimmy Kimmel, it's a day for trimming your Facebook friend list of people you don't really know.

days.name: Unicorn Day
days.about: A whimsical day for unicorn fans, with unicorn-themed crafts, clothes and treats, especially popular with kids.

days.name: Unique Names Day
days.about: A day about rare and unusual names and the people who have them. It started as one of the days of Celebrate Your Name Week, and people use it to recognize uncommon names and the stories behind them.

days.name: United Nations Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the UN Charter taking effect in 1945, with events highlighting the UN's work and purpose.

days.name: United States Marine Corps Birthday
days.about: Marks the founding of the Continental Marines in 1775. Marines worldwide hold birthday balls and a ceremonial cake-cutting.

days.name: Universal Children’s Day
days.about: A UN-backed day for promoting children's welfare and rights, tied to the anniversaries of the Declaration and Convention on the Rights of the Child. Schools, charities, and governments hold events and campaigns about kids' wellbeing.

days.name: Upcycling Day
days.about: A day to get people upcycling, which means turning old things they'd otherwise throw away into something new and useful. One example is making planters out of old plastic bottles.

days.name: Upsy Daisy Day
days.about: Stephanie West Allen started this day in 2003 to encourage people to get out of bed each morning in a positive, grateful mood. On it, people try to start the day with a good attitude.

days.name: Use Less Stuff Day
days.about: A day to cut down on waste, for example by buying less, skipping excess packaging, and reusing or recycling what you already have.

days.name: Use Your Common Sense Day
days.about: A day created by career coach Bud Bilanich as a reminder to stop and think things through, using plain practical judgment in everyday decisions.

days.name: V-J Day
days.about: Marks Victory over Japan, the end of World War II. People remember those who served and the war's end with ceremonies and reflection.

days.name: Valentino Day
days.about: A day remembering the silent film star Rudolph Valentino on the anniversary of his death. People watch his films, read about him, or go to the yearly memorial service at his crypt in Hollywood Forever Cemetery.

days.name: Vanilla Cupcake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating vanilla cupcakes.

days.name: Vanilla Custard Day
days.about: A day for making or eating vanilla custard.

days.name: Vanilla Ice Cream Day
days.about: A day for having a scoop of plain vanilla ice cream, on its own or as a base for toppings and desserts.

days.name: Vanilla Milkshake Day
days.about: A day for treating yourself to a vanilla milkshake.

days.name: Vascular Birthmarks Awareness Day
days.about: Raises awareness of vascular birthmarks such as hemangiomas and port-wine stains, and of the support and treatment available for people who have them.

days.name: VCR Day
days.about: A nostalgic nod to the video cassette recorder. People dig out old VHS tapes or reminisce about taping shows.

days.name: Vermouth Day
days.about: A day for appreciating vermouth, the herb-flavored fortified wine, by sipping it on its own or in cocktails like a martini or negroni.

days.name: Vesuvius Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of Mount Vesuvius erupting in 79 AD and burying Pompeii and Herculaneum. People read about or remember the disaster.

days.name: Vet Nurse Day
days.about: A day for thanking veterinary nurses for the care they give animals and the support they give vets.

days.name: Veterinary Day
days.about: Promoted by the World Veterinary Association to recognize vets and their work for animal and public health, often with a yearly theme.

days.name: Vichyssoise Day
days.about: A day for making or eating vichyssoise, the chilled leek and potato soup.

days.name: Video Games Day
days.about: A day for playing video games and appreciating gaming, whether solo, with friends, or revisiting old favorites.

days.name: Vinegar Day
days.about: A day for appreciating vinegar and its many uses, from cooking and pickling to cleaning.

days.name: Vinyl Record Day
days.about: Started to appreciate vinyl records and their cultural history. People spin their records, visit record shops, or add to their collections.

days.name: Violin Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the violin, whether by listening to violin music or playing one.

days.name: Virtual Assistants Day
days.about: Recognizes freelance virtual assistants who handle administrative and other work for clients remotely, and thanks them for it.

days.name: Virtually Hug a Virtual Assistant Day
days.about: A day for thanking the remote virtual assistants who help people and businesses with admin work. People send them a 'virtual hug' by email, text or video chat.

days.name: Virus Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for learning about viruses as more than just germs, including their role in nature and their use in science and medicine. No one knows for sure who started it.

days.name: Visit The Zoo Day
days.about: A day for going to the zoo to see the animals and learn about wildlife and conservation.

days.name: Visit Your Local Quilt Shop Day
days.about: Encourages quilters to stop by and support their independent local quilt shop, often with in-store events or sales.

days.name: Visit Your Relatives Day
days.about: A day for making time to see family members you don't visit often.

days.name: Vitamin C Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of why vitamin C matters for health, including its role in supporting the immune system.

days.name: Vlogging Day
days.about: A day for recognizing people who make video blogs, and for nudging others to pick up a camera and try sharing their own stories in video.

days.name: Vodka Day
days.about: A day for having vodka, neat or in a cocktail, responsibly.

days.name: Volunteer Recognition Day
days.about: A day for thanking volunteers for the time and work they give to their communities and organizations.

days.name: Waffle Day
days.about: A day for eating waffles. It has Swedish roots, where Waffle Day grew out of a pun on a Lady Day church holiday, and in the US it's also tied to the waffle iron patent.

days.name: Waffle Iron Day
days.about: Marks the 1869 US patent for the waffle iron. People make waffles at home.

days.name: Waiters Day
days.about: A day for appreciating waiters and waitresses, typically by being a gracious customer and tipping well.

days.name: Waitstaff Day
days.about: A day for thanking restaurant servers for their hard work, often with kind words and a generous tip.

days.name: Walk Around Things Day
days.about: A lighthearted day about getting around obstacles. People take it literally by walking around objects, or figuratively by sidestepping problems or topics they'd rather avoid for now.

days.name: Walk On Stilts Day
days.about: A day for stilt walking, an old skill you mostly see in parades and at the circus. It encourages people to try stilts for fun or even as a career, and it was started by stilt walker Bill "Stretch" Coleman.

days.name: Walk On Your Wild Side Day
days.about: A day for stepping outside your comfort zone and doing something unusual or adventurous that you've always wanted to try.

days.name: Walk to Work Day
days.about: Encourages people to walk to work, or partway, instead of driving, for health and the environment.

days.name: Walking the Dog Day
days.about: A day for taking your dog out for a good walk, for both of your health.

days.name: Walt Disney Day
days.about: Marks Walt Disney's birthday. People remember his work with films, animation, and theme parks.

days.name: Wash Your Nose Day
days.about: A day started by the sinus-care company Xlear to remind people that rinsing your nose is as important for health and hygiene as washing your hands. People mark it by cleaning their nasal passages, for example with a saline rinse.

days.name: Water a Flower Day
days.about: A reminder to water your flowers and give your garden and houseplants some care. Some people also bring freshly watered flowers to a friend who could use cheering up.

days.name: Water Monitoring Day
days.about: Encourages people to test the quality of local streams, lakes, and rivers, often with simple test kits, to raise awareness of clean water.

days.name: Watermelon Day
days.about: A day for eating watermelon.

days.name: Wave All Your Fingers At Your Neighbors Day
days.about: A day for being friendly with your neighbors. You give them a big wave with all five fingers, kids and adults alike.

days.name: We Jump The World Day
days.about: A day for parkour, started in 2016 by the group Team Farang. People go out on their own or with their crew to practice moving over and around obstacles.

days.name: We Love Memoirs Day
days.about: Grew out of the We Love Memoirs online community of readers and memoir writers. It's a day for reading, writing, and sharing memoirs.

days.name: Wear Brown Shoes Day
days.about: A day for wearing brown shoes, which were once seen as less classy than black ones. People wear their brown shoes, dressy or casual, or buy a new pair.

days.name: Wear Red Day
days.about: Run by the American Heart Association to raise awareness of heart disease in women. People wear red to show support.

days.name: Wear Something Gaudy Day
days.about: A day for putting on your loudest, flashiest clothes and accessories. It's said to have started with Larry Dallas's over-the-top outfits on the TV show Three's Company.

days.name: Wear Your Pajamas To Work Day
days.about: A day for showing up to work in your pajamas, or working from home in them, just for comfort and a laugh.

days.name: Weatherperson’s Day
days.about: Honors meteorologists and weather forecasters. It falls on the birthday of John Jeffries, one of America's first weather observers.

days.name: Web Designer Day
days.about: A day for recognizing the people who design how websites look and work. People thank the web designers they know and pay attention to the work behind the sites they use every day.

days.name: WebMistress Day
days.about: Kat Valentine started this day in 2016 to recognize women who design, build and maintain websites and to back the job title "webmistress." People use it to give credit to women in web development and to encourage more women to get into the field.

days.name: Wedding Planning Day
days.about: The Knot started this day to mark the move from proposal season to wedding planning season. Newly engaged couples use it to get going on their plans, like setting a budget, booking vendors and picking dates.

days.name: Weed Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for appreciating weeds, the plants. People learn which common weeds are edible, medicinal or useful, like dandelions.

days.name: Weigh-In Day
days.about: Kellogg's Special K brand started this day for checking your weight and health after the holidays. People step on the scale and set new-year goals to eat better and exercise more.

days.name: Weights & Measures Day
days.about: Marks the 1875 signing of the Metre Convention, which set up international standards for measurement. It recognizes the people who keep scales and measures accurate.

days.name: Welsh Rarebit Day
days.about: A day for making and eating Welsh rarebit, a savory cheese sauce, often with ale and mustard, poured over toast.

days.name: Western Monarch Day
days.about: California set up this day to draw attention to western monarch butterflies, which spend the winter along the coast and whose numbers are dropping. People visit the places where the butterflies spend the winter and do things to help them, like planting milkweed and other plants they need.

days.name: What If Cats and Dogs Had Opposable Thumbs Day
days.about: A tongue-in-cheek day for imagining the mischief pets could get into if they had thumbs, and for appreciating them while they don't.

days.name: Whipped Cream Day
days.about: A day for enjoying whipped cream. It falls on the birthday of Aaron Lapin, who invented Reddi-wip.

days.name: Whiskey Sour Day
days.about: A day for mixing and drinking whiskey sours, the classic cocktail of whiskey, lemon juice and sugar.

days.name: White Cane Safety Day
days.about: A U.S. day recognizing people who are blind or visually impaired and the white cane as a symbol of independence. It also reminds drivers to yield to people using one.

days.name: White Chocolate Cheesecake Day
days.about: A day for baking or eating white chocolate cheesecake.

days.name: White Chocolate Day
days.about: A day for eating white chocolate or baking treats with it.

days.name: White Day
days.about: Observed in Japan, Korea and other parts of East Asia one month after Valentine's Day. People who got Valentine's gifts, traditionally men, give return gifts like white chocolate or candy.

days.name: White Shirt Day
days.about: Marks the end of the 1937 Flint sit-down strike that won recognition for the auto workers' union. Workers wear white shirts to show labor solidarity.

days.name: White Wine Day
days.about: A day for drinking and appreciating white wine.

days.name: Wienerschnitzel Day
days.about: A day for eating Wiener schnitzel, the Austrian dish of thin, breaded and fried veal cutlet.

days.name: Wife Appreciation Day
days.about: A day for husbands and families to show wives some extra thanks, through gifts, help around the house or time together.

days.name: Wiggle Your Toes Day
days.about: A light-hearted day for paying a little attention to your feet. People take off their shoes and socks and wiggle their toes to relax and ease some stress.

days.name: Wildfire Community Preparedness Day
days.about: Promoted by the National Fire Protection Association to get neighbors working on projects that lower wildfire risk, like clearing brush and debris around homes.

days.name: Wildlife Day
days.about: Started in memory of Steve Irwin to raise awareness of wildlife and the threats to it. People learn about animals or support conservation groups.

days.name: Wine and Cheese Day
days.about: A day for pairing wine with cheese, often with a tasting or a spread at home.

days.name: Wine Day
days.about: A day for enjoying wine, whether a favorite bottle, a new one or a winery visit.

days.name: Winnie the Pooh Day
days.about: Falls on the birthday of A. A. Milne, Pooh's author. People read the stories, especially with kids.

days.name: Winston Churchill Day
days.about: Marks the day in 1963 when Winston Churchill was made an honorary U.S. citizen. It's a day to remember him and his role in World War II.

days.name: Wobbly Wednesday
days.about: An awareness and fundraising day for nystagmus, an eye condition that causes involuntary eye movements, started by the Nystagmus Network. People raise money and spread the word, and schools often take part.

days.name: Women in Engineering Day
days.about: Started by the UK's Women's Engineering Society to highlight women working in engineering and encourage more girls to go into the field.

days.name: Women’s Equality Day
days.about: Marks the 19th Amendment giving U.S. women the right to vote. It's a day to reflect on progress toward gender equality and the work still left.

days.name: Women’s Healthy Weight Day
days.about: Part of Healthy Weight Week, it pushes back on dieting and weight prejudice. It encourages women to focus on healthy habits and accept their bodies at their natural size.

days.name: Wonderful Weirdos Day
days.about: A day for embracing your quirks and the things that make you different. People feel free to be their odd, eccentric selves and appreciate the same in others.

days.name: Won’t You Be My Neighbor Day
days.about: Falls on Fred Rogers' birthday and honors his show Mister Rogers' Neighborhood. People are encouraged to be kind and neighborly, sometimes by wearing a sweater.

days.name: Work From Home Day
days.about: A day to promote flexible working and show that letting people work from home now and then is good for both employers and staff. Office workers skip the commute and work from home for the day.

days.name: Work Like a Dog Day
days.about: A day for recognizing people who work especially hard, and sometimes the working dogs who do too.

days.name: Work Your Proper Hours Day
days.about: A UK union campaign day about unpaid overtime. Workers are urged to take a full lunch break and leave on time.

days.name: Workers’ Memorial Day
days.about: Remembers workers who were killed, injured or made ill by their jobs, and pushes for safer workplaces.

days.name: Working Naked Day
days.about: Started by home-office expert Lisa Kanarek as a joking nod to people who work from home. It's about the freedom and casualness of the home office.

days.name: Working Parents Day
days.about: A day to recognize parents and stepparents who juggle a job and raising a family. People thank the working parents they know, and some employers use it to offer more support to staff with kids.

days.name: World Afro Day
days.about: Founded in the UK to celebrate Afro-textured hair and culture and to fight discrimination against natural hair at school and work.

days.name: World AIDS Day
days.about: A global day to raise awareness of HIV and AIDS, remember those who have died, and support people living with HIV. Many people wear a red ribbon.

days.name: World Alzheimer’s Day
days.about: Raises awareness of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias and challenges the stigma around them. It also supports patients and caregivers.

days.name: World Animal Day
days.about: Held on the feast of St. Francis of Assisi, patron saint of animals, to raise awareness of animal welfare. People support shelters, adopt pets or have animals blessed.

days.name: World Aquatic Animal Day
days.about: Started by a law school animal law clinic to draw attention to fish and other water animals and the threats they face.

days.name: World Arthritis Day
days.about: Raises awareness of arthritis and other musculoskeletal diseases, encouraging early diagnosis and support for people living with them.

days.name: World Autism Day
days.about: The UN-recognized day for autism awareness and acceptance. Many people promote understanding and inclusion of autistic people.

days.name: World Backup Day
days.about: Reminds people to back up their computers, phones and important files before data gets lost. It falls the day before April Fools'.

days.name: World Baking Day
days.about: Encourages people to try baking something, often something new, and share it with others.

days.name: World Bartender Day
days.about: A day to recognize bartenders and the skill and hospitality they bring to their work. People visit a bar, try something the bartender recommends, and leave a good tip.

days.name: World Bee Day
days.about: A UN day, proposed by Slovenia, for raising awareness of bees and other pollinators and why they matter for food. People learn about beekeeping, plant bee-friendly flowers, or buy local honey.

days.name: World Bicycle Day
days.about: A UN day recognizing the bicycle as a cheap, clean, healthy way to get around. People ride to work or school, join group rides, and push for better cycling infrastructure.

days.name: World Blood Donor Day
days.about: A WHO day to thank blood donors and encourage more people to give blood regularly. Blood services run drives and campaigns around it.

days.name: World Book Day
days.about: A UNESCO day promoting reading, books, and copyright. In the UK and Ireland it's a school event where kids dress up as book characters and get tokens toward a free book.

days.name: World Book Night
days.about: A UK and Ireland event where volunteers hand out free books to people who don't read much, to get more adults reading.

days.name: World Braille Day
days.about: Held on Louis Braille's birthday to raise awareness of braille and the importance of accessible information for blind and partially sighted people.

days.name: World Bratwurst Day
days.about: A day devoted to bratwurst, the spiced German sausage. People grill, boil or fry brats and eat them on a roll with mustard or with sauerkraut.

days.name: World Breast Pumping Day
days.about: A day to recognize the time and effort that moms who pump breast milk put in. People use it to support and thank pumping mothers and to talk about the challenges they face.

days.name: World Calligraphy Day
days.about: A day for promoting calligraphy, the art of decorative handwriting. People pick up a pen and practice their lettering, or go to workshops, demos and exhibitions.

days.name: World Cancer Day
days.about: An international day led by the Union for International Cancer Control to raise awareness of cancer and push for better prevention, detection, and treatment.

days.name: World Car Free Day
days.about: A day for leaving the car at home and walking, cycling, or taking transit instead. Some cities close streets to traffic for it.

days.name: World Cerebral Palsy Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of cerebral palsy and support the rights and inclusion of people living with it. Many people wear green.

days.name: World Cocktail Day
days.about: Marks the anniversary of the first printed definition of the word 'cocktail' in 1806. People mix or order a classic cocktail.

days.name: World Compliment Day
days.about: Started in the Netherlands, it's a day for giving people sincere compliments, with no gifts or money involved.

days.name: World Consumer Rights Day
days.about: Organized by Consumers International, inspired by JFK's 1962 speech on consumer rights, to push for fair treatment and protection of shoppers.

days.name: World Creativity and Innovation Day
days.about: A UN-recognized day encouraging people to use creative thinking to solve problems, with workshops and brainstorming events.

days.name: World Diabetes Day
days.about: Held on Frederick Banting's birthday (he co-discovered insulin) to raise awareness of diabetes. Its symbol is a blue circle and landmarks are lit up blue.

days.name: World Donkey Day
days.about: A day to appreciate donkeys and the hard work they do for people around the world, and to raise awareness of their welfare.

days.name: World Down Syndrome Day
days.about: Held on 3/21 to represent the three copies of chromosome 21, it raises awareness and supports inclusion of people with Down syndrome. Many people wear mismatched socks.

days.name: World Dream Day
days.about: A day for saying out loud what you dream of doing and taking a first step toward it. People write down a 'dream declaration' and join live or online events with others working on their goals.

days.name: World Duchenne Awareness Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a genetic muscle-wasting disease that mostly affects boys, and support research.

days.name: World Ego Awareness Day
days.about: A day started by the nonprofit Ego Awareness Movement to help people notice how their ego shapes their thoughts and behavior. People use it to check whether their ego is getting in the way and to read up on the topic, for example through the movement's free online resources.

days.name: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day
days.about: A UN day to draw attention to the abuse, neglect, and exploitation of older people and how to prevent it. Supporters often wear purple.

days.name: World Elephant Day
days.about: Started in 2012 to raise awareness of threats to elephants like poaching and habitat loss, and support conservation.

days.name: World Emoji Day
days.about: Started by Emojipedia's founder, a day for having fun with emoji, and when new emoji are often announced. It's on July 17 because that's the date shown on the calendar emoji.

days.name: World Environment Day
days.about: The UN's main day for environmental awareness, with a different theme and host country each year. People do cleanups, tree plantings, and similar action.

days.name: World Facilities Management Day
days.about: A day recognizing the people who manage and maintain buildings and workplaces, and the role they play in keeping things running.

days.name: World Farm Animals Day
days.about: Held on Gandhi's birthday by animal rights groups to mourn and draw attention to animals raised and killed for food. People hold vigils and promote plant-based eating.

days.name: World Fiddle Day
days.about: Started in Ireland and tied to the anniversary of Stradivari's death, a day when fiddlers gather to play together, give lessons, and share fiddle music.

days.name: World Food Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization and focuses on ending hunger and improving food security. Groups hold food drives and events.

days.name: World Freedom Day
days.about: A US-proclaimed day marking the fall of the Berlin Wall and the end of communism in Eastern Europe, honoring democracy and freedom.

days.name: World Gin Day
days.about: Started by a gin fan in 2009, a day for enjoying gin, with bars and distilleries running tastings and cocktail specials.

days.name: World Giraffe Day
days.about: Held on the longest day of the year for the animal with the longest neck, it raises awareness of declining giraffe numbers and supports conservation.

days.name: World Gratitude Day
days.about: Started in 1965 at a meditation gathering at the UN, it's a day for appreciating the good things in life and thanking people.

days.name: World Green Roof Day
days.about: A day for pointing out green roofs, which are roofs covered in plants, and what they do for people and nature, such as cooling cities and supporting wildlife. People post photos of green roofs on social media and go to related events and get-togethers.

days.name: World Habitat Day
days.about: A UN day about the state of towns and cities and everyone's right to adequate housing and shelter.

days.name: World Health Day
days.about: Marks the founding anniversary of the World Health Organization, with a different global health theme highlighted each year.

days.name: World Heart Day
days.about: Run by the World Heart Federation to raise awareness of heart disease and stroke and encourage heart-healthy habits.

days.name: World Hello Day
days.about: Started in 1973 in response to the Yom Kippur War, it promotes peace through communication. The idea is to greet at least ten people.

days.name: World Hemophilia Day
days.about: Organized by the World Federation of Hemophilia to raise awareness of hemophilia and other bleeding disorders. Landmarks are often lit red.

days.name: World Hepatitis Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of Baruch Blumberg, who discovered the hepatitis B virus, to promote testing, vaccination, and treatment for viral hepatitis.

days.name: World Heritage Day
days.about: Also called International Day for Monuments and Sites, it promotes protecting historic buildings and cultural heritage. Sites often offer free tours.

days.name: World Homeless Day
days.about: A day to draw attention to homelessness and get people involved in helping, through volunteering or donating to local shelters.

days.name: World Honey Bee Day
days.about: Started by US beekeepers to promote beekeeping and honey bees, with hive open days, honey tastings, and talks.

days.name: World Human Spirit Day
days.about: A day for reflecting on your inner life and spirituality and appreciating the human capacity for kindness and resilience.

days.name: World Humanist Day
days.about: Held around the June solstice by humanist groups to promote reason, ethics without religion, and human rights.

days.name: World Hypertension Day
days.about: Run by the World Hypertension League to encourage people to get their blood pressure checked and learn how to control it.

days.name: World Industrial Design Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the World Design Organization and highlights how industrial design shapes the products we use every day.

days.name: World Introvert Day
days.about: Started by a German psychologist and held just after the holiday season, it's about understanding introverts and letting them recharge in peace.

days.name: World Jump Day
days.about: A 2006 art project/prank that asked millions of people to jump at the same moment to supposedly shift the Earth's orbit and fix global warming.

days.name: World Kindness Day
days.about: A day started by the World Kindness Movement to encourage everyday acts of kindness. People do small good deeds for strangers, friends and their communities.

days.name: World Laughter Day
days.about: Started by Dr. Madan Kataria, founder of laughter yoga, to promote laughter for health and peace. People gather for group laughter sessions, often in parks.

days.name: World Lindy Hop Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of dancer Frankie Manning to honor the swing dance he helped popularize. Dancers hold social dances, workshops and flash mobs.

days.name: World Lion Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of falling wild lion numbers and the threats they face. People share facts and support conservation groups working to protect lions.

days.name: World Lung Cancer Day
days.about: An awareness day for lung cancer, the deadliest cancer worldwide. People promote early screening, quitting smoking, and support for patients and research.

days.name: World Lupus Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of lupus, an autoimmune disease that is often misunderstood and hard to diagnose. Groups push for better research, diagnosis and patient care.

days.name: World Maths Day
days.about: Originally an online mental arithmetic competition run by Mathletics, where students around the world race each other at math problems. Schools use it to make maths fun.

days.name: World Meditation Day
days.about: A day declared by the United Nations to recognize meditation's benefits for mental health and well-being. People take time to meditate, alone or in group sessions.

days.name: World Mental Health Day
days.about: Started by the World Federation for Mental Health to raise awareness of mental health issues and reduce stigma. Organizations run campaigns and people are encouraged to talk openly and seek support.

days.name: World Milk Day
days.about: Set up by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization to recognize milk as a global food and the dairy industry. Farmers and dairy groups hold events promoting milk and dairy farming.

days.name: World Mosquito Day
days.about: Marks Sir Ronald Ross's discovery that female mosquitoes transmit malaria. It's used to raise awareness and funds for fighting malaria and other mosquito-borne diseases.

days.name: World Motorcycle Day
days.about: A day for motorcycles and the people who ride them. Riders go out on their bikes, often in group rides, and spend time with other people from the riding community.

days.name: World Music Day
days.about: Began in France as the Fête de la Musique, when musicians of all levels play free public concerts. Cities around the world now host street performances and open-air shows.

days.name: World NGO Day
