days.about: A day to recognize the work of non-governmental and nonprofit organizations. People learn about NGOs, volunteer, and thank those who work in the sector.

days.name: World Nutella Day
days.about: Started by blogger Sara Rosso as a fan day for the hazelnut chocolate spread. People eat Nutella and share recipes and photos online.

days.name: World Oceans Day
days.about: A UN-recognized day for appreciating and protecting the oceans. People join beach cleanups, learn about marine life and support ocean conservation.

days.name: World Octopus Day
days.about: A day to appreciate octopuses and their intelligence and odd biology. Aquariums and nature fans share facts and hold educational events.

days.name: World Orphans Day
days.about: A day to draw attention to the problems faced by orphaned and displaced children around the world. People are encouraged to help, for example by supporting organizations that care for these children.

days.name: World Ozone Day
days.about: The UN's day for preserving the ozone layer, marking the signing of the Montreal Protocol. It highlights efforts to phase out ozone-depleting chemicals.

days.name: World Parkinson’s Disease Day
days.about: Held on the birthday of Dr. James Parkinson, who first described the disease, to raise awareness of Parkinson's. The red tulip is its symbol, and groups fundraise for research and support.

days.name: World Party Day
days.about: Also called P-Day, it was started in 1996 around the idea that everyone has a right to fun, peace and life. People around the world set their problems aside and throw or join parties together.

days.name: World Pasta Day
days.about: Started by pasta makers to promote pasta as a healthy, affordable food. People cook and share pasta dishes.

days.name: World Penguin Day
days.about: Timed with the yearly northward migration of Adélie penguins in Antarctica, it's a day to learn about penguins and the threats they face. Zoos and aquariums hold events.

days.name: World Pharmacists Day
days.about: Started by the International Pharmaceutical Federation to recognize pharmacists' role in health care. Pharmacies and health groups thank pharmacists and promote their work.

days.name: World Physical Therapy Day
days.about: A day set by the global physiotherapy federation to recognize physical therapists and their work. Clinics run awareness campaigns about movement, rehab and staying active.

days.name: World Piano Day
days.about: Started by pianist Nils Frahm on the 88th day of the year, for the piano's 88 keys. Pianists hold concerts and people play or listen to piano music.

days.name: World Play Your Ukulele Day
days.about: A day for getting out your ukulele and playing it, started in 2011 by Mike Lynch ("Ukulele Mike"). People strum along on their own or join other players to make music together.

days.name: World Plumbing Day
days.about: Started by the World Plumbing Council to highlight how plumbing and clean water protect public health. Plumbing groups run awareness and community events.

days.name: World Poetry Day
days.about: Declared by UNESCO to support poetry and the languages it is written in. People hold readings and share poems.

days.name: World Population Day
days.about: A UN day to draw attention to global population issues such as family planning, maternal health and gender equality. It started after the world population hit five billion.

days.name: World Porridge Day
days.about: Run by the charity Mary's Meals, which feeds schoolchildren a daily meal, often porridge. People eat porridge and raise money for school feeding programs.

days.name: World Post Day
days.about: Marks the founding of the Universal Postal Union, recognizing the role of postal services. Post offices hold events and sometimes issue special stamps.

days.name: World Prematurity Day
days.about: A day to raise awareness of premature birth and support preterm babies and their families. Landmarks are lit purple and groups share stories and fundraise.

days.name: World Product Day
days.about: A day for people who work in product management and product development, organized by Mind the Product's ProductTank community. Product people in cities around the world gather for meetups, talks and networking.

days.name: World Productivity Day
days.about: A day for thinking about how to get things done more efficiently at work and at home, started by the World Confederation of Productivity Science. Businesses and individuals use it to review their habits and look for ways to work better.

days.name: World Quality Day
days.about: A day to promote quality management in business and organizations. Companies recognize their quality teams and share improvement work.

days.name: World Rabies Day
days.about: Held on the anniversary of Louis Pasteur's death, who made the first rabies vaccine, to promote rabies prevention. Communities run pet vaccination drives and education campaigns.

days.name: World Rainforest Day
days.about: Started by the Rainforest Partnership to raise awareness of rainforests and the need to protect them. People learn about deforestation and support conservation groups.

days.name: World Ranger Day
days.about: Started by the International Ranger Federation to honor park and wildlife rangers, especially those killed or injured on duty. People hold memorials and thank rangers.

days.name: World Rat Day
days.about: A day for pet rat owners and fans to show appreciation for rats as companions. People share photos and try to counter rats' bad reputation.

days.name: World Read Aloud Day
days.about: Started by the literacy group LitWorld to promote reading aloud and literacy as a right for everyone. Schools and families read stories aloud together.

days.name: World Refrigeration Day
days.about: Held on Lord Kelvin's birthday to recognize the role of refrigeration, air conditioning and heat pumps in modern life. Industry groups promote careers and awareness in the field.

days.name: World Refugee Day
days.about: A UN day honoring refugees and the strength of people forced to flee their homes. Events raise awareness and support for refugees.

days.name: World Rhino Day
days.about: Started by WWF South Africa to raise awareness of the five rhino species and the poaching threat they face. People support anti-poaching and conservation efforts.

days.name: World Samosa Day
days.about: A day devoted to the samosa, the fried triangular pastry with a savory filling. People eat samosas, try one for the first time, or share some with friends.

days.name: World Scout Scarf Day
days.about: A day when current and former Scouts wear their scout scarf (neckerchief) in public to show pride in Scouting and the memories it gave them.

days.name: World Sickle Cell Awareness Day
days.about: A UN-recognized day to raise awareness of sickle cell disease, an inherited blood disorder. Groups push for better diagnosis, treatment and support for patients.

days.name: World Sketchnote Day
days.about: A day for sketchnoting, the practice of taking visual notes with drawings and handwriting. People make and share sketchnotes online.

days.name: World Sleep Day
days.about: Organized by the World Sleep Society to raise awareness of the importance of good sleep and sleep disorders. Sleep experts share advice and hold events.

days.name: World Smile Day
days.about: Started by Harvey Ball, the artist who created the yellow smiley face, as a day for smiles and acts of kindness. People do a kind act to help someone smile.

days.name: World Snake Day
days.about: A day for learning about snakes and their role in nature, aimed at easing fear of them and supporting their conservation.

days.name: World Softball Day
days.about: A day for promoting softball, set up by the sport's international federation to mark the 1991 decision to add women's softball to the Olympics. Players and fans hold games and events to get more people, especially kids, into the sport.

days.name: World Soil Day
days.about: A UN day highlighting healthy soil and sustainable soil management, marked with talks, farm events and campaigns about soil loss.

days.name: World Speech Day
days.about: A day when people around the world give short public speeches on ideas they care about, at small local events open to anyone.

days.name: World Standards Day
days.about: A day from the international standards bodies (ISO, IEC, ITU) honoring the people who write technical standards and explaining why shared standards matter.

days.name: World Stationery Day
days.about: A day promoting pens, paper and notebooks and the habit of writing by hand, often marked by sending handwritten notes.

days.name: World Storytelling Day
days.about: A day around the spring equinox when people hold storytelling events and tell stories aloud, often around a shared theme.

days.name: World Students’ Day
days.about: A day honoring students, held on the birthday of former Indian president A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, who was devoted to students and education.

days.name: World Suicide Prevention Day
days.about: A day from the International Association for Suicide Prevention and the WHO to raise awareness about suicide, reduce stigma and point people toward help.

days.name: World Table Tennis Day
days.about: A day from the international table tennis federation encouraging everyone to pick up a paddle and play, with public games and events.

days.name: World Tapas Day
days.about: A day started in Spain to promote tapas, when bars and restaurants feature small plates and people go out to share them.

days.name: World Tapir Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness of the four tapir species, which are all threatened, and for supporting their conservation.

days.name: World TB-303 Appreciation Day
days.about: A day honoring Roland's TB-303 bass synthesizer, whose squelchy sound shaped acid house; fans play and share acid tracks.

days.name: World Teachers Day
days.about: A UNESCO day recognizing teachers and their working conditions, often marked by students and schools thanking their teachers.

days.name: World Telecommunications Day
days.about: An ITU day marking the founding of the International Telegraph Union, used to highlight how telecom and the internet can reach more people.

days.name: World Television Day
days.about: A UN day recognizing television's role in communication and in informing the public.

days.name: World Theater Day
days.about: A day from the International Theatre Institute to support theater, with a message from a theater figure read out and performances and events held worldwide.

days.name: World Thinking Day
days.about: A Girl Guides and Girl Scouts day, on the shared birthday of founders Robert and Olave Baden-Powell, for thinking about fellow Guides around the world and raising money for the movement.

days.name: World Toilet Day
days.about: A UN day drawing attention to the billions of people without safe toilets and to the need for better sanitation.

days.name: World UFO Day
days.about: A day for UFO enthusiasts to watch the skies for unidentified objects and talk about sightings and the evidence for them.

days.name: World Vegan Day
days.about: A day marking the founding of the Vegan Society, used to promote veganism with events, food samples and talks.

days.name: World Vegetarian Day
days.about: A day started by the North American Vegetarian Society to promote vegetarian eating and kick off a month of awareness about it.

days.name: World Water Day
days.about: A UN day focused on access to clean fresh water and how water resources are managed.

days.name: World Wetlands Day
days.about: A day marking the signing of the Ramsar Convention on wetlands, used to raise awareness of why wetlands matter and how fast they're being lost.

days.name: World Whale Day
days.about: A day started in Maui, Hawaii, with a festival and parade, to appreciate humpback whales and promote whale protection.

days.name: World Whisky Day
days.about: A day started by a Scottish student to encourage people to try whisky and share a dram, with tastings at bars and distilleries.

days.name: World Wide Web Day
days.about: A day for appreciating the web and how it changed access to information, sometimes noting Tim Berners-Lee's creation of it.

days.name: World Wildlife Conservation Day
days.about: A day for raising awareness about protecting wildlife and fighting wildlife trafficking.

days.name: World Wildlife Day
days.about: A UN day marking the signing of CITES, the treaty on trade in endangered species, used to highlight wild animals and plants and the threats they face.

days.name: World Wish Day
days.about: A day from Make-A-Wish marking the anniversary of its first wish, used to raise money and volunteers to grant wishes for seriously ill children.

days.name: World Yoga Day
days.about: Also called the International Day of Yoga, it promotes yoga's health benefits, with large group yoga sessions held in public places.

days.name: Worldwide Candle Lighting Day
days.about: A day from The Compassionate Friends when families light candles at 7 p.m. local time to remember children who have died, creating a wave of light around the world.

days.name: Worldwide Knit in Public Day
days.about: A day when knitters gather to knit together in parks, cafes and other public places, to enjoy the company and show off the craft.

days.name: Wright Brothers Day
days.about: A US day marking the Wright brothers' first powered airplane flight at Kitty Hawk, proclaimed each year by the president.

days.name: X-Ray Day
days.about: A day marking Wilhelm Röntgen's discovery of X-rays, used to recognize radiology and the people who work in it.

days.name: Yarn Bombing Day
days.about: A day when people cover public objects like trees, poles and benches with knitted or crocheted yarn as a kind of friendly street art.

days.name: Yellow Pig Day
days.about: A playful math holiday celebrating the number 17 and a mythical yellow pig, started by mathematicians Michael Spivak and David Kelly and marked at math camps with songs and cake.

days.name: Yo-Yo Day
days.about: A day for playing with yo-yos, held on the birthday of Donald F. Duncan, who popularized the toy in the US.

days.name: Yorkshire Day
days.about: A day of pride in the English county of Yorkshire, when people fly the white rose flag, read a declaration of the county's integrity and enjoy local food.

days.name: Yorkshire Pudding Day
days.about: A day for making and eating Yorkshire puddings, the batter puddings traditionally served with a roast dinner.

days.name: You’re Welcome Giving Day
days.about: The day after Thanksgiving. It's a play on the holiday's name: since Thanksgiving is about saying thank you, this day is for saying "you're welcome" back to the people who thanked you.

days.name: Z Day
days.about: A day giving first place to people and things whose names start with Z, since they usually come last in alphabetical order.

days.name: Za’atar Day
days.about: A day for za'atar, the Middle Eastern blend of dried wild thyme, sumac, sesame seeds and salt. People cook with it and post their favorite za'atar dishes online with the #ZaatarDay tag.

days.name: Zero Tasking Day
days.about: The day after daylight saving time ends, for spending the extra hour you gained doing nothing at all instead of more chores.

days.name: Zip Code Day
days.about: A day marking the introduction of the US Postal Service's ZIP code system in 1963.

days.name: Zipper Day
days.about: A day honoring the zipper, tied to Gideon Sundback's patent for the modern zipper.

days.name: Zoo Lovers Day
days.about: A day for visiting your local zoo and learning how zoos work to protect endangered species.

days.name: Zucchini Bread Day
days.about: A day for baking and eating zucchini bread, a sweet quick bread made with grated zucchini.
